articles.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow to discuss Ukraine war with Putin
articles.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Ukraine talks with Vladimir Putin
articles.summary: American negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Wednesday to discuss European security and the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. The visit followed two days of talks in Abu Dhabi and preceded a planned trip to Dublin to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces reported renewed connectivity issues with SpaceX service Starshield.
articles.description: Later on Thursday, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Dublin to meet Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

articles.headline: Six people killed in Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza
articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
articles.summary: An official from the Hamas-run civil defence agency reported that an Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killing at least six people and wounding twenty others. The strike occurred early on Thursday and caused extensive damage to the facility, while the Israeli military provided no immediate response.
articles.description: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.

articles.headline: Mississippi elects first Black Senator since 1874
articles.title: Mississippi elects first Black Senator since 1874
articles.description: Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi’s Senate race, becoming the state’s first Black senator since 1874.

articles.headline: Ukraine faces severe power outages as Russian strikes devastate energy grid
articles.title: 'No light, no water, no heat': Ukrainians struggle with blackouts as Russia hits power grid
articles.summary: Millions of Ukrainians endure rolling blackouts lasting up to twenty hours daily following intensified Russian missile attacks on national energy infrastructure. DTEK chief executive Maxim Timchenko stated that the scale of destruction has left generating facilities severely degraded, while repair teams face persistent air raids that will delay full restoration until at least next summer.
articles.description: For parents in parts of Ukraine, trying to lead a normal family life with just a few hours of power each day is taking its toll.

articles.headline: Israel steps up military readiness for possible strikes against Iran
articles.title: Iran warns of expanded retaliation as Israel reportedly readies to attack
articles.summary: Israel ordered its military to step up preparations for potential strikes on Iran after Tehran warned it would expand the regional conflict if attacked. Israeli media reported the security cabinet directives on Wednesday evening. Meanwhile, oil prices rose about one percent following Iran's rejection of a United States proposal regarding its uranium stockpile.
articles.description: Israeli security cabinet orders military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli media reports.

articles.headline: Nvidia board reportedly prepares to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang
articles.title: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia board members are reportedly planning to remove Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following allegations regarding a second extramarital affair with executive Kimberly Powell. The decision comes shortly after Huang admitted to another relationship with an alleged spy, causing company shares to drop over seven percent in after-hours trading as legal firms investigate the matter.
articles.description: Nvidia's board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a report from The New York Times about a second alleged extramarital affair, just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reports. The second alleged affair was with an executive who […]

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Russia, Ukraine hold second day of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Delegations from Moscow and Kyiv held a second day of United States-brokered negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 11, 2026, focusing on humanitarian issues and security guarantees. U.S. and Ukrainian officials reported constructive discussions, though no breakthrough occurred. Meanwhile, ongoing frontline fighting and overnight missile strikes caused civilian injuries and a fire at a Russian oil export port.
articles.description: ‘We are starting the second day of negotiations,’ Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, who leads Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, says on social media

articles.headline: New York building collapse leaves two dead and seventeen injured
articles.title: New York building collapse kills at least two, officials say
articles.summary: At least two individuals died and over seventeen sustained injuries after a three-storey structure in Brooklyn collapsed into an open construction site on Wednesday. Over two hundred and fifty first responders deployed to the Flatbush Avenue location for rescue operations. Authorities stated the cause remains undetermined while emergency crews continued searching through rubble for survivors trapped beneath the debris.
articles.description: A dangerous search for survivors continues after a three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday afternoon.

articles.headline: Indonesian vice president steps down following educational credential disputes
articles.title: Indonesia's Vice President resigns as eligibility and academic credentials are questioned
articles.summary: Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned as Indonesia's vice president on November 12, 2026, following Supreme Court and Constitutional Court rulings regarding his overseas education documents. The thirty-nine-year-old submitted his resignation to the People's Consultative Assembly in Jakarta after one hundred twenty lawmakers filed a petition initiating parliamentary procedures that could have led to his impeachment.
articles.description: The Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that the documents submitted by Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the 39-year-old son of former President Joko Widodo, regarding his overseas education didn't meet election requirements

articles.headline: Democrat Scott Colom secures historic Senate victory in Mississippi
articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi elects first black senator in 150 years
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith to win a United States Senate seat in Mississippi. This outcome makes him the state's first Black senator in over 140 years and expands the Democratic majority to fifty-five seats. Colom capitalized on public frustrations regarding economic issues and administration tariffs during a closely watched midterm contest.
articles.description: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.

articles.headline: US military bases become strategic liabilities following Middle East conflict
articles.title: From the UK to the Gulf, are US overseas bases becoming liabilities?
articles.summary: Recent military engagements in the Middle East have transformed critical overseas US installations into potential liabilities for Washington and its allies. Facilities in the United Kingdom and Gulf nations suffered damage during the war, prompting the relocation of assets and raising concerns among host governments regarding increased security risks from regional adversaries.
articles.description: For decades, these bases allowed the US to wage faraway wars. Now, Iran has changed that calculation.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping calls for complete reunification of Taiwan during commemorative speech
articles.title: Xi says Taiwan 'reunification' must happen as history cannot be stopped
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping stated on November 12, 2026, that the reunification of Taiwan is an unwavering historical mission that must be realized. Speaking in Beijing during an event honoring Sun Yat-sen, Xi emphasized peaceful development under the one-China principle while maintaining that the tide of history cannot be stopped despite strong Taiwanese opposition.
articles.description: China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei's strong rejection of that claim, and has repeatedly offered a "one country, two systems" model of autonomy

articles.headline: US officials report slight flexibility in Russia and Ukraine peace talks
articles.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
articles.summary: Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington are meeting in Abu Dhabi for trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. According to United States officials, both warring sides are showing private flexibility regarding the postwar control of Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. However, deep disagreements remain over territorial demands and the future security architecture of Europe.
articles.description: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.

articles.headline: Chinese AI firms rush to secure foreign Nvidia chip capacity
articles.title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of U.S. curbs
articles.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are seeking to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at overseas data centres amid fears that a scandal involving the chipmaker's chief executive Jensen Huang could prompt Washington to tighten restrictions. Sources indicated that buyers are stockpiling restricted processors over concerns that U.S. authorities might crack down further on cross-border technology smuggling.
articles.description: A major Chinese ‌cloud provider has discussed internally whether to lock in overseas Nvidia chip capacity, while some companies have ‌contacted ⁠data-centre operators about reserving it, per sources

articles.headline: NIA probes Pakistani gangster over online radicalisation of Indian youths
articles.title: NIA to probe online radicalisation of Indian youths by Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency registered a case on November 12, 2026, targeting Pakistan-based gangster Shahzad Bhatti and Inter-Services Intelligence agents for allegedly radicalising Indian youths through social media. Officials stated the suspects lured individuals with financial incentives to conduct disruptive acts, building upon an initial investigation launched by the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad earlier in April.
articles.description: During the investigation, it emerged that Pakistani gangster Bhatti, Jatt and radical Pakistani YouTubers, allegedly acting on instructions from the ISI, were attempting to radicalise Indian youths and entice them with financial incentives

articles.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow for high-level peace talks with Putin
articles.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Russia-Ukraine talks with Putin
articles.summary: United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to Moscow on Thursday for discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The visit followed trilateral peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi that concluded on Wednesday without a breakthrough on the nearly five-year war, though participants discussed post-war security guarantees and upcoming prisoner exchanges.
articles.description: The meeting with Kushner and Witkoff comes after two days of trilateral talks in the UAE yielded no breakthrough.

articles.headline: Pakistani influencer linked to terror investigations across fourteen Indian states
articles.title: The digital recruiter | Shahzad Bhatti
articles.summary: Over the past two years, Pakistani social-media influencer Shahzad Bhatti has been implicated in multiple Indian anti-terror investigations spanning 14 states. Authorities reported that young men allegedly acting on his instructions were arrested under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act for tasks including hanging promotional posters, installing live-streamed CCTVs, and making extortion calls.
articles.description: The Pakistani social media influencer’s campaign to establish fear and clout in India has spread to 14 States, leading the Home Ministry to designate his network as a terror group

articles.headline: Iran Revolutionary Guards report tanker explosions in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran’s Guards say ‘accident’ left two tankers on fire in Hormuz
articles.summary: According to the Iranian Revolutionary Guards, two oil supertankers carrying over four million barrels caught fire following an accident on an unauthorized Strait of Hormuz route. Tehran blamed aggressive American military policies for the incident on November 12, 2026. The route was restricted amid ongoing West Asian conflict, while U.S. forces maintained a naval blockade and denied active mine threats.
articles.description: Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits

articles.headline: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submits resignation letter
articles.title: Indonesia's vice-president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto after the Supreme Court invalidated a high-school document used in his 2024 election campaign. The ruling sparked parliamentary impeachment initiatives and highlighted widening fractures within the ruling political alliance established by former leader Joko Widodo.
articles.description: The news comes at a turbulent time for President Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.

articles.headline: Donald Trump weighs potential military action against Iran following UN remarks
articles.title: Is Trump’s ‘no-war, no-peace’ plan on Iran sustainable?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump considered potential military strategies regarding Iran, including a possible short and intense war targeting infrastructure after the November 3 midterm elections. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost his governing majority in October 27 elections, advocated for renewed air strikes alongside Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper.
articles.description: Despite the U.S. President’s decision to hold off on further strikes, he remains neck-deep in the war he launched alongside Israel’s Netanyahu on February 28 this year

articles.headline: India exempts rules to purchase Israeli phone-hacking and surveillance technology
articles.title: India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
articles.summary: India exempted an Israeli firm from procurement regulations, allowing government agencies to purchase phone-extraction and surveillance technology. Documents reviewed by digital-rights groups revealed Home Minister Amit Shah approved waivers for forensic equipment, enabling security forces to access cloud data and bypass security locks despite privacy concerns raised by legal experts.
articles.description: India's expansive surveillance capabilities extend beyond cloning phones to accessing cloud-based data of tech giants.

articles.headline: Gunmen kill ten police officers and eighteen fighters in Pakistan
articles.title: Ten police officers, 18 fighters killed in northwest Pakistan attack
articles.summary: Ten police officers and 18 fighters died during violence in northwestern Pakistan after armed men attacked officers returning from an illegal gold mining operation in the Kohat district. The Pakistani Taliban claimed responsibility for the assault, which also left 12 police personnel wounded as security forces continue battling intensifying regional unrest.
articles.description: Officers were returning from a mine in Kohat district when fighters opened fire on them, authorities say.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping says Taiwan ‘reunification’ with China must happen
articles.title: Xi Jinping says Taiwan ‘reunification’ with China must happen
articles.description: Xi Jinping, President of China, has called for the peaceful ‘reunification’ of Taiwan with China.

articles.headline: Iran open to deal if US ‘refrains from excessive demands’, says Ghalibaf
articles.title: Iran open to deal if US ‘refrains from excessive demands’, says Ghalibaf
articles.description: Iran’s chief negotiator says Iran is open to a deal if the US refrains from creating distrust and excessive demands.

articles.headline: G7 Foreign Ministers warn China's actions east of Taiwan threaten stability
articles.title: G7 Foreign Ministers say China's actions east of Taiwan threaten stability
articles.summary: Group of Seven Foreign Ministers issued a joint declaration in Paris late Wednesday stating that China's assertive maritime activities east of Taiwan threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation. Taiwan views the increased coast guard patrols as preparation for a potential blockade, while China claims sovereignty over the democratically governed island.
articles.description: The G7 statement said the Ministers ⁠stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait

articles.headline: Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital building in Khan Younis kills five
articles.title: Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital kills six, health authorities say
articles.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis on Thursday, killing at least five people including a surgeon named Rezik Abushira and wounding twenty others, according to the civil defence service. The strike caused extensive damage to the facility. This event occurs amid ongoing conflict and mounting casualties across the Gaza Strip since the October 2023 offensive began.
articles.description: Israeli forces have previously targeted Nasser Hospital; in 2025, the military killed five journalists — including AP contributor Mariam Dagga — when it struck a gathering point for local reporters at the complex

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu urges national unity government during contentious Israeli parliament session
articles.title: Netanyahu’s legacy: Personality politics reshapes Israeli democracy
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a national unity government during the swearing-in of the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, on Tuesday. The session featured intense heckling and walkouts as political rivals opposed his leadership. Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming a new administration, cancelled coalition talks and declared Netanyahu unfit for office amid ongoing corruption trials and political polarization.
articles.description: Netanyahu's fight for political survival turns the parliament's opening into a scene of insults and acrimony.

articles.headline: Indonesian vice president resigns amid credential dispute and political pressure
articles.title: Indonesia vice president resigns amid dispute over eligibility
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on Thursday after court rulings disputed his educational credentials, according to parliamentary officials. The thirty-nine-year-old official stepped down during a period of widespread public protests regarding economic hardship and corruption, leaving the People's Consultative Assembly sixty days to elect a presidential nominee as his replacement.
articles.description: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former President Joko Widodo, resigns as court questions his overseas education.

articles.headline: Nvidia board prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang following affair revelations
articles.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: U.S. media
articles.summary: The board of directors at chip manufacturer Nvidia is preparing to remove co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. This development follows recent disclosures that the sixty-three-year-old executive had an extramarital affair with an individual accused by United States intelligence of being a Chinese spy, alongside a second relationship with a subordinate at the technology company.
articles.description: The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with Nvidia's vice-president of health care, Kimberly Powell

articles.headline: Climate finance disputes test negotiators at United Nations summit in Antalya
articles.title: Why climate finance remains a recurring flashpoint at UN summits
articles.summary: Negotiators gathered in Antalya for the United Nations climate summit are clashing over climate finance commitments. Developing nations argue that current funding falls significantly short of estimated requirements and consists largely of repayable loans rather than essential grants. India and other Global South countries emphasize that financial support must remain accessible, predictable, and adequate to address severe warming impacts.
articles.description: As climate negotiators meet in Türkiye, the familiar battle over climate finance exposes a deeper divide. While wealthy nations count the money they mobilise, developing countries question how much actually reaches them

articles.headline: Yemen conflict intensifies as Houthis deny targeting Mecca
articles.title: Fighting intensifies in Yemen as Houthis deny targeting Mecca
articles.summary: Yemeni Houthis rejected Saudi allegations regarding a drone strike on Mecca, claiming instead that strikes targeted Yanbu and Riyadh. Meanwhile, fighting escalated inside Yemen between government forces and Houthi fighters, with total casualties reaching 11,755 according to the World Health Organization. Over 320,000 people have been displaced since August as intensified clashes continue to impact health facilities and emergency services.
articles.description: World Health Organization says more than 320,000 people have been displaced in Yemen fighting since August 1.

articles.headline: Iran’s chief negotiator tells Al Jazeera ‘ball in US court’
articles.title: Iran’s chief negotiator tells Al Jazeera ‘ball in US court’
articles.description: Iran’s chief negotiator says it’s up to the US to answer Iran’s position in the latest round of peace talks.

articles.headline: Protesters clash with police across Spain following housing cost rallies
articles.title: Protesters clash with police in Spain after huge housing cost rallies
articles.summary: Police deployed tear gas and rubber bullet launchers after sporadic clashes erupted in Madrid and Barcelona on Wednesday following nationwide protests over housing affordability and purchasing power. Hundreds of thousands participated in Spain's first nationwide twenty-four-hour strike since 2012, occurring weeks before an early general election set for November 29.
articles.description: The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez

articles.headline: Amnesty International criticises UN and South Sudan over village massacre
articles.title: Amnesty says UN, South Sudan officials failed to prevent village massacre
articles.summary: Amnesty International stated that United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to act on warnings before armed men attacked an Abiemnom village and killed more than 200 people. Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty's director for East and Southern Africa, said Thursday that stronger preventive action could have saved lives ahead of the upcoming December 22 elections.
articles.description: Peacekeepers knew of likely raid on Abiemnom, where more than 200 people were killed, according to rights group report.

articles.headline: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64bn in New York stock market listing
articles.title: Anthropic heads for lower than expected $1.3 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic is planning to raise up to $64 billion through an initial public offering on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making firm priced shares between $70 and $78 each, yielding a valuation below prior predictions amid market volatility surrounding artificial intelligence investments. According to analyst Fiona Cincotta from City Index, the move demonstrates continued industry optimism despite wider financial concerns.
articles.description: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78.

articles.headline: First information report registered against Mamata Banerjee over remarks
articles.title: FIR against former CM Mamata Banerjee over alleged communal remarks in Bengal
articles.summary: A police case was filed against former West Bengal Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee concerning alleged communal statements made during a campaign. According to a senior police official, the initial zero FIR was registered on June 7, 2026, following a complaint by Tushar Kanti Das, and was later transferred to the Hare Street police station.
articles.description: During a protest against the SIR, the TMC chief allegedly told a minority community that their safety depended on her, advising them not to pay heed to the BJP’s ‘misleading’ words

articles.headline: Indonesian VP resigns over education qualification row
articles.title: Indonesian VP resigns over education qualification row
articles.description: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned amid a dispute over his educational qualifications.

articles.headline: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang faces scrutiny amid spy allegations against associate
articles.title: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
articles.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang faces escalating scrutiny after allegations that a Chinese businesswoman he associated with engaged in espionage. U.S. authorities have launched investigations into the cloud computing firm Megaspeed, while President Donald Trump stated he spoke with Huang about the controversy. The developments arrive as Nvidia remains central to artificial intelligence infrastructure and U.S. economic strategies, prompting bipartisan calls for congressional probes.
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confronts a widening political and legal storm in Washington over an alleged extramarital affair and claims a former Megaspeed executive spied for China, as federal investigators probe export controls and possible national-security breaches tied to Nvidia’s chips in the high-stakes U.S.-China AI race

articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections determining presidential power
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
articles.summary: Americans went to the polls on November 3, 2026, in midterm elections that will determine how much power United States President Donald Trump retains for the remainder of his term. Voters decided all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats, and 36 state governorships. Over 210 million registered citizens were eligible to cast ballots across the country as voting concluded.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states went for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote

articles.headline: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race
articles.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom as state's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction
articles.summary: Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely contested United States Senate race. The prolonged ballot count concluded with the local prosecutor winning the election, making him the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. This historic outcome adds to a decisive midterm rebuke against the political party of President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Former President Bill Clinton and former Vice-President Kamala Harris campaigned on Scott Colom's behalf in the campaign's closing weeks

articles.headline: Israel strikes intensive care at Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
articles.title: Israel strikes intensive care at Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
articles.description: Gaza's Civil Defence says an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital has killed at least six people.

articles.headline: Nvidia board discusses chief executive Jensen Huang following controversy
articles.title: Nvidia shares plunge amid reports board to discuss CEO Huang’s future
articles.summary: Nvidia shares dropped more than eight percent during after-hours trading on Wednesday as media outlets reported that the board of directors scheduled a meeting to evaluate the future of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. According to the New York Times, Financial Times, and Wall Street Journal, the discussions follow controversy surrounding an alleged extramarital relationship with an employee and a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. The company did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
articles.description: Chip giant's stock price falls more than 8 percent amid speculation over co-founder's position.

articles.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi US Senate race
articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins closely watched US Senate race in Mississippi
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom won the United States Senate contest in Mississippi by defeating Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith after a week of counting mail-in ballots. Colom will become the first Black senator from the state in more than 140 years. The victory follows broader midterm successes for Democrats who flipped multiple seats previously held by Republicans.
articles.description: The historic victory flips an eighth US Senate seat for Democrats after last week's pivotal midterm election.

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill nine in Gaza amid severe flooding
articles.title: Israeli strikes hit medical complex as nine killed across Gaza
articles.summary: Israeli military attacks resulted in at least nine deaths across the Gaza Strip while the United Nations issued urgent appeals for waterproof shelter materials. Heavy rainfall recently submerged tens of thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians. International officials emphasized that humanitarian aid deliveries continue to face severe restrictions and permit delays from Israeli authorities.
articles.description: Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis attacked as UN appeals for urgent aid to deal with heavy rains in the enclave.

articles.headline: Trump defends war against Iran during Veterans Day address
articles.title: Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump defended the ongoing military conflict against Iran on Wednesday at a Veterans Day commemoration held at Arlington National Cemetery near Washington. Speaking before troops and administration officials, the eighty-year-old leader claimed Tehran initiated the hostilities and praised Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, whose presence sparked controversy after a military sentinel reprimanded visitors for laughing at a sacred site.
articles.description: Mr. Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which “has been waging war on America since 1979”

articles.headline: Spain faces widespread general strike over housing and living costs
articles.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
articles.summary: Transport and public services across Spain experienced serious disruption on Wednesday during the country's first general strike in fourteen years, called by major unions over affordable housing and the high cost of living. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez encouraged workers to participate, while opposition leaders criticized the move as political. Electricity usage fell by 7.5 percent.
articles.description: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

articles.headline: Russia, Ukraine and U.S. begin peace talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: U.S.-mediated talks on ending war between Russia, Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Delegations from Russia, Ukraine and the United States commenced two days of discussions focusing on security guarantees in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026. Moscow and Kyiv remain deeply divided over territorial demands, military limitations and ceasefires. Russian President Vladimir Putin insists on retaining annexed regions and curbing Ukrainian military expansion, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy demands immediate hostilities cessation and rejects territorial surrenders.
articles.description: The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees

articles.headline: Donald Trump says Iran war is militarily over
articles.title: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump declared during a White House briefing that the conflict with Iran is militarily finished, citing positive momentum in negotiations following talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani. Trump stated that further military strikes remain unlikely while a naval blockade maintains regional security, despite domestic political fallout and Republican midterm election pressures.
articles.description: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation change.

articles.headline: Iran official says Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war status
articles.title: Hormuz Strait will ‘never return’ to pre-war status, Iran’s Ghalibaf says
articles.summary: Iran parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated in an interview published on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz will not revert to its pre-war condition. He noted that Tehran reached an understanding with Oman to oversee the waterway and outlined seven conditions for peace talks with the United States, adding that Iran awaits an official response delivered via a Qatari mediator.
articles.description: Iran's parliament speaker and top negotiator says Tehran is waiting for an official US response to its seven conditions.

articles.headline: Scenes show aftermath of horrific Israeli strike on Gaza tents
articles.title: Scenes show aftermath of horrific Israeli strike on Gaza tents
articles.description: Palestinian families have returned to the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City after an Israeli strike killed three people.

articles.headline: United Nations says over one million people face severe food shortages in Lebanon
articles.title: More than one million people in Lebanon face acute food shortages, UN says
articles.summary: More than one million individuals in Lebanon confront critical food shortages driven by economic collapse and consecutive conflicts, according to United Nations agencies and the Ministry of Agriculture. Officials warned that food scarcity will likely worsen as household budgets remain strained. The ongoing crisis compounds years of financial turmoil and the aftermath of devastating warfare since October 2023.
articles.description: UN warns hunger crisis affecting almost quarter of Lebanon's population could escalate without 'urgent action'.

articles.headline: Navi Mumbai named India's cleanest city in central government rankings
articles.title: Navi Mumbai recognised as India’s cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
articles.summary: Navi Mumbai secured the top position as India's cleanest city during a central government awards ceremony, followed by Surat and Vijayawada. President Droupadi Murmu presented the accolades at the event. Ujjain led the three lakh to ten lakh population bracket, while Greater Visakhapatnam topped the ten lakh-plus category. Over 4,751 cities participated in the assessment conducted under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban initiative.
articles.description: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year

articles.headline: Ireland fears subsea cables face growing threat from malign actors
articles.title: ‘Malign actors’: Ireland fears Russia could threaten undersea cables
articles.summary: Ireland faces heightened vulnerability regarding transatlantic subsea cables passing through its waters, which connect North America with Europe and support major technology multinationals. According to the Irish government, increased presence of Russian vessels and the shadow fleet near critical infrastructure has raised sabotage concerns. Former officials and politicians emphasize the need for stronger national defense capabilities and international cooperation to protect vital digital networks.
articles.description: Home to many US tech multinationals, Ireland raises alarm over Russia's so-called shadow fleet.

articles.headline: Russian ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev dies at 66
articles.title: Russia’s ambassador to US, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
articles.summary: Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States, died unexpectedly at the age of sixty-six, according to an announcement by the Russian Foreign Ministry. Moscow stated that he passed away suddenly on Wednesday, roughly eighteen months after taking up the Washington posting. Darchiev previously served as ambassador to Canada and headed the ministry's North America department during a career spanning several decades in international diplomacy.
articles.description: Moscow announces the veteran diplomat's sudden passing without further details.

articles.headline: Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi conclude without major breakthrough
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
articles.summary: Trilateral negotiations between Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi ended without a breakthrough regarding the five-year war. While officials noted some momentum, deep distrust remains over territorial disputes in Donetsk and European security architecture. US negotiators plan further meetings in Moscow and Dublin to discuss a potential framework for future regional peace.
articles.description: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.

articles.headline: Spain faces nationwide protests over soaring housing costs
articles.title: Spain faces nationwide protests over soaring housing costs
articles.description: Spain faces nationwide protests over soaring housing costs

articles.headline: Militants ambush police vehicles in northwestern Pakistan, killing 10 officers
articles.title: Militants ambush police vehicles in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 10 officers
articles.summary: Ten police officers were killed in a militant ambush on Wednesday in Kohat, a district within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in northwestern Pakistan. Local police official Faisal Khan confirmed two senior officers were among the fatalities during the ongoing gunbattle. The Pakistani Taliban subsequently claimed responsibility for the assault. The region has experienced a surge in violence attributed to the group, which operates near the Afghan border and shares close ties with the Afghan Taliban.
articles.description: Police say militants have ambushed vehicles carrying police officers in northwestern Pakistan, triggering a gunbattle that killed at least 10 officers

articles.headline: Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 confirmed cases
articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded over 11,000 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,387 deaths during its 17th outbreak, according to the National Institute of Public Health. Armed conflict continues to severely hamper the medical response across affected regions. Health authorities reported that youths recently set fire to an Ebola treatment centre in Ituri province. The ongoing instability and militia clashes have repeatedly disrupted health operations and suspended emergency containment efforts throughout northeastern areas.
articles.description: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

articles.headline: Leaders at COP31 urge climate action despite global conflicts
articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.summary: The presidents of Brazil and Turkey warned at the COP31 climate conference that global conflicts and trade disputes must not derail international efforts to combat global warming. Speaking on November 11, 2026, leaders emphasized the urgent need for clean energy adoption as delegates negotiate new agreements to address escalating extreme weather events and rising global temperatures.
articles.description: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

articles.headline: United States Senate Republicans re-elect John Thune as party leader
articles.title: John Thune re-elected as US Senate Republican leader after midterm losses
articles.summary: United States Senate Republicans re-elected South Dakota lawmaker John Thune to lead their conference during a closed-door meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday. Thune ran unopposed despite recent midterm losses that saw the party lose at least seven Senate seats. He stated that the electoral backlash stemmed largely from the high cost of living for American people. Thune will now prepare to work alongside a Democratic-controlled Congress and a White House aiming to advance its controversial policies.
articles.description: The Republican ran unopposed, despite some GOP lawmaker demands to evaluate the party's stinging midterm losses to Democ

articles.headline: US charges three operatives over Iran-backed terror plots in Europe and America
articles.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
articles.summary: The United States Department of Justice unsealed an indictment charging three operatives with orchestrating nearly twenty attacks across Europe and America on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kataib Hezbollah. Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel stated the accused planned incidents including a September plot near the United Kingdom base RAF Fairford. Iran strongly rejected the allegations as malicious speculations.
articles.description: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.

articles.headline: Russia-Ukraine talks in UAE secure major prisoner exchange deal
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks in UAE secure major prisoner exchange deal
articles.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a major prisoner exchange following two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi

articles.headline: India and France hold dialogues on economic security and space
articles.title: India, France hold dialogues on economic security, space, technology
articles.summary: India and France convened meetings in Paris from November 9 to 10, 2026, focusing on critical technologies, supply chain security, and space cooperation. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and French official Martin Briens led the talks, which included preparations for an upcoming free trade agreement expected when Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits Brussels on December 16, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.
articles.description: The two sides discuss supply chain vulnerabilities, critical technologies, cybersecurity and safeguarding strategic supplies, as part of the India-France Economic Security and Critical Technologies Dialogue

articles.headline: Israeli air strike in Gaza kills Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Kamal Abdel-Malek
articles.title: Israeli army kills Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Kamal Abdel-Malek in Gaza
articles.summary: Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Kamal Abdel-Malek was killed in an Israeli air strike on Gaza City's Sabra neighbourhood, the Palestinian Football Association confirmed. The 20-year-old goalkeeper served as captain of Gaza Sports Club and was the 1,017th sports figure killed in the conflict. His death occurred days after he competed in the Thousand Martyrs Cup. Palestinian health officials report that at least 74,645 people have died across the territory since October 7, 2023.
articles.description: Abdel-Malek, the captain and goalkeeper of Gaza Sports Club, recently played in the Thousand Martyrs Cup final.

articles.headline: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after Iran-linked threats
articles.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was moved to a military base following security concerns driven by Iran-linked threats. US media reports indicated the relocation occurred after an online photo revealed his Washington residence. US intelligence warns that efforts by Iran to target current and former American officials have escalated significantly during ongoing geopolitical tensions.
articles.description: Bessent is now one of several Trump administration officials to live on military bases due to safety concerns.

articles.headline: J&K: terrorists open fire on CRPF personnel in Kulgam; three injured | Above the Fold | Nov 11, 2026
articles.title: J&K: terrorists open fire on CRPF personnel in Kulgam; three injured | Above the Fold | Nov 11, 2026
articles.description: Several CRPF personnel were injured after terrorists opened fire in Kulgam district of south Kashmir on Wednesday afternoon. What do we know about the attack?

articles.headline: Iran security chief says enriched nuclear material will remain domestic
articles.title: ‘Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country’
articles.summary: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated in televised remarks that the Islamic Republic will keep all enriched nuclear material inside the country for naval propulsion purposes. Speaking after US officials downplayed the need for military action, Rezaei warned of retaliation against distant American bases if new strikes occur, while the International Atomic Energy Agency monitors Tehran's existing uranium stockpiles.
articles.description: Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington

articles.headline: Iran prepares for potential zero oil revenue amid persistent US blockade
articles.title: Can Tehran survive a ‘zero oil’ budget, if US blockade on Iran persists?
articles.summary: Tehran is bracing for a severe economic crisis as US sanctions and a naval blockade threaten to eliminate oil income. President Masoud Pezeshkian’s administration is reviewing public spending and energy subsidies to manage potential deficits. While officials deny prospects of total collapse, economists warn that replacing oil revenue remains difficult under current international financial restrictions.
articles.description: The government is defiant and planning for the worst, but a US siege is expected to make most Iranians poorer.

articles.headline: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated following alleged Iranian threats
articles.title: Bessent’s relocation: From US to EU, is Iran bringing war to Western soil?
articles.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved to a military base after reports of threats linked to Iran. The relocation follows an investigation into his residence's location. Meanwhile, US forces have diverted aircraft from UK bases amid security concerns. Tehran has denied involvement in plots against officials, despite ongoing tensions over economic sanctions.
articles.description: A deliberate expansion of Iran’s campaign of retaliation beyond the Middle East could be taking place, said an expert.

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu denies Israel is blocking winter aid to Gaza
articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected claims that Israel is delaying winter supplies to Gaza, blaming Hamas for the humanitarian crisis instead. This follows reports from the U.S.-created Board of Peace that aid delays worsened conditions during severe flooding. International figures, including British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, have called for an end to aid restrictions.
articles.description: Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes

articles.headline: Niraj Kumar secures quota place for 2028 Olympics with bronze medal
articles.title: Rifle shooter Niraj Kumar secures LA Olympics quota with bronze in men's 50m 3-position
articles.summary: Indian shooter Niraj Kumar won the bronze medal in the men's fifty-metre rifle three-positions event at the International Shooting Sport Federation World Championships in Doha on Wednesday, securing a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Individual Neutral Athlete Dmitrii Pimenov claimed the gold medal with a world junior record score.
articles.description: It was India’s second Olympic quota at the championships, following Jaypal Malviya’s silver in the men’s 10m air pistol event a few days ago

articles.headline: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 to predict genetic variant effects
articles.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
articles.summary: Google DeepMind has launched AlphaGenome 2, an artificial intelligence model capable of predicting how DNA mutations influence specific cell types and states. Trained on over 100 million cell profiles, the tool identifies twice as many gene-altering variants as its predecessor. It is now available for non-commercial research to assist scientists in developing targeted medical treatments.
articles.description: Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease - and point the way to new treatments. AlphaGenome 2 is the successor […]

articles.headline: Global leaders to gather for Bharat Summit in Hyderabad
articles.title: Leaders from nearly 70 countries to attend Bharat Summit
articles.summary: The Bharat Summit 2026 will take place in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14, hosting political leaders, diplomats, and academics from nearly 70 countries. The event aims to showcase regional development initiatives. It concludes with addresses from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, following a tour of local government landmarks.

articles.headline: Karnataka government challenges court ruling on reservation quota increase
articles.title: Quota row: Karnataka files SLP in Supreme Court over reservation breaching 50% mark
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has filed a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court to contest a High Court decision that struck down increased reservation quotas for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The High Court had ruled the 56% total reservation cap unconstitutional, exceeding the 50% limit established by the Supreme Court in 1992.
articles.description: The Karnataka High Court, stating that the enhancement was ‘constitutionally impermissible’, had quashed the higher reservation to SCs and STs that took it to 56 %, breaching the cap of 50% imposed by the Supreme Court in 1992

articles.headline: US administration debates strategy regarding ongoing conflict with Iran
articles.title: Rubio backs blockade, Vance wants deal: Is Trump’s team split on Iran war?
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that current economic pressure on Iran makes further military action unnecessary, aligning with President Donald Trump's recent comments. While some officials favor continued blockades, Vice President JD Vance reportedly supports pursuing a diplomatic deal. The administration faces pressure to de-escalate following significant Republican losses in the recent midterm elections.
articles.description: Torn between military action and diplomacy, US appears to settle for drawn-out economic pressure campaign, blockade.

articles.headline: Floods in Gaza kill four people after heavy rain submerges camps
articles.title: ‘Our neighbours are gone’: Gaza survivors recount horrors of deadly floods
articles.summary: Catastrophic flooding caused by heavy rain submerged displacement camps and destroyed cities in Gaza on Sunday, killing four people after a sandbank collapsed at the Ard al-Ribat camp in Deir el-Balah. According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, more than 26,000 households reported shelter damage, compounding severe infrastructure destruction.
articles.description: A deadly sandbank collapse buried families alive in Deir el-Balah, as survivors describe desperate rescue attempts.

articles.headline: Donald Trump says further military action against Iran is not currently necessary
articles.title: Trump says U.S. military action against Iran not necessary ‘at this point’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump told reporters in Washington that additional military strikes against Iran do not appear necessary at this time. Speaking on Monday, November 9, 2026, Trump stated that he expects the ongoing conflict to conclude fairly soon. However, he emphasized that the United States military remains fully prepared to respond if circumstances change in the region.
articles.description: “The military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” Trump said

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree on prisoner exchange following Abu Dhabi talks
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with prisoner exchange agreement
articles.summary: Negotiators from Russia and Ukraine concluded two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday with an agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange, though no breakthrough was reached on ending the war. United States envoy Jared Kushner stated that further discussions involving Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy would continue.
articles.description: The talks in the UAE capital were the first ⁠between the two warring sides since February.

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi discusses new memoir and political history in interview
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi interview: ‘Great damage done to the fabric of India by BJP’
articles.summary: In an interview with The Hindu regarding her forthcoming book Belonging: A Journey of Love published by HarperCollins India, senior Indian National Congress politician Sonia Gandhi answered questions from N. Ram about her life, the Emergency, and Indian politics. Gandhi reflected on her decades in India, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi and Indira Gandhi, and her decision to author her own story.
articles.description: Ahead of the launch of her book, Sonia Gandhi speaks to The Hindu, answering a number of questions — personal and political

articles.headline: Antonio Guterres urges world leaders to accelerate climate action at COP31
articles.title: ‘Climate crisis is outrunning us,’ UN chief Guterres says at COP31
articles.summary: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for immediate global responses to climate change at the thirty-first Climate Change Conference in Antalya on Wednesday. He accused the fossil fuel lobby of delaying necessary transitions, noting that emissions reached record highs in 2025 and warning that current environmental trajectories threaten mutual destruction.
articles.description: Guterres says the world must fight harder, accuses the fossil fuel lobby of delaying climate action at critical talks.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap after U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Representatives from Russia and Ukraine agreed to their largest prisoner release during United States-mediated talks held in Abu Dhabi on November 11, 2026. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner stated that final numbers would be announced subsequently, while ongoing fighting and long-range aerial attacks continued to impact both nations during these diplomatic negotiations.
articles.description: The two sides have exchanged thousands of captured soldiers throughout the almost five-year war, started by Russia’s 2022 invasion

articles.headline: El Salvador military destroys headquarters of Haitian gang
articles.title: Haitian PM praises El Salvador after joint strike on alleged home of gang leader
articles.summary: El Salvador's military conducted a ground and air attack that destroyed the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang in Port-au-Prince, according to Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele. The operation followed the deployment of 2,000 Salvadoran troops to Haiti last month after four air force technicians were abducted, drawing mixed international reactions regarding operational legality and human rights.
articles.description: The 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by El Salvador's military, which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.

articles.headline: United Kingdom unveils maritime defence framework to counter Russian threats
articles.title: What is northern Europe’s new drone and warship plan to counter Russia?
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has launched the Northern Navies Initiative to integrate maritime defence capabilities across 10 allied nations in response to escalating Russian threats. Announced by Minister for Defence Readiness Luke Pollard in Oslo on Tuesday, the British-led framework connects autonomous surveillance systems and warships. The agreement involves Joint Expeditionary Force members and aims to enhance critical infrastructure protection and deterrence.
articles.description: UK-led coalition of 10 Northern European nations announces joint defence framework amid rising threats from Moscow.

articles.headline: US House blocks impeachment bid against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: The United States House of Representatives voted 211 to 204 to refer articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee on November 10, 2026. Introduced by Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, the measure effectively halted the push to remove Mr. Hegseth over the war in Iran. Supporters and the Pentagon defended the military actions.
articles.description: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.

articles.headline: India approves ₹62,370 crore fertiliser subsidy for rabi season
articles.title: Cabinet approves ₹62,370 cr. subsidy for P&K fertilisers in rabi season
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved a ₹62,370 crore subsidy for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for the 2026-27 rabi season on November 11, 2026. Union Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated the measure shields farmers from price spikes caused by geopolitical conflicts, ensuring di-ammonium phosphate remains priced at ₹1,350 per bag.
articles.description: Ashwini Vaishnaw said the fertiliser prices have shot up immensely due to the West Asia crisis and the Russia-Ukraine war. However, the Minister said the government has protected farmers' interests by providing adequate fertiliser subsidy

articles.headline: Tech sell-off raises global economic concerns over artificial intelligence spending
articles.title: AI boom or bubble?
articles.summary: A recent technology sector sell-off has triggered widespread economic anxiety regarding heavy investments in artificial intelligence outstripping actual corporate profits. Stock markets plummeted following the Democratic Party victory in United States midterm elections and subsequent proposals for stricter data centre regulations, threatening broader pension funds and economic growth.
articles.description: A tech sell-off has raised questions about AI spending and the risks to jobs and growth across the global economy.

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls Iran war effectively over following discussions with Qatari officials
articles.title: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ militarily
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that the military conflict with Iran is effectively finished following talks at the White House with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani. Speaking in Washington, Trump said regional allies prefer maintaining naval blockades. Iranian officials dismissed the remarks as a distraction while expressing openness to further negotiations without coercion.
articles.description: Iranian officials dismissed Trump's remarks as 'fake news' after he suggested keeping the 'status quo'.

articles.headline: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocates to military base over threats
articles.title: US Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after ‘Iranian threats’
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved from his Washington residence to an undisclosed military base following Iranian threats to his life. The relocation occurred after media outlets published aerial photographs of his newly purchased Georgetown mansion. Bessent continues to lead Operation Economic Outcast, an economic pressure campaign targeting Tehran over regional shipping attacks.
articles.description: Iran is said to have geo-located Bessent's $12.5m mansion in Washington, DC after a photo of it was published.

articles.headline: Severe flooding in Gaza worsens due to extensive wartime infrastructure damage
articles.title: Gaza’s infrastructure collapse leaves residents defenceless against floods
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall caused severe flooding across Gaza, submerging thousands of tents and affecting approximately 350,000 displaced people. Local officials reported that Israeli military operations destroyed vital stormwater and sewage networks, leaving civil defence teams with severely depleted equipment and fuel shortages that severely limit emergency responses to distress calls.
articles.description: Winter weather has continued to wreak havoc in Gaza, with flooding and strong winds.

articles.headline: What do Kyiv residents think about giving up territory to Russia?
articles.title: What do Kyiv residents think about giving up territory to Russia?
articles.description: US President Donald Trump says post-war Ukraine will have a 'different shape' ahead of peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: Beijing denies claims that former tech executive Alice Huang was a Chinese spy
articles.title: Alice Huang, who reportedly had affair with Nvidia CEO, is Chinese banker turned tech exec
articles.summary: Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, formerly linked to Singapore-based cloud partner Megaspeed, faced allegations in a New York Times memo that she was recruited as a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. While public records show fluctuating ownership ties to Megaspeed and past senior roles at Chinese investment firms, Beijing's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations this week as unsubstantiated smears.
articles.description: An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds

articles.headline: China faces economic challenges despite reaching a record one trillion dollar trade surplus
articles.title: Why China’s $1 trillion trade surplus isn’t all good news for its economy
articles.summary: China achieved a record trade surplus of one point zero four trillion dollars in the first ten months of the year, driven by strong semiconductor and tech exports. However, economists warn that chronically weak domestic demand, low household consumption, and inadequate social safety nets leave the country's export-dependent economic model vulnerable to international trade curbs and tariffs.
articles.description: Booming exports mask a thriftiness among the Chinese that could undermine long-term growth.

articles.headline: Oil tanker catches fire after striking naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
articles.summary: An oil tanker caught fire on November 11, 2026, after striking a naval mine in an unauthorised area of the eastern Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's army. The incident follows severe restrictions on the strategic waterway by Tehran since the West Asia war began in February, alongside ongoing US naval blockades and escorts to protect regional oil exports.
articles.description: The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait

articles.headline: Iran security chief says Tehran is waiting for Washington to respond to peace terms
articles.title: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
articles.summary: Iran security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated that Tehran is awaiting a response from the United States regarding seven conditions for peace talks, while dismissing reports of ongoing negotiations in Qatar. Rezaei insisted the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until demands including lifted sanctions and ending regional fighting are met, despite US President Donald Trump noting positive diplomatic momentum.
articles.description: Mohsen Rezaei's comments come as the IRGC said at least three ships had hit mines and caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

articles.headline: U.S. immigration arrests continue nationwide despite President Trump expressing midterm election misgivings
articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations continued nationwide following the midterm elections, with arrests reported in states including California, Florida, and Alabama. While President Donald Trump suggested his crackdown may have been too tough, Department of Homeland Security officials confirmed that deportations will proceed without interruption despite pending asylum applications and valid work permits held by some detainees.
articles.description: After Democrats trounced GOP and won control of the next Congress, Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party

articles.headline: Moody's raises India's fiscal year 2027 growth forecast to 7 percent
articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.summary: Moody's Ratings on November 11, 2026, upgraded India's current fiscal year growth projection to 7 percent from 6.5 percent, citing broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience. According to the U.S.-based agency, robust consumption and strong fundamentals support the outlook, though inflation risks and monetary tightening by the Reserve Bank of India remain concerns.
articles.description: Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said

articles.headline: Congo surpasses 11,000 Ebola cases in deadliest outbreak
articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.summary: Congo's Health Ministry reported on November 11, 2026, that infections in the country's severe Ebola outbreak have reached 11,042, with 5,387 deaths recorded. The epidemic, declared in mid-May and driven by the Bundibugyo virus, has spread to eight provinces, presenting significant containment challenges due to ongoing regional conflicts and strained health systems.
articles.description: Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis

articles.headline: Chinese university procures Nvidia artificial intelligence chips despite United States ban
articles.title: Chinese university buys Nvidia AI H200 chips despite US ban, records show
articles.summary: Northwestern Polytechnical University in China purchased two restricted Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips last month for 874,700 yuan through a local supplier, according to procurement records. The military-linked institution is subject to United States export blacklist restrictions, highlighting ongoing challenges in enforcing technological controls amid broader scrutiny facing Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.
articles.description: Investigation reveals Chinese entities accessing US-restricted AI tech despite stringent export control measures.

articles.headline: Iran security official denies ongoing negotiations with Washington
articles.title: No talks underway with U.S., says Iran top security official
articles.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, a senior Iranian security official, stated that no direct talks are occurring between Tehran and Washington. Speaking with the broadcaster Al-Mayadeen, Rezaei noted that Iran is awaiting an explicit response from the United States regarding seven specific conditions set out in a June interim agreement before normal diplomatic channels can resume.
articles.description: Iran ‌has insisted ‌the ⁠U.S. must meet ⁠seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement ​before the ‌Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume

articles.headline: US treasury secretary urges caution on artificial intelligence competition
articles.title: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized that Washington and Beijing must remain clear-eyed regarding artificial intelligence differences while pursuing cooperation on risk mitigation. Speaking in New York ahead of an upcoming leaders summit in Shenzhen, Bessent outlined plans for a bilateral dialogue on superintelligence and new mutual evaluation practices.
articles.description: Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”

articles.headline: US secretary of state sees no immediate need for attacks on Iran
articles.title: Rubio says 'no need' to attack Iran as diplomacy gathers pace
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that devastating economic pressure on Iran makes major combat operations unnecessary at this stage. Following a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio emphasized that diplomacy is gaining momentum as Tehran continues urging Washington to accept its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table

articles.headline: Qatar PM meets with Trump for talks on ending war on Iran
articles.title: Qatar PM meets with Trump for talks on ending war on Iran
articles.description: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani has met with US President Donald Trump.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality reaches very poor levels following Deepavali
articles.title: Delhi air quality deteriorates, AQI settles at 303
articles.summary: Delhi recorded a very poor air quality index of 303, according to Central Pollution Control Board data released on Wednesday. The deterioration follows post-Deepavali pollution and agricultural stubble burning in neighbouring States. Meanwhile, the Safdarjung weather station recorded a minimum temperature of 14.8 degrees Celsius, and the India Meteorological Department forecast morning fog or mist with a maximum temperature reaching 28 degrees Celsius.
articles.description: The national capital is battling rising pollution levels after Deepavali, with stubble burning in neighbouring States contributing to the deterioration

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu navigates political challenges as opposition builds majority
articles.title: Netanyahu fights to stay relevant as Israel’s opposition closes in
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a unified government amid ongoing coalition negotiations following October elections. While former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot works to form a government holding 67 Knesset seats with parties such as United Torah Judaism, Netanyahu faces multiple corruption trials and intense political pressure regarding security failures connected to the October 7 Hamas attack. The newly sworn-in Knesset includes many members directly affected by the conflict.
articles.description: A new Knesset shaped by October 7 prepares to convene as Netanyahu fights to prevent an opposition-led government

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels report heavy casualties in escalating clashes
articles.title: Yemeni forces, Houthis exchange attacks, claim to inflict heavy losses
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces reported killing or injuring approximately 190 Houthi fighters during hundreds of recent air and artillery attacks across multiple governorates. Meanwhile, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed that Saudi-backed strikes on Sanaa and other areas caused numerous casualties, while reporting retaliatory Houthi missile attacks targeting Riyadh and an oil facility in Abqaiq. The World Health Organization reports thousands of casualties and widespread displacement since August amidst broader regional hostilities.
articles.description: Yemen's government says 190 rebel fighters killed and wounded, as Houthis also claim dealing heavy blows.

articles.headline: US charges three men for allegedly plotting attack on UK base
articles.title: US charges three men for allegedly plotting attack on UK base
articles.description: The US has charged three men over alleged involvement in a plot to attack a Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, UK.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 11,000 cases
articles.title: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
articles.summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 11,042 alongside 5,387 deaths, according to government data released on Tuesday. Health authorities are struggling to contain the rare Bundibugyo strain across eight provinces amid delayed detection, conflict, and strained health services. This marks the second-largest outbreak on record, with containment further hindered by the current lack of specific vaccines or treatments.
articles.description: Authorities struggling to contain DRC's largest Ebola outbreak due to delayed detection and conflict.

articles.headline: Russia intercepts 146 drones in Leningrad region during ongoing escalation
articles.title: Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes as Baltic nations issue drone alerts
articles.summary: Russian authorities reported shooting down 146 drones over the Leningrad region on Tuesday and Wednesday, causing a fire in Ust-Luga and following a refinery strike in Kirishi. Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko stated counter-action is ongoing. The escalation coincides with United States-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi and heightened security warnings across Latvia and Lithuania regarding unidentified drones entering Baltic airspace.
articles.description: Attacks also reported in Russia's northwest as US-mediated talks continue in Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: Bangladesh seeks extradition of ousted leader Sheikh Hasina from India
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained
articles.summary: Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir announced that Bangladesh is seeking the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner transfer process after she applied for a new passport and national identity card in Dhaka on November 9, 2026. Hasina has been living in India since August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising, and faces a death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for a deadly police crackdown.
articles.description: Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it

articles.headline: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese intelligence ties
articles.title: Nvidia shares slump amid investigation into CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia shares dropped more than 4 percent after the semiconductor giant launched an independent board inquiry into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. The probe examines whether Huang was targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation through a former executive at Megaspeed. Huang stated he will fully cooperate with the investigation while broader technology stocks rose on US markets.
articles.description: Huang admits infidelity, denies compromising Nvidia security as China spy inquiry shakes $4.5 trillion AI firm.

articles.headline: Section 219: the future of US-Israeli defence partnership
articles.title: Section 219: the future of US-Israeli defence partnership
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has announced plans to end the billions of dollars in annual US military aid to Israel.

articles.headline: Iran opens training camp for women in readiness for war
articles.title: Iran opens training camp for women in readiness for war
articles.description: Iran has opened its first all-women military training camp amid fears of renewed US attacks.

articles.headline: World leaders gather for climate summit in Turkiye
articles.title: World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
articles.summary: Dozens of heads of state and government officials are scheduled to speak during the high-level segment of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkiye.
