While leaders including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva are attending, several prominent G7 figures are noticeably absent from the annual United Nations summit.
articles.description: COP31 host Turkiye is championing a voluntary initiative to accelerate the electrification of transport, buildings and industry, with a target of raising electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035

articles.headline: Right-wing populism faces potential global shift as political dynamics evolve
articles.title: Is right-wing populism set to retreat?
articles.summary: Right-wing populism surged following the 2008 financial crisis by targeting ruling elites, capitalism, and immigrants while strengthening executive authority in democracies. Donald Trump amplified this movement globally by supporting leaders in Brazil, El Salvador, and Hungary. Observers note that political equations worldwide could change if the former United States president experiences a political weakening.
articles.description: Does the Republicans’ historic defeat in the midterm elections in the United States signal a waning of right-wing populism? Does the right’s emphasis on immigration and foreigners as political issues have an impact on voters? How will the anger of young protesters in India, France and other countries find political expression?

articles.headline: El Salvador fires missiles on Haitian gang hideout
articles.title: El Salvador fires missiles on Haitian gang hideout
articles.description: El Salvador’s military fired rockets at a compound allegedly belonging to the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang.

articles.headline: House panel report details federal failures in Jeffrey Epstein sex crimes case
articles.title: GOP-led House report slams systemic failures in handling of Epstein case
articles.summary: The United States House of Representatives Committee on Oversight and Government Reform released a 137-page report on Tuesday condemning federal negligence in handling Jeffrey Epstein's case. Republican lawmakers criticized a 2007 non-prosecution agreement and jail monitoring lapses preceding his 2019 death. The committee urged the Department of Justice to re-interview witnesses, investigate associates, and ensure survivor record access.
articles.description: Decades of preferential treatment shielded Epstein and his associates, GOP-led report finds.

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy expresses satisfaction with US diplomatic messages on ending war
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says he is pleased with messages from U.S. envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated on November 10, 2026, that he was very pleased with messages from United States presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff regarding the ongoing conflict with Russia. Speaking in Denmark after discussions wrapped up in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Zelenskyy emphasized the critical sequence of achieving a ceasefire before establishing European security guarantees.
articles.description: “I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked about the recent messages by U.S. presidential ‌envoys ⁠Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff

articles.headline: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocates to military base following Iranian threats
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, reports say
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base due to advanced Iranian threats against his life, according to a report published on November 10, 2026, by the New York Times. The security measure occurred amid heightened tensions and an ongoing economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the U.S.-Israeli war.
articles.description: Iran has previously denied plotting to attack ‌officials and people on U.S. soil

articles.headline: Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader following midterm election losses
articles.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader after midterm election rout
articles.summary: On November 10, 2026, U.S. Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio was elected leader of House Republicans, defeating Steve Scalise by 106 votes to 73. Mr. Jordan will replace outgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson as the leader of the party's opposition following significant defeats in the midterm elections that cost Republicans control of Congress.
articles.description: The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress

articles.headline: Delhi voter deletion applications concentrate on three Muslim neighborhoods
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party-appointed booth level agents filed 796 voter deletion applications in Delhi's Mustafabad that were concentrated across 25 polling booths in Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur, and Chandu Nagar. According to an analysis of records and local interviews by The Hindu published on November 10, 2026, all targeted electors were Muslim and selected from areas with sizeable populations and few initial draft roll deletions.
articles.description: 796 Form 7 applications against Muslims, filed by 20 BJP BLAs, concentrated on the rolls of 25 polling booths in Mustafabad. However, BJP claims it has not directed the filing of these applications

articles.headline: US charges three men over alleged terrorist plot targeting UK air base
articles.title: US charges 3 men over alleged Iranian-backed plot at UK Fairford air base
articles.summary: United States prosecutors have charged three men with terrorism-related offenses for allegedly planning attacks across the US and Europe, including a plot targeting the United Kingdom air base RAF Fairford. According to the Department of Justice, the suspects acted in support of Iran and Iraq groups. The UK incident led the US military to withdraw aircraft from British bases.
articles.description: The men, including one who is already in jail, face charges over alleged plot at UK air base used in US war on Iran.

articles.headline: Republicans block Hegseth impeachment motion
articles.title: Republicans block Hegseth impeachment motion
articles.description: Republicans have blocked a motion to impeach US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth over the war on Iran.

articles.headline: House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over handling of Epstein records
articles.title: U.S. House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over release of Epstein records
articles.summary: On November 10, 2026, the Republican-led House Oversight Committee released a report criticising the Trump administration for failing to properly manage the public release of millions of pages of records relating to Jeffrey Epstein. According to the committee, missed deadlines, inadequate redactions that exposed survivors' sensitive information, and concealed names of alleged co-conspirators marred the disclosure process mandated by the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
articles.description: The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act

articles.headline: House Republicans derail impeachment resolution targeting Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.summary: Republicans in the United States House of Representatives blocked an impeachment resolution targeting Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on November 10, 2026. The 211 to 204 vote sent the measure to the Judiciary Committee, averting a formal floor vote. Representative Thomas Massie introduced the articles over unauthorised military actions, while Pentagon officials and President Donald Trump strongly dismissed the allegations.
articles.description: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee; this halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January

articles.headline: Rubio defends Iran war as necessary protection against nuclear threats
articles.title: Rubio says Trump's war against Iran not 'necessarily popular' but needed to stop a nuclear threat
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the military campaign against Iran on November 7, 2026, stating it was launched to neutralize nuclear dangers despite political fallout. The conflict has impacted the economy and contributed to Republican losses in Congress. Meanwhile, mediators are attempting to revive diplomatic talks as regional tensions remain high and military strikes continue.
articles.description: America's top diplomat offered a robust defence of the more than eight-month-old war even as voters blamed Mr. Trump's policies for the hit to their pocketbooks, including higher energy prices that stemmed from disruptions to shipments in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.headline: Displaced Tigray families face renewed uncertainty as fighting escalates in Ethiopia
articles.title: Tigray displaced families fear renewed war as hopes of returning home fade
articles.summary: Families displaced from Western Tigray and currently sheltering in Abi Adi continue to struggle with shortages of food, clean water, and medicine. Four years after the signing of the Pretoria agreement, renewed fighting that began in September 2026 has deepened uncertainty for displaced residents, while thousands of former fighters undergo rehabilitation training in Mekelle.
articles.description: Displaced families face renewed uncertainty as fighting returns to Tigray.

articles.headline: Senate Republicans reelect John Thune as leader despite midterm election defeats
articles.title: U.S. Senate Republicans vote to keep John Thune as leader after steep midterm election losses
articles.summary: On November 11, 2026, United States Senate Republicans reelected South Dakota Senator John Thune as their leader following steep midterm election losses that cost the party its majority. Despite internal frustrations and a 31-15 vote over a delay attempt, no alternative candidates emerged to challenge Mr. Thune for the position during the closed-door meetings.
articles.description: South Dakota Sen. John Thune has spent much of the last two years navigating President Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate

articles.headline: Trump announces possible trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin next week
articles.title: Trump says likely to meet Putin, Xi at China APEC summit
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on November 8, 2026, that he plans to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin during the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Beijing confirmed it is communicating with relevant parties regarding the gathering. The agenda is expected to cover global issues, though analysts note significant political hurdles and differing national priorities among the three nations.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated to reporters that a deal on the Russia-Ukraine war, the Iran issue and nuclear arms control would be on the agenda

articles.headline: Spain holds state funeral for 69 victims of deadly train crash
articles.title: Spain holds state funeral for 69 victims of deadly train crash
articles.description: Spain’s King and Queen have joined families of the 69 victims from a deadly train collision at a state funeral.

articles.headline: US judge allows Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
articles.title: U.S. judge says Trump’s $10 billion BBC defamation case can proceed
articles.summary: A United States federal judge in Florida ruled on November 10, 2026, that President Donald Trump can proceed with a ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against the BBC regarding a deceptively edited speech clip. Judge Jeffrey Kuntz dismissed an unfair trade practices claim while finding the defamation allegations plausible. The BBC previously admitted the edits were misleading and apologised.
articles.description: U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz in Florida declined to throw out Mr. Trump’s defamation ​claim against the BBC, ‌saying Mr. Trump had plausibly alleged that the broadcaster damaged his reputation and knew or should have known the clip was misleading

articles.headline: US Justice Department charges three Iranian operatives over British airbase plot
articles.title: U.S. charges three ‘Iranian operatives’ over U.K. airbase plot
articles.summary: The United States Justice Department announced an eight-count indictment on November 10, 2026, against three men identified as Iranian operatives for allegedly planning a terrorist plot at Britain Royal Air Force Fairford airbase in September. Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri, and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani faced charges involving material support for terrorism, conspiracy, and attempted destruction of property.
articles.description: Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at Britain’s RAF Fairford airbase

articles.headline: Farooq Abdullah urges India-Pakistan dialogue to resolve disputes
articles.title: Will be too late by the time guns fall silent: Farooq Abdullah pushes for India-Pakistan dialogue
articles.summary: National Conference President Farooq Abdullah asserted on November 12, 2026, that military confrontation cannot resolve political disputes between India and Pakistan. Speaking in Jammu and Kashmir, the former chief minister called for immediate engagement without waiting for hostilities to cease, while emphasizing that the region remains an integral part of India despite persistent security threats.
articles.description: The former Chief Minister also asserted that Kashmir is, was and will remain an integral part of India

articles.headline: Megaspeed pledges cooperation with US probe into Nvidia CEO scandal
articles.title: Megaspeed to cooperate with U.S. probe into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scandal
articles.summary: Singapore-headquartered technology firm Megaspeed announced on November 12, 2026, that it will fully cooperate with United States investigations regarding national security risks. The statement followed Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang admitting to a past relationship with a former executive of the company, as Nvidia board members reportedly met to discuss the unfolding situation.
articles.description: Megaspeed, in a statement on November 12, said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously

articles.headline: Nvidia hires law firm to investigate CEO affair with alleged spy
articles.title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
articles.summary: Nvidia has appointed New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to examine a romantic relationship between Chief Executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singaporean executive at customer firm Megaspeed whom the US government alleges is a Chinese spy. The independent probe runs alongside an FBI investigation as the company faces scrutiny and falling stock market values.
articles.description: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

articles.headline: Woman loses arm after being pushed from Naigaon railway station platform
articles.title: Woman loses arm after being pushed off platform at Naigaon railway station; suspect arrested
articles.summary: A 20-year-old woman lost her left arm on November 4, 2026, after being pushed into the gap between two train coaches at Naigaon railway station. According to police statements, the victim confronted a 53-year-old man named Jitendra Hirmukhe for molestation before being shoved. Authorities examined closed-circuit television footage and arrested the suspect on November 9 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
articles.description: The police arrested the accused after examining CCTV footage on November 9, and booked him under Sections 117 (2), 74, and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.headline: Gold heist reported at Tanishq showroom in Madurai
articles.title: Major gold heist at Tanishq jewellery showroom in Madurai
articles.summary: A gold heist occurred at the TATA Tanishq showroom in Madurai on November 11, 2026. Discovered by employees on November 12, Commissioner of Police S. Rajendiran stated that a lone masked man entered through a terrace lift vent and stole display items. Security personnel were deployed outside as forensic teams and police investigated the ongoing theft assessment.
articles.description: The heist occurred on Wednesday night at the recently opened TATA Tanishq showroom on Bypass Road

articles.headline: Authorities demolish alleged illegal mosque in Sambhal district
articles.title: Demolition of 'illegal' mosque in U.P.’s Sambhal village under way amid heavy police deployment
articles.summary: Officials began demolishing an alleged illegal mosque in Qutubpur Satta village within the Asmoli area of Sambhal district on November 12, 2026. Circle Officer Aman Singh stated that a joint team inspected the public land site before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate ordered the action. Heavy police deployment, drone monitoring, and security forces were implemented to maintain peace.
articles.description: Police and revenue officials had received information from local residents over a month ago that a mosque was being constructed illegally on land meant for public use in Qutubpur Satta village

articles.headline: US House begins vote on motion to advance Pete Hegseth impeachment
articles.title: US House Republicans block Pete Hegseth impeachment effort
articles.summary: The United States House of Representatives commenced a procedural vote on Tuesday to evaluate an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Introduced by Republican Representative Thomas Massie, the measure accuses the Pentagon chief of launching an illegal war against Iran and overseeing extrajudicial strikes. Democrats support the initiative, while President Donald Trump and party leaders maintain their backing.
articles.description: Hegseth has been accused of spearheading war on Iran without required congressional approval.

articles.headline: Punjab Police file case over death threat against Arvind Kejriwal
articles.title: Kejriwal, his daughter get death threat from ‘Bishnoi gang member’; case filed in Punjab
articles.summary: The Punjab Police registered a case after Delhi Aam Aadmi Party MLA Jarnail Singh reported receiving a death threat and a seven crore rupee extortion demand. According to the complaint filed at the Cyber Crime Police Station in Mohali, an individual claiming to be part of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang targeted Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal.
articles.description: Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh alleged caller demanded ₹7 crore from Mr. Kejriwal and threatened to kill him and his daughter Harshita Kejriwal if the money was not paid

articles.headline: Manchester United sack manager Michael Carrick amid relegation struggles
articles.title: Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as manager
articles.summary: Manchester United confirmed the departure of men's first-team head coach Michael Carrick on November 12, 2026, following their worst start to an English top-flight season in 40 years. Sitting in the Premier League relegation zone, the club announced they will appoint a permanent successor swiftly, with Mauricio Pochettino heavily linked to the vacant managerial position.
articles.description: This is a breaking news story.

articles.headline: Special investigation team files first charge sheet in Veeramani POCSO case
articles.title: ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani POCSO case: First charge sheet filed, Madras High Court told
articles.summary: A special investigation team filed the initial charge sheet against Gem Granites founder R. Veeramani before a Chennai special court under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan informed the Madras High Court on November 12, 2026, that additional charge sheets will follow within fifteen days, while the judge expressed satisfaction with the ongoing investigation progress.
articles.description: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan told that the charge sheet was filed before a special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on November 11, 2026, and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in the next few days

articles.headline: Owaisi and Azad likely to announce Uttar Pradesh election alliance
articles.title: Owaisi names Chandrashekhar Azad as Uttar Pradesh CM face of Samajik Parivartan Morcha
articles.summary: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen president Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad are expected to declare a political alliance for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh state assembly elections during a joint press conference in Lucknow. The potential coalition aims to consolidate Scheduled Caste and minority voters in the state, presenting a new electoral front outside the major political blocs according to analysts.
articles.description: In a joint press conference with the AIMIM chief, Mr. Azad said, “If SP, Congress or any other party wants to join us to stop BJP from coming to power, we are open to it”

articles.headline: Seoyon and Hwashin commit ₹1,370 crore in investments to Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Amid reports of Korean firms shifting to Andhra Pradesh, Hwashin and Seoyon commit ₹1,370-crore investments in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: South Korean automotive component makers Seoyon E-Hwa Summit Automotive India Private Limited and Hwashin Automotive India Private Limited committed investments totalling ₹1,370 crore in Tamil Nadu on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Hwashin pledged ₹850 crore for research and advanced manufacturing over five years, while Seoyon committed ₹520 crore for technology upgrades. The announcement follows reports that both firms were considering shifting investments to Andhra Pradesh.
articles.description: A formal MoU is expected to be signed at the upcoming Investment Conversion Conclave of the TVK government

articles.headline: United Nations peacekeeping patrol comes under fire in southern Lebanon
articles.title: UNIFIL patrol comes under fire in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: A United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon patrol faced about a dozen rounds of gunfire near Wadi Jilu in the Tyre district on Tuesday, according to the peacekeeping mission. The unit returned fire and reported no casualties before calling for an investigation. The incident highlights ongoing security concerns as G7 foreign ministers debate the future of the force ahead of its mandate expiration in December 2026.
articles.description: UNIFIL said on Tuesday that 'about a dozen rounds' were fired at one of its patrols, without identifying the assailants.

articles.headline: Infosys Science Foundation announces six winners of Infosys Prize 2026
articles.title: Six researchers win Infosys Science Foundation prizes for 2026
articles.summary: The Infosys Science Foundation announced the recipients of the Infosys Prize 2026 across six academic categories on November 12, 2026. Each laureate receives a gold medal, citation, and a prize purse of $100,000. Among the winners is Riddhipratim Basu from the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, selected by an international panel of jurors evaluating early career researchers under forty.
articles.description: A total of 222 applications were received across six categories with the highest for ‘Engineering and Computer Science’ category, ISF said

articles.headline: OpenAI introduces local API processing and model inference for Indian enterprises
articles.title: OpenAI now allows enterprises to process AI requests within India
articles.summary: OpenAI announced local processing and inference for its application programming interface in India on November 12, 2026, enabling eligible businesses to execute workloads entirely within the country. The update extends existing data residency offerings to cover model computations and responses for the GPT-6 Luna model, addressing data localisation requirements for sectors like financial services.
articles.description: The facility initially supports GPT-6 Luna through OpenAI’s API, allowing requests to be processed and AI responses generated within the country to address enterprise data localisation requirements

articles.headline: Madras High Court sentences senior IAS officer Anshul Mishra to imprisonment
articles.title: Madras High Court sentences senior IAS officer to one-month simple imprisonment in contempt case
articles.summary: The Madras High Court found Indian Administrative Service officer Anshul Mishra guilty of contempt of court, ordering him to undergo simple imprisonment for one month. Justice P. Velmurugan directed the court registry to secure the custody of the former Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority Member Secretary if he fails to appeal within thirty days.
articles.description: Justice P. Velmurugan also directs Anshul Mishra, former member secretary of CMDA, to pay a compensation of ₹25,000 from his salary to two aged petitioners

articles.headline: Delhi’s air was already toxic before Deepavali. Here’s what a new study found
articles.title: Delhi’s air was already toxic before Deepavali. Here’s what a new study found
articles.description: A new analysis by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) has found that Delhi entered the Deepavali season with its worst pre-festival air quality in three years.

articles.headline: BBC Verify finds discrepancies in Delhi air pollution data during Diwali
articles.title: Was Delhi pollution data during Diwali misleading?
articles.summary: BBC Verify revealed that official datasets from the Central Pollution Control Board omitted hourly particulate matter readings exceeding 1,000 micrograms during Diwali celebrations in Delhi. Researchers warned that excluding extreme pollution episodes from monitoring stations misrepresents actual air quality levels and prevents accurate daily averages, potentially undermining public trust in official figures across the capital city.
articles.description: BBC Verify analysis indicates missing data led official Diwali pollution figures to be lower than they should be.

articles.headline: Infosys Science Foundation announces six winners for the 2026 Infosys Prize
articles.title: Bengaluru researcher among six Infosys Science Foundation prize winners for 2026
articles.summary: The Infosys Science Foundation announced six laureates for the Infosys Prize 2026 on November 12, honoring researchers under forty across multiple academic disciplines. Each category winner receives a gold medal, citation, and one hundred thousand dollars. Recipients include Riddhipratim Basu from ICTS-TIFR in Bengaluru, alongside scholars from Princeton, Carnegie Mellon, Jindal Global Law School, Gladstone Institutes, and Singapore University of Technology and Design.
articles.description: A total of 222 applications were received across six categories with the highest for ‘Engineering and Computer Science’ category, ISF said

articles.headline: Ladakh Police remove activist Sonam Wangchuk from protest site in Leh
articles.title: Ladakh elections row: Sonam Wangchuk removed from protest site, escorted to residence by Police
articles.summary: Ladakh Police removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site in Leh and escorted him home on November 11, 2026. Authorities advised him to stay indoors under prohibitory orders issued by the Chief Electoral Officer and District Magistrate. The action followed protests by Wangchuk and regional bodies opposing hill council elections scheduled for December 4 due to severe winter conditions and seasonal migration.
articles.description: Mr. Wangchuk is protesting the holding of hill council elections on December 4, citing harsh winter conditions and large-scale seasonal migration

articles.headline: US military member arrested in the UK on suspicion of espionage
articles.title: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
articles.summary: British authorities detained an unidentified 41-year-old United States military member near Gloucester on Tuesday under the National Security Act 2023 for allegedly assisting a foreign intelligence service. London Metropolitan Police counterterrorism forces collaborated with the FBI and US military on the operation. The suspect remains in custody in London while officers search two Gloucestershire properties.
articles.description: London Metropolitan Police says its 'counterterror' forces worked closely with the FBI and US military to make arrest.

articles.headline: Congressional report finds federal failures in Jeffrey Epstein investigation
articles.title: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
articles.summary: Crimes committed by late financier Jeffrey Epstein after 2005 could have been prevented due to investigative and prosecutorial failures, a congressional investigation concluded on Tuesday. The Republican-led House Oversight Committee released its final report following a fifteen-month review, criticizing the united states attorney office for a 2007 agreement allowing Epstein to evade federal prosecution. The panel also cited institutional failures at the New York prison where Epstein died in 2019.
articles.description: The report by a Republican-led congressional committee follows a 15-month investigation into the handling of the late disgraced financier's case.

articles.headline: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang in operation leaving 20 dead
articles.title: Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead
articles.summary: Salvadoran forces supported an operation by Haitian police on Sunday that targeted the 400 Mawozo gang headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, resulting in twenty deaths. Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele announced the attack on social media platform X. Amnesty International subsequently urged both governments to ensure that all military deployments comply strictly with international human rights law.
articles.description: Salvadoran troops backed the police operation ahead of the Haitian prime minister’s visit to El Salvador.

articles.headline: British police arrest US Army soldier near Gloucester for alleged Russian espionage
articles.title: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
articles.summary: Counter Terrorism Policing London detained a forty-one-year-old senior serviceman near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023 on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence. Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel confirmed the arrest involved espionage allegations regarding sensitive military information. The unnamed suspect, stationed at Imjin Barracks, remains in custody at a London police station while investigations continue.
articles.description: The 41-year-old senior soldier is accused of national security offences and is being questioned in London.

articles.headline: Vizianagaram district expects increased investments from Bhogapuram airport development
articles.title: CII Partnership Summit: Vizianagaram likely to attract more investments due to Bhogapuram airport, officials say
articles.summary: Vizianagaram district in Andhra Pradesh is expected to attract significant investments during the CII Partnership Summit 2026, held on Thursday and Friday, November 12 and 13, 2026, in Visakhapatnam, driven by proximity to the Bhogapuram international airport. Officials highlighted local geographical advantages and planned infrastructure, including a Reliance Industries Limited data centre project expected to draw nearly ₹1 lakh crore.
articles.description: The government has recently given its nod for Reliance Industries Limited for the construction of its data centre in Bhogapuram and the project is expected to attract nearly ₹1 lakh crore investments

articles.headline: US administration proposes new eligibility rules to cut food aid
articles.title: Trump administration seeks to cut food aid for more than six million people
articles.summary: The United States Department of Agriculture published a proposed rule on Tuesday to eliminate automatic Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program eligibility tied to Temporary Assistance for Needy Families. The change would remove approximately 6.3 million people from the federal food aid programme and strip 1.8 million children of free school lunches, prompting strong criticism from Democratic lawmakers.
articles.description: Trump’s proposal builds on earlier cuts to federal food aid programme used by more than 36 million low-income Americans.

articles.headline: Alice Huang visited Taiwan eight times during 2024 and 2025
articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.summary: Alice Huang, an executive accused of spying for Beijing while linked to Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, entered Taiwan eight times between 2024 and 2025 using a Hong Kong passport, according to Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Taiwanese officials stated she entered under standard business visitor status and security agencies are currently investigating the matter.
articles.description: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

articles.headline: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
articles.title: Republicans elect Trump ally Jim Jordan as new US House minority leader
articles.summary: House Republicans chose Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan as their new minority leader in a secret ballot vote on Tuesday following their midterm election losses. Jordan, who currently chairs the House Oversight Committee and cofounded the House Freedom Caucus, defeated Steve Scalise to succeed Mike Johnson as the top Republican in the chamber.
articles.description: Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to succeed Mike Johnson as GOP minority leader, promising unity and a robust opposition.

articles.headline: Ugandan police investigate deaths of four pupils in suspected poisoning
articles.title: Oranges investigated after four girls die in suspected Uganda school poisoning
articles.summary: Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four girls aged nine to 11 at Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre in Kampala on Tuesday, November 11, 2026, suspected to result from poisoning after eating oranges shared by a fellow pupil. The head teacher has been arrested to assist investigations, while post-mortem examinations are conducted to determine the exact cause of death.
articles.description: The girls started vomiting after eating oranges brought in by a fellow pupil - police are travelling to the village they came from.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh leaders pitch the State as a global investment hub
articles.title: Pawan Kalyan pitches Andhra Pradesh as trusted global hub; Lokesh unveils red-carpet framework at 31st Vizag CII Summit
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and IT Minister Nara Lokesh promoted the state as a secure corporate destination at the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Mr. Lokesh announced that the government has attracted ₹22.6 lakh crore in investment commitments since June 2024, highlighting projects such as Google's upcoming AI hub in Visakhapatnam.
articles.description: Mr. Lokesh urged corporate leaders to move beyond setting up manufacturing units and relocate their primary corporate headquarters to Andhra Pradesh, citing superior quality of life, skilled talent pipelines, and seamless connectivity anchored by new ports and the Bhogapuram International Airport

articles.headline: Pope Leo arrives in Peru for final leg of Latin American tour
articles.title: Pope Leo welcomed by millions in his second ‘homeland’ of Peru
articles.summary: Millions of people gathered in Lima on Wednesday to welcome the 71-year-old pontiff during his visit to Peru, which he regards as his adopted homeland. According to a Vatican statement, three million individuals greeted him, marking a record for his papacy. During his address to President Keiko Fujimori, the religious leader urged the nation to address past conflicts and build trust.
articles.description: On his Latin America tour, the pontiff is expected to spend 3 days in Chiclayo, where ​he was bishop from 2015-2023.

articles.headline: Rubio says no need for major combat operations against Iran
articles.title: Rubio says no need for major combat operations against Iran
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says there is “no need” for further major combat operations against Iran

articles.headline: Nigeria President Bola Ahmed Tinubu launches re-election manifesto
articles.title: Can Nigeria's president regain voters' trust after painful first term?
articles.summary: Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu launched his official re-election manifesto ahead of the general election scheduled for January 2027. The plan aims for six percent annual economic growth by 2031 alongside major additions of security personnel and affordable housing. While administration officials highlighted falling inflation rates, voters continue to face severe cost-of-living pressures resulting from earlier economic reforms.
articles.description: For Nigerians to feel meaningful improvements, reforms will need to go beyond the promises outlined, analysts say.

articles.headline: Nepal passenger vehicle crash kills ten people in Bagmati province
articles.title: At least 10 killed as passenger vehicle plunges off steep slope in Nepal
articles.summary: Ten individuals died and five sustained injuries when a passenger vehicle carrying roughly fifteen people plunged down a steep slope in Nepal's Makawanpur district. The vehicle fell approximately 500 metres while travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi. The deceased included three women, two girls, and five men, while the injured were transported to Hetauda Hospital for medical treatment following the accident.
articles.description: The vehicle, carrying around 15 people, was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi at the time of the accident

articles.headline: Protests erupt in Bangladesh demanding return of ousted prime minister
articles.title: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest
articles.summary: Demonstrations broke out across Bangladesh as supporters of deposed leader Sheikh Hasina demanded her return from exile in India, leading to clashes with security forces and the death of a 60-year-old bus driver in Faridpur on Tuesday. Protesters blocked traffic on the Padma bridge and set fire to police and passenger vehicles. Government officials rejected passport requests and called her a fugitive facing a death sentence.
articles.description: Supporters of Sheikh Hasina want her to return from exile in India.

articles.headline: Telangana police rescue twenty nine women in fertility centre raids
articles.title: Why are fertility centres in Hyderabad in crosshairs over human egg harvesting? | Explained
articles.summary: Telangana police raided three premises in Hyderabad and rescued twenty nine women from six states who were confined for human egg harvesting. Specialized fertility centres offer various medical procedures and assisted reproductive technology packages ranging from two lakh fifty thousand rupees to fifty lakh rupees, according to local reports.
articles.description: The police have arrested a number of people including the persons who had rented the premises and were liaisoning with the fertility centres. The Health and Medical Department has issued notices to 13 ART centres out of the 44 identified facilities

articles.headline: Protests emerge over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.title: Why the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project has been contentious | Explained
articles.summary: The planned construction of a dam on the Siang river by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation has sparked opposition from the Adi community in Arunachal Pradesh, resulting in activist arrests starting in October. articles.description: What does the project promise? Why are Adi community members protesting against the building of the dam? And what is the Government saying?

articles.headline: Nvidia chief executive admits affair with woman suspected of Chinese espionage

He also wears a cool leather jacket. Which makes […]

articles.headline: Four family members die in Arunachal Pradesh fire destroying 24 houses
articles.title: Four of family dead in Arunachal town fire, 24 houses gutted
articles.summary: A devastating blaze swept through Parsi-Parlo town in Arunachal Pradesh on November 12, 2026, killing four family members and destroying 24 houses. Deputy Commissioner Cheechung Chukhu stated that the husband remains missing and the casualty toll may rise. Officials noted the remote town lacks adequate firefighting facilities, hindering emergency response efforts.
articles.description: The exact cause of the blaze is yet to be established, though preliminary reports suggest that it may have originated in a kitchen

articles.headline: Security officials move Kolkata to Mumbai flight to isolation bay after hijack threat note found
articles.title: Hijack threat note found in Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight; aircraft taken to isolation bay
articles.summary: A Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight was moved to an airport isolation bay on November 11, 2026, after a hijack threat note was discovered in the aircraft washroom before departure. Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh stated that security protocols were immediately activated and all passengers were deboarded following the discovery of the note, which threatened that the plane would be hijacked at 11:10 a.m.
articles.description: All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and it was taken to the isolation bay

articles.headline: Passenger detained over bomb hoax on Kolkata Mumbai flight
articles.title: Passenger held over hijack threat to Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight
articles.summary: Authorities apprehended a passenger and handed them over to airport police following a hoax hijack threat aboard an Air India flight from Kolkata to Mumbai. A cabin crew member discovered a handwritten threat note inside the aircraft lavatory before departure, prompting safety checks and deboarding of all 105 passengers. The flight eventually departed several hours later after security procedures declared the threat a hoax.
articles.description: The passenger was handed over to the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International (NSCBI) Airport Police Station

articles.headline: Nvidia and chief executive face shareholder lawsuit over alleged spy scandal
articles.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
articles.summary: Nvidia Corporation and sixty-three-year-old Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang face a proposed class-action lawsuit filed on November 9, 2026, in a federal court in San Jose, California. Shareholders accuse them of misleading investors by failing to disclose an alleged relationship between Mr. Huang and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed who has been linked to Chinese intelligence. Mr. Huang admitted to infidelity, and Nvidia announced an independent investigation.
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Chinese executive Alice Huang.

articles.headline: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak begins house arrest
articles.title: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
articles.summary: Disgraced former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak arrived at his Kuala Lumpur residence on Tuesday to serve the remainder of a corruption sentence under house arrest. The seventy-three-year-old was escorted by a heavily armed police convoy after a high court ruled the transfer effective immediately following a royal pardon. Najib previously served four years in prison for embezzling funds from the one million development berhad sovereign wealth fund and faces another pending sentence.
articles.description: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.

articles.headline: Rockstar Games releases Grand Theft Auto VI after thirteen year wait
articles.title: From Pong to GTA VI: Play your way through 50 years of video games
articles.summary: Rockstar Games releases Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, ending a thirteen-year sequel wait within a global video game industry that generated $201.6bn in revenue in 2025, according to market research firm Newzoo. This milestone highlights five decades of gaming evolution from early arcade titles like Pong to modern open-world blockbusters.
articles.description: Video games are now a $200bn business. Play through the six games that tell the story of how they got there.

articles.headline: Noel Tata retires as Tata Investment Corporation chairperson with successor named
articles.title: Noel Tata retires as Tata Investment chaiperson; Bahram Vakil to succeed him
articles.summary: Noel Tata stepped down as chairperson and director of Tata Investment Corporation on November 11, 2026, concluding over sixteen years of leadership. In accordance with Tata Group Governance Guidelines, the board appointed Bahram Vakil as the new chairperson effective November 12, 2026, while also naming Abizer Shabbir Diwanji as an independent director.
articles.description: Recognising his contribution, the board appointed Mr. Tata ‘Chairman Emeritus’ with effect from November 12

articles.headline: Two Special Police Officers go missing in the Kishtwar district
articles.title: Two missing policemen found dead in J&K’s Kishtwar
articles.summary: Two Special Police Officers identified as Babi Chand and Rashpal Kumar disappeared on November 12, 2026, while traveling between Dachhan and Marwah in Jammu and Kashmir. Security forces, including police and the Army's Rashtriya Rifles, initiated a joint search operation across mountainous forest terrain after their mobile phones became unreachable. articles.headline: Iran remains committed to nuclear non-proliferation treaty

articles.summary: Iran maintains its commitment to the treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons despite restricting cooperation with the international atomic energy agency following military attacks, foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated on Monday. Mediated talks continue between Tehran and Washington to prevent further regional escalation.

articles.headline: State security forces restrict access to proposed Siang dam site

articles.headline: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion valuation in upcoming stock market debut

articles.headline: Drone Federation India warns against heavy reliance on imported components
articles.title: Drone industry needs deeper localisation as import dependence poses risks: DFI
articles.summary: The Drone Federation India warned that heavy reliance on imported components leaves the domestic unmanned aerial vehicle sector vulnerable to foreign supply restrictions, particularly from China. articles.title: More than 300 migrants rescued off Spain’s Canary Islands

Eisenkot must navigate deep divisions over military conscription and relations with Arab-led parties to succeed during his 28-day window.

articles.summary: Young chimpanzees acquire their calls through a learning process similar to human language acquisition, according to scientific insights highlighted in a newsletter on November 11. articles.description: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon.

articles.headline: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan hospitalized and returned to prison

articles.description: The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities

articles.headline: High Court directs authorities to protect LGBTQIA students in schools
articles.title: What the Punjab and Haryana High Court said about protecting LGBTQIA+ students in schools? | Explained
articles.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court directed the Haryana education department and the Central Board of Secondary Education to comply with Supreme Court guidelines on student mental health. articles.headline: Israel's new parliament convenes as Eisenkot seeks to form government

articles.description: President Isaac Herzog, ceremonially opening the session, called on all sides to work together and avoid a fresh election in a deeply polarised country weary from three years of war.

articles.headline: Legislator and farmers protest against Centre regarding drought relief funds

articles.summary: Aland MLA B.R. Patil staged a protest in Kalaburagi against the Central Government for allegedly failing to release drought relief funds for Karnataka. articles.summary: The board of peace called on Israel to immediately allow essential humanitarian supplies into Gaza after heavy rain and sewage flooding affected tens of thousands of tents. articles.description: The group, formed by Trump, issues rare criticism of Israel, while also blaming Hamas for the suffering of civilians in Gaza.

articles.summary: Diplomatic efforts to conclude the United States-Israel war on Iran gained traction as US President Donald Trump and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani discussed peace at the White House. articles.headline: Building collapse in Brooklyn construction site leaves two people dead

Critics argue that an alternative overland alignment through paddy fields would be safer and more cost-effective.
articles.description: The proposed tunnel between Balaramapuram and Vizhinjam to provide rail connectivity to Vizhinjam International Seaport has triggered serious environmental and land stability concerns in the region

articles.headline: Hegseth promises to defend ‘warriors’ as he faces impeachment

articles.headline: Three-storey building collapses in Brooklyn
articles.title: Three-storey building collapses in Brooklyn
articles.description: A three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn, New York, killing at least two people and injuring several others.

articles.headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth prepares for first Pentagon briefing amid impeachment threat
articles.title: Pete Hegseth to hold first Pentagon briefing since May amid impeachment threat
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to hold a news conference on November 10, 2026, to address an impeachment resolution filed by Representative Thomas Massie. The congressional move follows criticism over military actions in Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela, though President Donald Trump continues to support the Pentagon chief despite widespread political fallout from the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: The briefing will be Pete Hegseth’s first since May even as the U.S. military has kept up intermittent operations against the Islamic Republic as well as fatal strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America

articles.headline: Google expands tensor processing unit lineup to challenge Nvidia
articles.title: Google launches two AI chips as it seeks to challenge NVIDIA’s dominance
articles.summary: Google introduced two new artificial intelligence chip systems, the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, aiming to challenge Nvidia corporation in the computing infrastructure sector. The new processors are designed for secure inference and memory-intensive workloads, as the technology giant seeks to attract external customers and expand custom accelerator adoption beyond its own data centres.
articles.description: New systems target secure AI inference and memory-intensive workloads as Google seeks to expand enterprise adoption of its in-house AI processors

articles.headline: Attacks escalate between Saudi-led forces and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis
articles.title: Attacks escalate between Saudi-led forces and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis
articles.description: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles fired by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen as attacks between them escalate.

articles.headline: Bangladesh prosecutor says ousted leader Sheikh Hasina faces execution
articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
articles.summary: A Bangladeshi prosecutor stated that ousted leader Sheikh Hasina will face execution upon returning home after missing the deadline to appeal her death sentence. Convicted in absentia for crimes against humanity during the 2024 protest crackdown, the 79-year-old former Prime Minister has vowed to return from India in December despite legal risks. Her planned homecoming creates political challenges for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as authorities manage diplomatic tensions and domestic security concerns.
articles.description: ‘Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,’ Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.

articles.headline: Investigation reveals Israeli soldiers operating as West Bank settlers
articles.title: Israeli soldiers are also settlers in West Bank: Al Jazeera investigation
articles.summary: An investigation by Al Jazeera found that Israeli settlers participating in violent attacks in the occupied West Bank frequently return wearing military uniforms to impose orders on Palestinian victims. According to the report, fourteen of sixty-three Palestinians killed by settlers since October 7, 2023, were shot by individuals serving in the army or wearing military uniforms.
articles.description: Blurred lines between Israeli soldiers and settlers fuel systematic West Bank violence and mass displacement.

articles.headline: US lawmakers demand Nvidia CEO testify regarding alleged affair with Chinese intelligence
articles.title: What could Chinese intelligence have learned from Nvidia CEO’s affair?
articles.summary: Republican leaders in the United States House of Representatives have ordered Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang to attend a closed-door briefing regarding his past extramarital relationship with Alice Huang. Intelligence officials suspect the former Singapore-based tech executive acted as a Chinese intelligence operative to influence chip export restrictions. While Nvidia launched an internal investigation finding no compromised secrets, President Donald Trump confirmed Federal Bureau of Investigation scrutiny while supporting the executive.
articles.description: Nvidia says no secrets were compromised, but experts question what sensitive information may have been exposed.

articles.headline: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng blocked from entering India for Bharat Summit
articles.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit
articles.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng stated that orders from India's Ministry of Home Affairs cancelled her valid visa, preventing her from attending the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen, was invited as a speaker on press freedom. She linked the entry denial to a question she previously asked Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Norway.
articles.description: Ms. Lyng says she has been denied entry into India despite having a visa

articles.headline: United States defense secretary condemns impeachment push as sabotage
articles.title: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth calls US House impeachment effort a ‘farce’
articles.summary: United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defended his military record during a Pentagon news conference, dismissing impeachment resolutions introduced by Representative Thomas Massie as a farce and sabotage. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also defended the actions taken, while lawmakers discussed the potential congressional timeline and the votes required for removal from office.
articles.description: Hegseth condemns impeachment resolution against him as 'sabotage', defending his actions and policy decisions.

articles.headline: Bangladesh prosecutor warns Hasina faces execution if she returns
articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor warns Hasina faces execution if she returns
articles.description: Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal has said ousted PM Sheikh Hasina will be executed if she returns home.

articles.headline: Health experts meet to review measles elimination status across the Americas
articles.title: Why the US, Mexico and Guatemala may lose their measles-free status
articles.summary: International health experts gathered in Washington, DC, for an annual conference hosted by the Pan American Health Organization to determine whether countries including the United States, Mexico, and Guatemala retain their measles elimination status. The regional monitoring commission is reviewing epidemiological data amid a major resurgence of the virus, with the United States experiencing its largest outbreak in nearly thirty years following sustained transmission since January 2025.
articles.description: An independent commission is reviewing whether countries in the Americas still meet measles elimination criteria.

articles.headline: Cameroon power structures face continued scrutiny amid presidential absences
articles.title: Cameroon: Who is really calling the shots?
articles.summary: President Paul Biya of Cameroon returned to Yaounde on August 20 after more than 10 weeks abroad, reigniting public debate regarding executive authority and decision-making during his prolonged absences. Although the constitution permits delegation of powers and a constitutional amendment reintroduced the office of vice president, researchers and analysts note that informal networks and close presidential aides continue to heavily influence governance.
articles.description: Biya’s absences raise questions about who holds power and what comes next in Cameroon.

articles.headline: Malaysian court clears legal hurdles for Najib Razak house arrest
articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.summary: A High Court in Malaysia removed all legal obstacles for imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to serve his graft sentence under house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home until August 23, 2028. According to his lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, the ruling follows royal clemency and a political party paying a 50 million ringgit fine. The decision covers only his reduced six-year sentence tied to the 1MDB scandal, while a separate 15-year sentence remains under appeal.
articles.description: Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.

articles.headline: Supreme Court highlights vehicular emissions as major Delhi polluter
articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India stressed that vehicular emissions are a primary driver of toxic air pollution in Delhi and the National Capital Region, surpassing festival-related concerns. Led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, the court directed local municipal, police, and state authorities from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Rajasthan to submit compliance reports on traffic regulations. The bench emphasized immediate intervention and time-bound action plans to curb worsening air quality across the capital region.
articles.description: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

articles.headline: Hezbollah secretary-general welcomes US and Israeli electoral setbacks
articles.title: US election results could be positive for Lebanon, Hezbollah chief says
articles.summary: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem has praised Republican setbacks in US midterm elections and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failing to secure a governing majority in Israeli polls. Speaking via video-link, Qassem stated that these political shifts benefit Lebanon and reinforced his refusal to disarm the Iran-backed group while Israeli forces continue to occupy parts of southern Lebanon.
articles.description: Naim Qassem says Republican losses and Israel's election result could help Lebanon maintain sovereignty.

articles.headline: Barcelona erupts in violence after general strike
articles.title: Barcelona erupts in violence after general strike
articles.description: Protesters hurled fireworks at police and set rubbish bins ablaze in Barcelona after Spain’s general strike.

articles.headline: Amnesty International faults UN peacekeepers over South Sudan massacre
articles.title: UN peacekeepers failed to protect civilians before South Sudan massacre: Amnesty
articles.summary: United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to take adequate preventive action prior to a March 1 village raid in Abiemnom that left at least 213 people dead, according to an Amnesty International report released on November 12, 2026. The rights group stated that the mission known as UNMISS received advance warnings but did not reinforce its forces until after armed men from Mayom County carried out the attack.
articles.description: “Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director

articles.headline: FBI investigates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy affair
articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced that the FBI is investigating Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang regarding an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent named Alice Huang. Nvidia shares dropped over 4 percent following the revelations, and the company launched an independent inquiry. Meanwhile, China denied any plot to ensnare the executive, dismissing the allegations as unfounded smears.
articles.description: The sudden emergence of Nvidia CEO Huang's infidelity has created concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence

articles.headline: Delhi pollution data vanishes from monitoring stations during Deepavali night
articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.summary: Air quality data disappeared from multiple government monitoring stations across Delhi during Deepavali night, prompting criticism from analysts who noted the missing figures artificially lowered the Air Quality Index. Readings blanked out for several hours on November 9, 2026, at locations like Patparganj and Anand Vihar, where previous levels reached extreme multiples of World Health Organization limits amid severe regional smog.
articles.description: Missing PM2.5 data for several hours on CPCB website understated city’s pollution levels: experts; 227 PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 stations; govt. will look into it: Mishra

articles.headline: Iran designates Argentinian navy and air force as terrorist organisations
articles.title: Iran designates Argentinian navy, air force as ‘terrorist organisations’
articles.summary: The Iranian Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday that it will classify the naval and air forces of Argentina as terrorist organisations in a reciprocal move following Argentina's similar designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in March. Argentina's foreign ministry categorically rejected the measure, while historical tensions between the nations stem from the nineteen ninety-four AMIA Jewish community centre bombing in Buenos Aires.
articles.description: The move comes months after the government of Javier Milei designated Iran's IRGC as a 'terrorist organisation'.

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept ballistic missile over Riyadh
articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: Sources
articles.summary: The military coalition fighting in Yemen intercepted a ballistic missile targeting Riyadh on November 10, 2026, causing explosions across the Saudi capital. The incident follows recent strikes on the city's business district. In response to ongoing Houthi attacks, Saudi warplanes carried out airstrikes against a gas facility and a state oil company building in Sanaa, according to the Houthi news agency Saba.
articles.description: AFP journalists heard the blasts, and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an aerial threat

articles.headline: US judge permits Donald Trump to proceed with defamation lawsuit against BBC
articles.title: Judge rules Trump’s $10bn BBC defamation suit can proceed
articles.summary: A federal district judge in Florida partially rejected a motion from the British Broadcasting Corporation to dismiss a defamation lawsuit filed by United States President Donald Trump. The civil case stems from an October twenty twenty-four documentary that allegedly used deceptive editing on a January sixth speech, leading the court to rule the reputation damage claims as plausibly alleged while the broadcaster maintains confidence in its legal position.
articles.description: The BBC denies defamation charge as Trump celebrates “huge victory” in court decision.

articles.headline: COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains
articles.title: COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains
articles.description: From catastrophic floods in Nepal to record-breaking heat, droughts and wildfires, the climate crisis is no longer a future threat. It is happening now. As world leaders gather in Antalya for COP31, the focus has shifted from promises to implementation. Countries are under pressure to cut emissions, fund adaptation efforts and help vulnerable nations cope with rising climate impacts.

articles.headline: United Airlines bans personal AI assistants from booking passenger flights
articles.title: United won’t let your AI agent book your flight
articles.summary: United Airlines announced it will prohibit personal artificial intelligence agents from purchasing tickets on its platform, citing data privacy and regulatory compliance challenges. Company executives highlighted concerns regarding unauthorized transactions and the inability of automated tools to complete mandatory safety attestations, aligning with similar restrictions implemented by other major corporations across various industries.
articles.description: United says it won't let personal AI assistants book tickets on the airline, citing both privacy and regulatory concerns. The company says it hasn't yet seen many people try to use AI agents to book their flights, The Wall Street Journal reports, in line with observations from other businesses like Doordash. But United is concerned […]

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to open debate after ‘Intellectual Naxal’ remark
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to open debate after ‘Intellectual Naxal’ remark
articles.description: A fresh political confrontation has erupted between the Congress and the BJP after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks about “intellectual Naxals” during his Deepavali visit to Bastar. Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi responded by challenging the Prime Minister to an open debate on who is truly anti-national and who is influenced by foreign forces. The Congress has accused PM Modi of using official platforms to attack political opponents, while the BJP maintains that Parliament remains the proper forum for debate.

articles.headline: Senior U.S. Justice Department officials resign following midterm elections
articles.title: Wave of resignations from U.S. Justice Department after midterms
articles.summary: Several high-ranking United States Justice Department officials have resigned, including civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon and national security prosecutor John Eisenberg. Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the departures on Thursday and Friday, following midterm elections that resulted in heavy defeats for President Donald Trump’s Republican Party. Dhillon previously sought voter registration lists across approximately 30 states while Eisenberg and Jason Reding Quinones oversaw investigations into perceived political opponents.
articles.description: The Justice Department under Donald Trump has pursued cases against a number of perceived enemies, and several prosecutors have lost their jobs over their reluctance or inability to bring charges

articles.headline: Nvidia executive espionage allegations intensify US chip export debate
articles.title: Nvidia spy scandal fuels debate over chip exports to China
articles.summary: Nvidia board members launched an inquiry into CEO Jensen Huang following claims he had a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. US lawmakers cited the controversy to demand tighter export controls on advanced artificial intelligence chips destined for China. Meanwhile, industry analysts noted that the investigation could significantly diminish Huang's anti-restriction influence in Washington.
articles.description: US lawmakers call for tighter restrictions on chip sales amid inquiry into Nvidia CEO's relationship with alleged spy.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO admits affair involving executive tied to chip smuggling
articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang acknowledged having an affair with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based firm suspected of smuggling advanced artificial intelligence microchips into China. The revelation highlights how Chinese startups continue acquiring restricted processors through smuggling or foreign data centre loopholes to train competitive models despite United States export controls.
articles.description: With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies

articles.headline: Thousands march to mark Poland’s Independence Day
articles.title: Thousands march to mark Poland’s Independence Day

articles.headline: Hoax bomb threats target schools across Italy, UK and Ireland
articles.title: Hoax bomb threats target schools across Italy, UK and Ireland

articles.headline: U.S. lawmakers introduce eight articles of impeachment against defence secretary
articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.summary: Representative Thomas Massie and supporting lawmakers filed eight articles of impeachment against United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth. The resolution cites alleged violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution regarding military actions in Iran, civilian casualties from a strike on an Iranian elementary school, maritime strike fatalities, retaliation against Senator Mark Kelly, and the unauthorized capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.
articles.description: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

articles.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan accuses Keralam government of concentrating power in chief minister office
articles.title: Keralam government centralising power in Chief Minister’s office: Pinarayi Vijayan
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan criticized the Keralam administration for centralizing authority within the Chief Minister office. Speaking at a Communist Party of India Marxist meeting in Chathurakkinar, he alleged that cabinet ministers remain uninformed about major departmental decisions. Vijayan called for a formal judicial inquiry into administrative actions regarding an electricity purchase agreement.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia boosts crude oil production to highest level since February war
articles.title: Oil production nears pre-Iran war levels, OPEC says
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia increased crude oil output to 10.563 million barrels per day in October, reaching its highest level since military actions against Iran disrupted global energy markets in February. An OPEC report indicated that the production surge helped stabilize exports and lower fuel costs. Meanwhile, OPEC kept its global demand growth forecasts unchanged for the upcoming year.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia reports oil outputs soared to highest levels in months despite continued shipping disruptions.

articles.headline: Gaza goalkeeper killed in Israeli attack
articles.title: Gaza goalkeeper killed in Israeli attack
articles.description: Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Abdel-Malek was killed in an Israeli strike days after the Thousand Martyrs Cup.

articles.headline: White House accuses congressional Democrats of abusing power through upcoming investigations
articles.title: Trump’s White House calls Democratic plans for congressional probes ‘abuse’
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump issued a letter criticizing incoming Democratic congressional majorities for planning investigations into executive officials. White House lawyer William Scharf argued that proposed subpoenas exceed constitutional limits and threaten government operations. Democrats countered that their oversight role is a legitimate legislative function necessary to hold officials accountable.
articles.description: Democratic lawmaker Robert Garcia denounced a White House letter as an unconstitutional attack on legislative branch.

articles.headline: Democratic Republic of Congo sentences soldiers to death
articles.title: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for being 'cowards'
articles.summary: A military court in Walikale sentenced sixty-six soldiers to death for cowardice, mutiny and abandoning frontline positions during clashes with the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation rebel coalition. The trials aim to improve troop discipline as the Congolese army battles armed groups in eastern regions. The government lifted its death penalty moratorium in March 2024 to target traitors and insurgents within its ranks.
articles.description: The Congolese army's fight against rebel groups has long been hampered by disarray within its ranks.

articles.headline: Lewis Hamilton urges Israel to reopen Rafah border crossing for Gaza aid
articles.title: F1 champion Lewis Hamilton calls on Israel to open Gaza’s Rafah border
articles.summary: Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton called upon Israel to reopen the Rafah border crossing to allow critical humanitarian supplies into Gaza following heavy rains and flooding. During a visit to el-Arish, the British driver inspected Egyptian Red Crescent warehouses holding blocked aid. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denied allegations of delaying winter supplies as the United Nations reported thousands of tents awaiting entry.
articles.description: Hamilton visited the Egypt-Gaza border as conditions worsened for Palestinians in Gaza after heavy rains.

articles.headline: First Palestinian American elected in New York talks to Al Jazeera
articles.title: First Palestinian American elected in New York talks to Al Jazeera
articles.description: Palestinian American senator-elect Aber Kawas says Gaza and affordability in New York drove her into politics.

articles.headline: Donald Trump says FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO over alleged Chinese spy affair
articles.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that Federal Bureau of Investigation agents are probing an extramarital relationship between Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang and a woman allegedly operating as a Chinese spy. Trump spoke with Huang on Monday and expressed belief that the executive had no knowledge of espionage. The Chinese foreign ministry rejected the accusations entirely.
articles.description: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.

articles.headline: Representative Thomas Massie moves to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over Iran war
articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky launches bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.summary: Representative Thomas Massie introduced an impeachment resolution on November 9, 2026, targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over his role in military operations involving Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela. The legislative push emerges amid Republican midterm election losses attributed to the conflict, drawing backing from Democratic leaders while receiving staunch opposition from President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Thomas Massie, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Pete Hegseth's actions amounted to high crimes and misdemeanors

articles.headline: Indian boxer Ambekar Meetei reaches Youth Olympics 50kg final
articles.title: Ambekar Meetei storms into men’s 50kg final at Youth Olympics
articles.summary: India's Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei advanced to the men's 50kg boxing final at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games following a 5-0 semifinal win over Colombia's Izzon Jeffrey Galea Arevalo. The victory ended a 16-year wait for an Indian boxer in a Youth Olympics final, matching Shiva Thapa's milestone from the Singapore 2010 Games. Ambekar trains at the National Institute of Sports in Patiala.
articles.description: Ambekar’s semifinal victory against the Colombian ended a 16-year wait for an Indian boxer in a Youth Olympics final, matching the milestone set by Shiva Thapa at the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games

articles.headline: US relocates military aircraft from British airbase over Iranian threat
articles.title: US moves aircraft from second UK base over ‘threat from Iran’
articles.summary: The United States military moved refuelling tankers from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England to Germany and other locations on November 9, 2026, following intelligence regarding a likely terrorist threat from Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal.
