Congressional sources indicate the resolution may pass the Republican-controlled House before Democrats take control on January 3, though Senate conviction appears unlikely. President Donald Trump and other officials have defended Hegseth, while critics warn his strained congressional relations could threaten future defence spending packages.
articles.description: U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday, setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power

articles.headline: Spain holds first general strike in fourteen years amid growing housing crisis
articles.title: Spain’s first general strike in 14 years brings clashing social and political desires to the fore
articles.summary: Millions of Spanish workers participated in a nationwide general strike on November 11, 2026, demanding government action against soaring housing costs shortly before an upcoming national election. Major unions including UGT and CCOO reported substantial work stoppages across strategic sectors such as transport, energy, and manufacturing. The labor protest follows widespread public anger over housing affordability and recent tenant evictions, while political analysts note the outcome could significantly influence Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's left-wing coalition and right-wing opposition parties.
articles.description: The two main unions calling for the strike, UGT and CCOO, reported widespread participation in the early hours “with significant work stoppages in strategic sectors”

articles.headline: Former YSRCP leader Vijayasai Reddy launches Parivartana Rajaneethi Party in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Vijayasai Reddy launches Parivartana Rajaneethi Party, vows to end ‘two-family’ politics in Andhra
articles.summary: Former Rajya Sabha member V. Vijayasai Reddy officially established the Parivartana Rajaneethi Party in Vijayawada on November 11, 2026, stating that the organization aims to dismantle the dominance of two political families in Andhra Pradesh. During the launch event, the founder announced that his new political outfit intends to contest all one hundred seventy-five Assembly constituencies across the state. He emphasized nurturing grassroots youth leadership and providing opportunities for capable individuals from all social backgrounds to participate in governance.
articles.description: The former YSRCP leader says he will mentor young leaders as Bal Thackeray and Kanshi Ram did, and that his Parivartana Rajaneethi Party will contest all 175 Andhra Assembly seats

articles.headline: Kerala Police book over 25500 drunk driving cases and seek licence suspensions
articles.title: Over 25,500 drunk driving cases booked in Keralam since October 13; police to seek licence cancellation for repeat offenders
articles.summary: Authorities in Keralam registered 25,594 drunk driving cases since October 13, prompting the police to recommend driving licence suspensions for first-time offenders and cancellations for repeat violators. Additional Director General of Police P. Vijayan stated that the crackdown has been extended to rural areas to prevent motorists from evading surveillance. The enforcement campaign also targets reckless driving and juvenile motorists to improve overall road safety across the State.
articles.description: Kerala Police to seek licence suspension for first-time offenders. Move as part of intensified crackdown on drunk and reckless driving launched in the wake of Nedumbassery accident that killed three youths

articles.headline: Indian stock markets surge in early trade led by foreign fund inflows
articles.title: Stock markets hit eight-month high as foreign investors return
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rallied sharply in early trade on November 11, 2026, driven by foreign institutional investor inflows and positive corporate results. The BSE Sensex jumped 1,097 points to reach 82,186.92, while the NSE Nifty gained 274 points. Analysts noted that moderating Brent crude oil prices at $92.44 per barrel provided additional macro relief for the domestic market.
articles.description: The Nifty ⁠50 and Sensex have soared 10% and 10.5%, respectively, so far in November, on track for their best month since November 2020 and outperforming emerging ​market peers

articles.headline: Russell Brand sentenced to 10.5 years over sexual assault charges
articles.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10.5 years over sexual assault charges
articles.description: Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being convicted of raping one woman

articles.headline: Steel plant explosion in western Turkiye kills at least 16 people
articles.title: Explosion at Turkish steel plant kills at least 16 people
articles.summary: An industrial explosion at the HABAS factory in Aliaga, located north of Izmir, killed at least 16 individuals and injured 13 others. The incident occurred when an overhead crane fell into a large furnace during boiler replacement operations. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced an ongoing government investigation into the disaster, while local labour representatives and eyewitnesses highlighted prior safety concerns and maintenance issues at the steel facility.
articles.description: President Erdogan announces an investigation after a crane collapsed into a furnace, triggering the blast near Izmir.

articles.headline: Nvidia shares fall following investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang
articles.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: Nvidia shares tumbled six percent on Monday, wiping out hundreds of billions of dollars in market value after the United States chipmaker announced an independent investigation into chief executive Jensen Huang. The probe follows reports that Beijing targeted Huang in an espionage campaign through Alice Huang, which China denied. Huang admitted infidelity, and analysts suggested the financial hit to the artificial intelligence hardware leader would be brief.
articles.description: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.

articles.headline: Himalayas agenda omitted from formal COP31 list
articles.title: Himalayas agenda left off COP31 formal list as major blocs withhold support: Nepal Foreign Minister
articles.summary: An agenda item focused on the Himalayas proposed by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan was excluded from the formal list of the thirty-first United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya. Nepali Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal stated that developed nations withheld support during negotiations. The conference, hosted in Turkiye under Environment Minister Murat Kurum, runs until November 20, 2026.
articles.description: Nepal's Minister of Foreign Affairs, said that the three countries would continue to face challenges in getting the issue formally recognised without the support of major countries

articles.headline: How is Gaza coping with another severe winter?
articles.title: How is Gaza coping with another severe winter?
articles.description: How is Gaza coping with another severe winter?

articles.headline: Yogi Adityanath defends Deepavali firecracker use and dismisses pollution concerns in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Yogi Adityanath dismisses Deepavali pollution concerns, says it will subside
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath defended the bursting of firecrackers during Deepavali, stating that festival celebrations should remain unrestricted while dismissing environmental concerns. Speaking in Lucknow on November 11, 2026, he argued that pollution would subside and accused critics of ignoring corruption. During the same government program, he also discussed upcoming employment appointment letter distributions scheduled through January.
articles.description: Nobody says anything to those who polluted the entire system with their corrupt misdeeds. But if the public burst crackers one day, it created pollution, the CM said

articles.headline: Bengaluru police recover all seven bodies in family murder case
articles.title: Bengaluru family murders: All seven bodies recovered
articles.summary: Karnataka police recovered the final two bodies from Shiradi Ghat, completing the recovery of all seven victims in a family murder case. Authorities previously detained Indushekhar and his minor daughter following a missing person complaint filed on November 5. The accused confessed that marital discord and humiliation prompted the killings, and families plan to conduct joint funeral rites.
articles.description: The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.

articles.headline: United States warns Madagascar against expanding military cooperation with Russia
articles.title: US warns Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia
articles.summary: The United States Africa Command warned Madagascar against deepening military ties with Russia, cautioning that partnerships mirroring the Sahel model risk worsening instability. Lieutenant General John Brennan noted that Madagascar occupies a vital geopolitical position along the Mozambique Channel. Despite the warning, Malagasy President Michaël Randrianirina recently signed multiple cooperation agreements with Moscow following a visit earlier in the year.
articles.description: US general warns the Sahel model-like security deal with Russia could lead to greater instability in Africa.

articles.headline: CII Partnership Summit begins in Visakhapatnam
articles.title: CII Partnership Summit begins in Visakhapatnam on November 12; Amit Shah to address inaugural session
articles.summary: The thirty-first Confederation of Indian Industry Partnership Summit opened on November 12, 2026, in Visakhapatnam. Jointly organised by the Government of India and Andhra Pradesh alongside industry bodies, the economic forum brings together over 3,800 delegates from nearly 59 countries. Union Minister Amit Shah addressed the inaugural session, while Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and various international ministers participate in discussions spanning technology, trade and sustainability.
articles.description: Over 3,800 delegates from 59 countries are expected at the two-day summit, with more than 160 MoUs lined up

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to launch new Vande Bharat service
articles.title: PM Modi and Railway Minister to flag off Bengaluru–Mangaluru–Goa Vande Bharat Express on November 13
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will inaugurate the Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express on November 13, 2026, with regular services beginning November 15. Operating with 16-car rakes and twelve halts, the route will become the longest and slowest Vande Bharat chair car service in India. The Railway Ministry will simultaneously discontinue the existing Mangaluru Central-Madgaon service.
articles.description: While Narendra Modi flags off the much awaited service from Bengaluru, Ashwini Vaishnaw will do it from Mangaluru Junction

articles.headline: Cyberattacks target connected supermarket fridges and critical infrastructure across Europe
articles.title: If hackers can take over a supermarket fridge, what else is at risk?
articles.summary: Hackers targeted internet-connected supermarket refrigerators across Europe using basic security failures such as exposed equipment and weak passwords. Attackers heated French units and affected businesses in nine countries. Officials warned that similar vulnerabilities threaten vital sectors like healthcare, water systems, and power plants, raising urgent concerns about the security of connected devices globally.
articles.description: As our lives become more digitised, we show which smart systems can be hacked and how to protect yourself.

articles.headline: India ranks 176th in environmental performance index on air quality
articles.title: India’s efforts to clean its air need not slow its economic growth
articles.summary: India placed 176 out of 177 countries in the 2026 Environmental Performance Index published by Yale and Columbia Universities in the United States. Assessing 47 indicators, the index revealed India performed worst on air quality at 175, despite ranking 88 on air pollution, highlighting that controlling select emissions does not automatically improve the health burden from breathable air.
articles.description: The best interventions must address air pollution while supporting development priorities. Cleaner industrial processes may reduce emissions while improving efficiency. Clean cooking can reduce household smoke while improving convenience and health. Better waste management can reduce open burning while improving urban services

articles.headline: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
articles.title: Millions fill Buenos Aires streets to welcome Pope Leo XIV
articles.description: The Pope celebrated an outdoor Mass in Argentina's capital, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, just three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

articles.headline: President Donald Trump questions integrity of US midterm elections
articles.title: Trump reverses stance, alleges fraud in recent US midterm elections
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump questioned the integrity of recent midterm elections on Truth Social, reversing his earlier acceptance of Democratic victories and congressional majorities. Trump alleged that pre-election polls were inaccurate and that early voting counts prevented Republican wins, though he provided no evidence of fraud. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer and various Republican figures responded critically to the president's renewed election denialism statements.
articles.description: Democratic Senate leader Schumer criticises Trump's poll denialism, calling it an avoidable return to baseless claims.

articles.headline: Canada has not decided on lifting Arctic drilling ban, says Mark Carney
articles.title: Canada has not made a decision about lifting Arctic drilling ban, says Mark Carney
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated on Tuesday that his government has not decided to lift the decade-long moratorium on offshore oil and gas exploration in the Arctic. The clarification followed recent federal budget funding aimed at supporting Inuit leadership governance. The original drilling ban was established in 2016 to protect the fragile marine ecosystem.
articles.description: The Toronto Star reported that Mr. Carney’s government is considering lifting the ban on oil and gas activities in the Arctic, quoting a Department of Finance official

articles.headline: Indian Prime Minister Modi discusses bilateral relations with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy
articles.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke on Monday with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy regarding the ongoing conflict and bilateral ties between Delhi and Kyiv. During the telephone call, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments. Prime Minister Modi reaffirmed India's human-centric approach, emphasized dialogue and diplomacy, and conveyed India's readiness to contribute to a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
articles.description: India is ready to mediate to establish grain safety agreement for “food corridors”, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy

articles.headline: BJP wins 77 Tripura civic body seats unopposed
articles.title: BJP wins 77 seats of five Tripura civic bodies unopposed; elections for rest on November 27
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party secured 77 seats across five civic bodies in Tripura without contest following nomination scrutiny. State Election Commissioner P.K. Chakravarty announced that remaining elections for 268 seats will take place on November 27, involving 810 candidates from parties including the Communist Party of India Marxist and the Congress, with vote counting scheduled for December 3.
articles.description: Now, the voting will be held in 268 seats, which are set to witness a triangular fight among the BJP-led NDA, CPI(M) and the Congress

articles.headline: Man arrested in Chhattisgarh for killing four-year-old to sell organs
articles.title: Man kills 4-year-old to sell his organs after watching video on making money quickly
articles.summary: Basudev Korwa was arrested in Jashpur for allegedly murdering his four-year-old relative to sell his organs after watching an online video. According to Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police Lal Umed Singh, the agricultural labourer used an artificial intelligence assistant in a chatting app to find methods for making money quickly. Villagers discovered the victim's body after the boy's father filed a missing person complaint.
articles.description: 27-year-old Basudev Korwa from Chhattisgarh is accused of having murdered his cousin’s son and extracting the boy’s organs, which he allegedly kept in a plastic bag

articles.headline: Usman Khawaja withdraws from book promotional interviews
articles.title: Khawaja withdraws from book interviews amid Sandpapergate row; ACA urges end to online abuse
articles.summary: Cricketer Usman Khawaja cancelled book promotional appearances following intense public backlash over claims in his autobiography regarding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Meanwhile, Australian Cricketers Association chief executive Paul Marsh urged an end to online abuse directed at players. The publication alleges widespread team knowledge of the incident, drawing varied responses from former teammates and publishers.
articles.description: Usman Khawaja claimed that then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft were made scapegoats by cricket administrators

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi schedules university discussions in United States
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi to discuss global student movements at Columbia University; geopolitics at Chicago University
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi will participate in fireside chats at Columbia University and the University of Chicago during a visit to the United States next week. Indian Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda confirmed the engagements covering global student movements and geopolitics, while also announcing the upcoming Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14.
articles.description: Slamming the BJP for its repeated attack on Mr. Gandhi, Mr. Pitroda said it was a “bogus” argument as it is “not a question of criticising anybody, it's a question of showing facts as you see it”

articles.headline: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta ends operations citing government pressure
articles.title: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes citing gov’t clampdown
articles.summary: Russian investigative outlet Novaya Gazeta ended operations due to state pressure, holding its final editorial meeting on Monday. Labeled a foreign agent last September, the publication struggled after banks halted reader donations. Cofounder Dmitry Muratov criticized the closure in Moscow, while the Kremlin described it as a normal change. United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk called the shutdown a devastating blow to independent media.
articles.description: The paper was one of the few remaining outlets in Russia that criticised Moscow's war on Ukraine.

articles.headline: Mother Dairy raises milk prices by two to four rupees per litre
articles.title: Mother Dairy raises milk prices by ₹2-4 per litre, effective November 12
articles.summary: Mother Dairy has increased consumer prices for its liquid milk variants by two to four rupees per litre, effective November 12, 2026, due to rising procurement costs from farmers. The price adjustments affect the Delhi-National Capital Region market, where toned milk, full cream milk, double toned milk, and cow milk have all seen price hikes. The company operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board.
articles.description: Mother Dairy, the largest milk supplier in Delhi-NCR, had last raised prices on May 14, 2026. Prior to that, the price revision was done in April, 2025

articles.headline: Krakow shooting suspect dies as Poland mourns six victims
articles.title: Krakow shooting suspect dies as Poland mourns six victims
articles.description: A 24-year-old man who killed six people and wounded 15 in a shooting in Krakow, has died in hospital.

articles.headline: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
articles.title: Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction
articles.description: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.

articles.headline: Ladakh administration announces upcoming hill council, panchayat and municipal elections
articles.title: Why Ladakh polls announcement fails to cut ice with protesting civil society groups | Explained
articles.summary: The Lieutenant Governor-led administration of Ladakh has announced three-tier local elections across the Union Territory, with panchayat and municipal polls slated for November 21 and hill council elections scheduled for December 4. These upcoming polls provide critical platforms for public representatives in the region. However, the short timeline established by the State Election Commission creates difficulties for political parties to campaign and form alliances.
articles.description: LAB and KDA are demanding postponement of hill council elections to April-May next year, citing unfavourable winter timing and lack of consultation

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Deadly aftermath of Gaza rainstorm continues
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Deadly aftermath of Gaza rainstorm continues
articles.description: Five Palestinians were killed in Gaza when heavy rain collapsed a sand embankment on a displacement camp.

articles.headline: Olympic swimming champion Tatjana Smith switches national allegiance to Netherlands
articles.title: South African swimmer Tatjana Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
articles.summary: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympic athlete, announced she will swim for the Netherlands, citing financial and practical challenges. The two-time Olympic champion, who holds dual citizenship, aims to target the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics with greater high-performance support. Smith won gold medals at the Tokyo and Paris Olympic Games and retired before announcing a competitive comeback two months prior to her announcement.
articles.description: Double Olympic gold medallist cites 'financial and practical challenges' of swimming.

articles.headline: Donald Trump questions midterm election integrity despite previous acceptance
articles.title: Trump questions midterm elections integrity after previously accepting results
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump questioned the legitimacy of midterm elections in which Republicans suffered sweeping losses, contradicting earlier remarks that he would accept the outcome. Writing on Truth Social, Trump cited vague claims about voting processes. Democrats secured majorities in both the Senate and the House while state and local officials reported problem-free voting.
articles.description: Trump made the claims, without evidence, on Truth Social on Monday.

articles.headline: Four-year-old girl raped in Goa with suspect arrested by police
articles.title: 4-year-old girl raped in Goa; Bihar native arrested, 2nd such case in a week
articles.summary: A man in his mid-20s from Bihar was arrested after allegedly raping a four-year-old girl on November 10, 2026, in Shristhal village in Canacona taluka, according to Goa police. This marks the second incident involving a minor in the coastal state within a week, following an unresovled case in Mapusa town. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant stated that perpetrators of such crimes will remain behind bars permanently.
articles.description: The incident occurred late night on November 10 at Shristhal village in Canacona taluka of Kushavati district, a senior police officer told PTI

articles.headline: Jamaica files reparations petition to King Charles III over slavery
articles.title: Why Jamaica’s reparations petition has a solid legal basis
articles.summary: Led by Culture Minister Olivia Grange, the Jamaican government filed a formal petition on September 7, 2026, asking King Charles III to refer three legal questions regarding transatlantic slavery to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. The move matters because it challenges U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's stance that contemporary Britons bear no liability for historical wrongs.
articles.description: The petition asks whether the enslavement of Africans in Jamaica violated international law

articles.headline: Sairang-Kolkata Express train derails in Assam with no reported injuries
articles.title: Several coaches of Sairang-Kolkata Express train derail at Digaru in Assam
articles.summary: Several coaches of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at Digaru railway station in Assam on November 11, 2026, after the locomotive pilot failed to control the train speed. Northeast Frontier Railway reported that all passengers are safe without any injuries. Relief operations are underway, and stranded passengers are being transported to their destinations by an alternate train.
articles.description: No injuries reported so far; loco pilot failed to control train’s speed while giving precedence to another train, authorities said

articles.headline: French government moves planned minimum wage increase forward to quell protests
articles.title: France accelerates minimum wage hike in bid to quell protest
articles.summary: The French government announced it will move a planned 1.6 percent minimum wage increase forward by a month to December 1, 2026, aiming to quell ongoing protests over the cost of living. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu detailed the hike during a press conference on Monday. The adjustment raises the monthly minimum wage by 24 euros to 1,502 euros, though major labor unions dismissed the measure as insufficient.
articles.description: Unions slam the increase as insufficient, as the government seeks to defuse the unrest ahead of upcoming elections.

articles.headline: Tech consultant sentenced to 16 years to life for killing Cash App founder
articles.title: Tech consultant sentenced to 16 years to life in stabbing death of Cash App founder Bob Lee
articles.summary: Nima Momeni was sentenced in San Francisco on November 10, 2026, to 16 years to life in prison for the second-degree murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee. A jury rejected the defendant claims of self-defense regarding the April 4, 2023, stabbing. Superior Court Judge Alexandra Gordon denied a request for a new trial before handing down the sentence.
articles.description: A jury in December 2024 found Nima Momeni guilty of second-degree murder, rejecting the defendant's claim that he had acted in self-defense

articles.headline: Spain protesters strike nationwide amid acute housing affordability crisis
articles.title: ‘I pay $500 for 5 square metres’: Spain’s protesters, in their own words
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of young residents participated in nationwide strikes across Spain to protest skyrocketing rental costs and severe property shortages. The demonstrations followed public outrage over the eviction of an elderly tenant in Madrid. Meanwhile, the Bank of Spain warned of a massive housing deficit. Citizens shared personal struggles with high rent burdens and insecure short-term housing contracts.
articles.description: Young people are stuck in the family home or forced into cramped, overpriced rentals with little security or control.

articles.headline: IBM ends U.S. visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
articles.title: IBM to end U.S. visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in its Consulting arm
articles.summary: International Business Machines Corporation announced on November 10, 2026, that it will terminate United States visa and green card sponsorships for the majority of positions within its consulting division. The decision impacts a unit with over 150,000 workers and follows increased scrutiny of foreign technology hiring by the administration of United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Workers impacted by the move can work with IBM ‌outside the U.S. or leave by the ​end of the year, a report said

articles.headline: Malaysia’s ex-PM transferred to house arrest for 1MDB graft sentence
articles.title: Malaysia’s ex-PM transferred to house arrest for 1MDB graft sentence
articles.description: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak has been transferred from prison to his Kuala Lumpur home for house arrest.

articles.headline: Liberia-flagged oil tanker hit by projectile in Persian Gulf carrying Indians
articles.title: Liberia-flagged VLCC hit in Persian Gulf, six Indian seafarers aboard: Sarbananda Sonowal
articles.summary: A Liberia-flagged very large crude carrier named MT Fujairah Energy was struck by a projectile in the Persian Gulf while traveling from Al Ruwais to Dubai on November 10, 2026. Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal stated four crew members were injured, including one Indian national with minor injuries who was brought ashore. The remaining 18 crew members, including five other Indian seafarers, are safe.
articles.description: Mr. Sonowal said four crew members sustained injuries in the attack, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and has been safely taken ashore

articles.headline: Gunmen abduct three polio workers in northwestern Pakistan
articles.title: Three polio workers abducted during vaccination campaign in northwestern Pakistan
articles.summary: Unidentified armed men abducted three polio vaccination workers during an immunisation campaign in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Police identified the victims and stated they were taken from Tank district to an undisclosed location. The incident follows a series of recent abductions and attacks targeting polio teams and security personnel across the region, raising serious security concerns.
articles.description: The gunmen took the three workers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district to an undisclosed location after abducting them. The abducted workers were identified as Mir Janan, Ikram and Khanzala, says police

articles.headline: India wins 25m pistol team gold as shooters miss Olympic quota
articles.title: India clinches 25m pistol team gold medal; Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh miss Olympic quota
articles.summary: India claimed the women 25-meter pistol team gold medal on November 10, 2026, at the International Shooting Sport Federation World Championships in Doha, Qatar. Team members Esha Singh and Manu Bhaker failed to secure individual podium finishes or quota places for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, as South Korea shooter Yang Jiin won gold with a world record score.
articles.description: India have so far secured just one Olympic quota place through men's 10m air pistol shooter Jaypal Malviya

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls resumption of war with Iran highly unlikely
articles.title: Trump says resumption of war with Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that renewed fighting with Iran is highly unlikely as long as peace talks progress. Speaking to CNN, Trump indicated that military actions depend on whether Tehran signs a strong agreement. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi previously suggested that negotiations have paused while assessing the impact of recent United States midterm election results.
articles.description: Iran continues to at least partly block traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which has dented oil supplies out of the Gulf.

articles.headline: Researchers publish global study examining subjective human experiences of physical pain
articles.title: Physical pain often peaks during your working years, not in old age
articles.summary: Researchers gathered subjective pain data from 6.1 million individuals across 118 countries between 1995 and 2005 to address a major gap in the Global Burden of Diseases study. Matthew Fillingim, a researcher at McGill University in Canada, and 98 colleagues from 63 institutions published their findings in Nature Medicine to highlight pain as a leading cause of disability.
articles.description: A large new study has also found that people’s pain levels varied according to their income, geography, conditions like obesity, and habits like smoking

articles.headline: At least 34 migrants die after Europe-bound boat sinks off Senegal
articles.title: At least 39 die after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
articles.summary: At least thirty-four people died when a wooden migrant boat capsized between Dakar and Saint-Louis while heading toward Spain's Canary Islands, according to the Senegalese Press Agency citing an official source. The interior ministry reported one rescue and ongoing search operations. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye pledged to intensify efforts against smuggling networks amid high youth unemployment.
articles.description: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life

articles.headline: OpenAI reports rising quarterly revenue alongside widening operating losses
articles.title: OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion: Report
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm OpenAI disclosed a revenue increase to $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, according to the Wall Street Journal. Documents reviewed by the newspaper indicate operating losses expanded to $10.9 billion. The financial details arrive as rival Anthropic prepares for an initial public offering, highlighting investor interest in the artificial intelligence sector despite ongoing profitability concerns.
articles.description: OpenAI told investors ‌its adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150% in ‌the prior quarter,

articles.headline: Netanyahu heckled by Bennett at Knesset opening session
articles.title: Netanyahu heckled by Bennett at Knesset opening session
articles.description: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett repeatedly heckled caretaker PM Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.headline: Houthi authorities report forty-four deaths from airstrikes near Sanaa
articles.title: Houthi rebels say at least 44 killed in airstrike near Yemeni capital
articles.summary: Airstrikes hitting homes in the village of al-Shariya near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, killed forty-four people, mostly women and children, according to Houthi health authorities on November 8, 2026. The attacks wounded forty others, including children and women. Anees al-Asbahi, spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, blamed Saudi Arabia for the strikes amid an escalation in the civil war.
articles.description: Al-Asbahi said rescue teams were still searching the area for missing people, raising fears that the death toll could rise.

articles.headline: Border clashes in Ethiopia displace more than fifty thousand people
articles.title: More than 50,000 displaced by deadly Ethiopia border clashes
articles.summary: Fighting rooted in a dispute over land and administrative control between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations has displaced over fifty thousand people. A government-led assessment and Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan confirmed the rising numbers as refugees crossed into Kenya. The conflict sparked tensions over flag displays in Moyale, leading to urgent humanitarian needs.
articles.description: Families arrive in Kenya with little food or shelter as host communities struggle to cope.

articles.headline: Kennedy family sues to halt construction of presidential monument
articles.title: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, arguing it would cast shadow on JFK's grave
articles.summary: Nine relatives of former President John F Kennedy filed a legal complaint to block United States President Donald Trump from building a memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia. The plaintiffs contend the structure would cast shadows over historical gravesites. United States District Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered a 14-day pause on construction while litigation proceeds following approvals granted by federal agencies.
articles.description: Nine members of the political dynasty say the 250ft structure would cast a shadow on gravesites.

articles.headline: CENTCOM announces Task Force Iron Gate to target Iranian supply networks
articles.title: Trump says Iran is sealed off. But can new US task force stop weapons flow?
articles.summary: United States Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate to prevent Iran from using land routes and the Caspian Sea to transport advanced weapons. Analysts warn the intelligence unit cannot seal borders without regional cooperation and risks widening the conflict. President Donald Trump claimed the unit and naval blockades had effectively sealed off Iran from the world.
articles.description: Analysts say a small intelligence-focused unit cannot seal Iran’s borders, and others warn it could expand the war.

articles.headline: Kennedy relatives join lawsuits attempting to block presidential arch
articles.title: Kennedy family joins US lawsuits to block Trump’s ‘unlawful’ arch plan
articles.summary: Members of the Kennedy family joined legal challenges seeking to stop United States President Donald Trump from constructing a granite arch in Washington, DC. The plaintiffs argue the project damages sightlines at Arlington National Cemetery. United States District Judge Tanya Chutkan halted ground preparation for 14 days, while representatives state the structure was authorised without required congressional approval.
articles.description: Kennedy dynasty has filed a motion to stop Trump's arch from obscuring JFK Eternal Flame and family gravesites.

articles.headline: IRGC strikes three tankers near Hormuz over ‘US links’
articles.title: IRGC strikes three tankers near Hormuz over ‘US links’
articles.description: An oil tanker caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz after Iran’s IRGC said it had struck three tankers on Sunday,

articles.headline: Bus crash in South Korea injures dozens of people
articles.title: Dozens injured in South Korea after bus crashes into 32 vehicles
articles.summary: A commuter bus collided with 32 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour in Seongnam, South Korea, injuring at least 57 people. Gyeonggi Province fire officials reported nine victims suffered serious injuries. Police questioned the driver, who tested negative for alcohol and attributed the collision on November 11, 2026, to brake failure.
articles.description: The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said

articles.headline: London court sentences Russell Brand to prison for sexual offenses
articles.title: UK court hands comedian Russell Brand 10.5 years for rape, sexual assault
articles.summary: London's Southwark Crown Court sentenced British comedian Russell Brand to ten years and six months in prison on November 9, 2026. Judge Joel Bennathan condemned the fifty-one-year-old actor as a sexual predator for attacks against four women between 2004 and 2009. Defense lawyers argued Brand is a changed person, while police confirmed he remains under investigation for other allegations.
articles.description: Brand was convicted last week of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three more between 2004 ​and 2009.

articles.headline: Iran maintains war demands despite United States military pressure and strikes
articles.title: Iran stands by demands to end the war as US ramps up military pressure
articles.summary: Iranian officials reported additional United States strikes on Qeshm island on Monday while insisting that the military pressure will not alter demands to end the conflict. Ahmad Nafisi confirmed the southern island was targeted without infrastructure damage. Meanwhile, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected criticism of Tehran's seven-point peace plan from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, as mediators continue efforts to prevent escalation.
articles.description: Talks aimed at preventing new major fighting between the US and Iran are ongoing.

articles.headline: Delegations from Ukraine, Russia and United States gather for Abu Dhabi talks
articles.title: ‘No concession’: What to expect from Russia-US-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Representatives from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are convening in Abu Dhabi for trilateral negotiations scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday to address the ongoing war. Analysts remain skeptical about achieving substantial breakthroughs given President Vladimir Putin's firm stance and territorial demands. The discussions involve senior officials including US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov, and Russian envoy Vladimir Medinsky.
articles.description: A fourth round of peace talks in 2026 takes place this week, with security guarantees high on the agenda.

articles.headline: Protesters throw milk at Joe Biden during Hunter event in Dublin
articles.title: Protesters throw milk at Joe Biden during Hunter event in Dublin
articles.description: Pro-Palestinian protesters hurled milk towards Joe Biden in Ireland over his support for Israel.

articles.headline: Former Iraqi lawmaker Ahmed al-Alwani found dead in Beirut apartment
articles.title: Former Iraqi lawmaker Ahmed al-Alwani found dead in Beirut
articles.summary: Former Iraqi lawmaker Ahmed al-Alwani was found dead in a Beirut apartment on Tuesday, with Lebanese authorities investigating his death as a killing. According to a judicial source, preliminary findings indicate he was strangled, and one suspect has been arrested while two others remain at large. Al-Alwani was recently released under an amnesty law.
articles.description: Lebanese authorities investigate the killing after al-Alwani's body is found in an apartment in Beirut.

articles.headline: Citizens collective alleges millions of missing voters in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Over 74 lakh voters missing from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls, says citizens’ collective
articles.summary: The Independent Young Citizens Collective alleged that over seventy-four lakh voters were removed from Tamil Nadu electoral rolls during a revision exercise. Activists demanded an inquiry, the scrapping of the exercise, and the restoration of eligible voters ahead of upcoming elections, while criticizing the heavy administrative burden placed on citizens.
articles.description: The collective has announced a rally on Anna Salai on November 26, as part of a nationwide day of action against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls

articles.headline: Supreme Court reaffirms office memorandum on OBC non-creamy layer
articles.title: Explained | What did the Supreme Court clarify on the OBC creamy layer?
articles.summary: The Supreme Court reaffirmed a March judgment upholding a 1993 memorandum that excludes parental salary and agricultural income from wealth tests determining status. The central government subsequently sought legal clarity regarding how this ruling affects candidate claims from civil services examinations. The decision directly impacts how authorities evaluate eligibility criteria for reserved category applicants across the nation.
articles.description: Can parental salary alone disqualify a candidate from claiming OBC reservation benefits? What role do the 1993 Office Memorandum and the 2004 clarification play in determining creamy-layer status?

articles.headline: US citizen Mathew Van Dyke threatens to reveal incarceration details
articles.title: Van Dyke threatens to ‘reveal shocking details’ of his arrest, incarceration in India, blames Russia
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 10, 2026, that legal proceedings continue regarding United States citizen Mathew Van Dyke. Arrested on March 13, 2026, by the National Investigation Agency for unauthorized entry from Myanmar, Mr. Van Dyke was granted bail after six months in Tihar jail. He claimed his arrest resulted from Russian pressure and threatened to disclose details publicly.
articles.description: MEA declines comment, says courts still hearing case; Mr. Van Dyke was arrested in March along with six Ukrainians, who crossed from Myanmar to Mizoram after allegedly training ethnic armed groups there

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi writes in memoir that Pranab Mukherjee hinted at wanting prime ministership
articles.title: Pranab Mukherjee hinted at desire to become PM, ‘shocked’ me, writes Sonia Gandhi
articles.summary: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi revealed in her memoir that former President Pranab Mukherjee shocked her in 2010 by suggesting a change at the top, which she interpreted as a desire to become prime minister. Published by HarperCollins, the book also details her relationships with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Maneka Gandhi. Sharmistha Mukherjee defended her late father by stating that political ambition is not a crime.
articles.description: In her memoir, former Congress president recalls 2010 conversation; Pranab Mukherjee’s daughter Sharmistha asks what there was to be shocked about, says it is not a crime to be ambitious

articles.headline: India states travel document is needed for deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina
articles.title: After Bangladesh rules out passport for Hasina, India says ‘travel document’ needed
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs stated on November 10, 2026, that former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requires a travel document for international movement. This followed remarks by Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir rejecting passport issuance and demanding her extradition. Officials noted Ms. Hasina could be extradited using a Bangladeshi passport or an Emergency Certificate confirming her citizenship status.
articles.description: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal described the passport’s requirement for extradition as a “technical issue” and said, “Obviously, for the travel of people, you need a travel document”

articles.headline: Federal judge allows Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
articles.title: Judge allows Trump's $10bn defamation case against BBC to proceed
articles.summary: A federal judge in Florida permitted United States President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the BBC to move forward, while dismissing a secondary claim under state unfair trade practices law. The lawsuit centres on a documentary that edited together segments of a speech Trump gave before the 2021 Capitol riot. The BBC expressed surprise at the ruling but confirmed it will continue defending its position through the legal process.
articles.description: But the court dismisses the other part of Trump's lawsuit that alleged the BBC had violated a Florida law.

articles.headline: Donald Trump meets Qatari Prime Minister as regional conflict continues
articles.title: Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end war
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Vice President J. D. Vance scheduled talks with Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani in Washington on November 9, 2026, to discuss ending the ongoing conflict with Iran. Despite diplomatic engagements following recent midterm elections, senior officials from the United States and the United Arab Emirates expressed skepticism regarding any imminent comprehensive resolution.
articles.description: Mutual attacks continue, with the U.S. striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and ‌Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi details political journey and family tragedies in new memoir
articles.title: 'They will kill you too': Sonia Gandhi's turbulent journey in Indian politics
articles.summary: Sonia Gandhi reflects on her life in Indian politics, the assassinations of her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi and her husband Rajiv Gandhi, and her eventual decision to lead the Congress party. In her new memoir, she details the profound personal grief, security fears, and political pressures that shaped her contentious rise to prominence.
articles.description: Sonia Gandhi's memoir revisits love, loss and political inheritance, offering a deeply personal defence of her family and its legacy.

articles.headline: Greta Thunberg criticizes COP31 climate summit as hypocritical in Turkey
articles.title: ‘Everything and everyone we love is at stake’: Thunberg slams COP31 talks
articles.summary: Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg condemned United Nations climate talks as hypocritical during her arrival at the COP31 conference in Antalya on Tuesday. Speaking ahead of the summit ending on November 20, she warned that economic and political systems are incompatible with human nature and that everyone is at risk from climate disasters. Youth activists welcomed her presence to push for meaningful change.
articles.description: Climate activist urges world leaders to put people and planet before profit as she arrives at UN climate talks.

articles.headline: Kenya prepares for potential severe flooding driven by El Niño
articles.title: 'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted
articles.summary: Kenyan residents in informal settlements like Kibera fear deadly flooding as the country braces for a potentially record-breaking El Ni�o event. Officials warn up to 900,000 people could be displaced, while drainage rehabilitation projects and relief preparations remain constrained by funding shortages. Meteorological experts report that ocean temperature patterns closely mirror the devastating 1997-1998 season.
articles.description: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could be one of the strongest on record, with heavy rain and flooding in Kenya.

articles.headline: Escitalopram outperforms other antidepressants in preventing patient relapse during analysis
articles.title: Antidepressant escitalopram more effective at preventing relapse, analysis finds
articles.summary: An analysis published in The Lancet Psychiatry examined nearly 10,000 patients and found that the antidepressant escitalopram was most effective at preventing relapse over a period of up to a year. Agomelatine and duloxetine ranked next, while fluoxetine ranked just below. Experts emphasized that the differences are modest and patients should consult doctors regarding individual factors before changing any treatments.
articles.description: Three pills came top and outperformed Prozac for preventing relapse in a large number of patients.

articles.headline: Twenty-one migrants and refugees die attempting to reach Crete
articles.title: At least 21 migrants and refugees die trying to reach Greece’s Crete
articles.summary: At least twenty-one individuals lost their lives attempting to reach the Greek island of Crete in separate maritime incidents. The Greek coastguard reported recovering twelve bodies and rescuing eighteen survivors from a vessel on November 9, 2026, while another operation on November 7 recovered eight bodies and saved twenty-eight people with assistance from European Union border agency Frontex aircraft.
articles.description: Greece's coastguard said more than 100 people rescued in several operations off the southern coast of Crete.

articles.headline: Iranian authorities contain fire on offshore South Pars gas platform
articles.title: Fire contained on platform in Iran’s South Pars gas field
articles.summary: Iranian authorities successfully extinguished a fire that erupted on Tuesday at a platform in Phase 14 of the South Pars gas field. Seventeen workers jumped into the sea during the incident and were later confirmed to be safe aboard rescue craft. Officials are investigating a potential gas leak or operational mishap as the cause of the emergency.
articles.description: Officials are considering a gas leak or an operational mishap as possible causes of the fire, Fars news agency said.

articles.headline: British police arrest US Army soldier in Gloucestershire for espionage
articles.title: U.S. Army member arrested in U.K. for alleged Russian links
articles.summary: British authorities arrested a 41-year-old unnamed United States Army member in Gloucestershire on Tuesday over allegations of spying for Russia. The soldier was stationed at Imjin Barracks, headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel stated that the bureau has zero tolerance for actions endangering national security.
articles.description: The U.K. authorities said the investigation was not linked to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations

articles.headline: Massive fire as Israeli settlers burn down business near Nablus
articles.title: Massive fire as Israeli settlers burn down business near Nablus
articles.description: Israeli settlers have set fire to Palestinian property in the village of Luban ash-Sharqiya, near Nablus.

articles.headline: Russia hits power stations in Ukraine, vessel in Black Sea
articles.title: Russia hits power stations in Ukraine, vessel in Black Sea
articles.description: Russia’s armed forces struck three Ukrainian power substations overnight.

articles.headline: French far-right figure Eric Zemmour announces 2027 presidential bid
articles.title: French far-right author Zemmour launches second bid for 2027 presidency
articles.summary: French far-right author Eric Zemmour announced on television that he will run in the April 2027 presidential election to maintain French national identity. The 68-year-old candidate pledged to reduce immigration and deport foreign offenders or long-term unemployed residents. He joins a crowded field that includes frontrunner Marine Le Pen and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon.
articles.description: Zemmour seeks to expel 'foreign unemployed people' after last month's violent protests.

articles.headline: World Meteorological Organization projects 2026 among four warmest years
articles.title: 2026 to be one of four warmest years on record: World Meteorological Organization
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization released a report on November 9, 2026, at the COP31 climate meeting in Antalya indicating that 2026 will rank among the four warmest years recorded. Global average temperatures between January and September surpassed pre-industrial levels by 1.47 degrees Celsius, driven by rising greenhouse gas concentrations and an intensifying El Nino weather pattern expected to persist into 2027.
articles.description: The key reason behind the rising global temperatures is that the Earth’s energy imbalance is rising, and the earth system is accumulating heat at an accelerating rate, said WMO

articles.headline: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Chisinau decision
articles.title: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move
articles.summary: Russia announced the expulsion of a Moldovan diplomat on Tuesday after summoning Ambassador Lilian Darii to lodge a protest. The decision mirrors Chisinau declaring a Russian embassy employee persona non grata following the discovery of drone debris containing explosives. Tensions between Moscow and Moldova have escalated amid a broader push by regional states to strengthen ties with the European Union.
articles.description: Relations between Moscow and Chisinau have worsened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

articles.headline: Tea industry stakeholders welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price
articles.title: Producers welcome proposal for minimum sustainable price for tea
articles.summary: Various industry associations on November 10, 2026, endorsed a Tea Board of India committee recommendation for a minimum sustainable price framework to bridge widening gaps between stagnant market realisations and rising production costs. Stakeholders including Dhunseri Tea and Industries chairman C. K Dhanuka stated that the policy will help accommodate wage revisions and secure long-term viability, while the Ministry of Commerce awaits a final decision.
articles.description: Tea Board of India has recommended a proposal to the Ministry of Commerce to implement minimum sustainable price (MSP) for tea. Several stake holders said that MSP is essential for long-term sustainability of the industry

articles.headline: Gallup poll shows death penalty support falls below fifty percent
articles.title: US poll shows death penalty lost majority support for first time since 1971
articles.summary: A Gallup survey released on Tuesday revealed that support for capital punishment in the United States dropped to 49 percent, marking the first time the practice lost majority support since 1971. The findings reflect decades of declining approval across age groups and political parties amid concerns regarding fairness and high costs. Twenty-seven states currently retain the death penalty despite shifting public sentiment.
articles.description: Support for capital punishment has been declining in the US for years over concerns about fairness and racial bias.

articles.headline: IBM's largest division ends most United States foreign worker sponsorships
articles.title: IBM’s biggest division ends most US foreign worker sponsorships
articles.summary: United States technology firm IBM confirmed on Tuesday that its consultancy division will discontinue sponsoring foreign worker visas and green cards for most positions. A company spokesperson told Reuters that reliance on high-skilled visa programmes had decreased alongside shifting client needs. The announcement follows increased pressure from the administration of President Donald Trump regarding the employment of foreign technology workers.
articles.description: Announcement follows Trump administration crackdown on visa programmes for skilled foreign workers.

articles.headline: Bihar Cabinet approves three percent DA hike for state employees and pensioners
articles.title: Bihar Cabinet hikes 3% DA for employees, pensioners
articles.summary: The Bihar Cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary approved a three percent increase in dearness allowance on November 10, 2026, raising it to sixty-three percent for employees and pensioners under the seventh pay commission. The decision adds a financial burden of one thousand eighty crore rupees to the state exchequer and introduces new welfare schemes for female students.
articles.description: The Cabinet approved the “Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme”, under which, 2,100 female students may be provided benefits beginning from the current financial year

articles.headline: Jharkhand Chief Minister recommends Central Bureau of Investigation probe into Nisha Bhagat death
articles.title: Hemant Soren recommends CBI probe into Nisha Bhagat’s death case
articles.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren recommended a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the death of tribal leader and social activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat on November 10, 2026. Bhagat died by suicide in Ranchi after posting a social media video criticizing state authorities. The decision follows protests by the Bharatiya Janata Party and demands from opposition leaders.
articles.description: Leader of the Opposition in Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on November 7 demanded a CBI investigation into the death of social activist Nisha Bhagat

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approves multiple policy frameworks to attract investments
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears policy frameworks to attract investments in AI, electronics, renewable energy
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu approved investment proposals and policy frameworks on November 10, 2026, to boost artificial intelligence, electronics, and renewable energy sectors. Major projects include an artificial intelligence data centre by AM Intelligence in Visakhapatnam and land allocations for industrial parks, aiming to drive regional development and employment.
articles.description: Directorate of Traffic Management and Road Safety to be set up at Mangalagiri; ₹31,387-crore green integrated AI data centre proposed by AM Intelligence at Amanam in Visakhapatnam district cleared

articles.headline: Analysts discuss fallout and political implications of the US midterm elections
articles.title: 2026 Midterms: Blue wave or anti-establishment backlash?
articles.summary: Guests Emma Vigeland and Olivia Troye joined host Josh Rushing to analyze the 2026 United States midterm elections and the decisive victories secured by the Democratic Party. The discussion explored whether the election results represented a definitive shift toward the Democratic Party or a broader public rejection of the existing political status quo.
articles.description: Emma Vigeland and Olivia Troye join Josh Rushing to discuss the fallout of the 2026 midterm elections.

articles.headline: White House awards funding to expand law enforcement resources in multiple cities
articles.title: White House announces funds for law enforcement programme in several cities
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump announced grants exceeding sixty million dollars each for St. Louis and Jackson to strengthen policing and prosecution under the Model Cities Initiative. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated the funding aims to combat violent crime, though the administration faces criticism from opponents over controversial federal law enforcement deployments.
articles.description: Trump administration awarded more than $60m each to St Louis, Missouri, and Jackson, Mississippi, in crime push.

articles.headline: Spanish royals join memorial service for victims of deadly train crash
articles.title: Spain's king and queen attend memorial service for rail crash victims
articles.summary: King Felipe and Queen Letizia joined mourners in Spain to honour the 69 people killed in a high-speed collision on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda. Archbishop Cerro Chaves led the Catholic Mass, which was attended by senior politicians including Transport Minister Carlos Cuerpo. The disaster remains under investigation while 28 survivors stay hospitalised and nationwide railway strikes protest safety conditions.
articles.description: Sixty-nine people died in the collision near Toledo two weeks ago and 28 are still in hospital.

articles.headline: Netanyahu and Eisenkot push for new government after election deadlock
articles.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot push for new government after election deadlock
articles.description: Netanyahu and Eisenkot push for new government after election deadlock

articles.headline: US poll shows majority of voters want Democrats to end Iran war
articles.title: US voters want Democrats focused on ending Iran war, lowering costs: Poll
articles.summary: A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on Tuesday revealed that seventy-one percent of Americans want congressional Democrats to pass legislation ending the war with Iran, while sixty-two percent support repealing tariffs enacted by President Donald Trump. Nine in ten respondents emphasized that addressing the cost of living should be the top priority during the first hundred days of the new term.
articles.description: Poll shows majority of Americans want Congress to prioritise addressing rising cost of living and economic challenges.

articles.headline: Ronaldo farewell marked by five-minute pre-recorded video on social media
articles.title: Ronaldo: prolific goal-scorer and a bona fide match-winner
articles.summary: The article discusses the quiet departure of Ronaldo, noting that there was no stadium farewell or public ovation. Instead, his exit was marked by a five-minute pre-recorded video released on social media, featuring a prepared speech and a nostalgic montage of memories rather than an in-person celebration under the stadium floodlights.
articles.description: The 41-year-old’s bitter fallout with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus pushed him into retirement from international football last week after a 23-year career. The manner of his exit and his dwindling impact in recent years shouldn’t detract from his status as the Iberian nation’s greatest footballer – he finishes with a record 234 appearances and 146 goals

articles.headline: US Senate advances bipartisan bill to accelerate energy infrastructure projects
articles.title: US Senate advances major bill boosting energy infrastructure
articles.summary: The United States Senate voted seventy-three to twenty-five on Monday to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which aims to overhaul permitting processes for energy projects and require data centres to cover power costs. Supported by President Donald Trump, the legislation promises billions in residential electricity savings while drawing strong opposition from environmental groups and incoming Democratic leaders.
articles.description: Rare bipartisan bill requires data centres to pay for infrastructure, but environmental groups say it falls short.

articles.headline: FDA orders GLP-1 weight-loss drug makers to add rare eye warnings
articles.title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
articles.summary: The United States Food and Drug Administration ordered manufacturers of weight-loss drugs including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound to include warnings about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a rare condition that can cause permanent blindness. While the agency concluded there is an increased risk, manufacturers such as Novo Nordisk stated the data do not definitively establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship.
articles.description: The US Food and Drug Administration says Ozempic, Wegovy, and other weight-loss drugs must have labels about the condition, known as NAION.

articles.headline: British author David Walliams faces accusations of grooming and sexual assault
articles.title: UK children’s author David Walliams accused of grooming minors
articles.summary: Multiple women accuse British author and comedian David Walliams of grooming and sexual misconduct in a joint investigation published by The Guardian newspaper and ITV News on Tuesday. Walliams denies the allegations through his legal representatives while acknowledging thoughtless behavior. Meanwhile, the BBC announced it is reviewing and removing his content from platforms following the publication.
articles.description: A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News details allegations made by multiple women against the 55-year-old.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone unit defends Slovyansk amid ongoing bombardment
articles.title: 'If I tell you to run, run': BBC joins a Ukrainian drone unit as it protects a front-line city
articles.summary: Members of a Ukrainian drone unit named Peaky Blinders are intercepting Russian drones in Slovyansk, one of four front-line cities forming a heavily reinforced defense belt in Donetsk. The heavily bombarded town is central to peace talks between Ukraine, Russia, and the United States in Abu Dhabi, where Russia seeks control of these strategic urban centers.
articles.description: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of its pre-war population remaining.

articles.headline: United States boycotts United Nations human rights review in Geneva
articles.title: Trump administration again boycotts UN human rights review
articles.summary: United States representatives skipped a United Nations examination of the American human rights record in Geneva, prompting the UN body to delay the review until January. The boycott, marking the second consecutive year Washington missed the evaluation, drew criticism from rights groups and experts who warned the absence damages the credibility of the council.
articles.description: UN Human Rights Council delays US human rights record examination until January after Washington refuses meeting.

articles.headline: Spain faces nationwide strike amid housing crisis and snap elections
articles.title: Spain braces for nationwide strike as anger over housing, costs boils over
articles.summary: Spain is bracing for a nationwide twenty-four-hour general strike called by major unions over soaring rents and living costs, disrupting transport and public services weeks before snap elections. The protest follows widespread anger over housing shortages and evictions, keeping the issue at the center of political debate as political parties clash over responsibility.
articles.description: The 24-hour walkout, called by Spain’s two biggest unions, is due to start on Wednesday.

articles.headline: UK court overturns colonial-era laws criminalising same-sex intimacy
articles.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
articles.summary: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago following an eleven-year legal battle brought by Jason Jones. The historic unanimous ruling determined the legislation violated individual privacy rights, ending laws that had carried harsh penalties based on colonial-era British statutes.
articles.description: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.

articles.headline: OpenAI introduces verified business agents for ChatGPT in the US
articles.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm OpenAI launched verified business agents in ChatGPT to help users with comparison shopping and brand inquiries. Available initially in beta for eligible United States e-commerce and online service businesses, these separate chats ensure authentic brand representation through verification via the Business Hub feature, according to company officials.
articles.description: ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified "Business Agents" that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to "eligible" e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in ChatGPT being announced today in beta. You […]

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh officials discuss making a father's name optional in official documents
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh weighs making father’s name optional in official documents
articles.summary: Government officials, child rights groups, and non-governmental organisations in Andhra Pradesh held a consultation on making a father's name optional in official records. Organised by the state child rights commission alongside groups like the Children India Foundation, the proposal aims to assist orphans, children of sex workers, and single parents. Participants emphasised examining legal implications to ensure educational and employment opportunities are not hindered.
articles.description: State consultation calls for a child-friendly policy to ensure that children of single parents, sex workers, divorced couples and orphans are not denied education, identity documents or welfare benefits

articles.headline: NMDC discusses potential lithium investments with Russia's Rosatom
articles.title: NMDC said to be in talks with Russia’s Rosatom over lithium investments
articles.summary: Indian state-run miner NMDC Ltd. held preliminary talks with Russian state nuclear firm Rosatom regarding potential investments in Russian lithium mining and processing projects. Company officials visited Russia last month to explore critical mineral opportunities amid India's heavy reliance on imports for its growing electric vehicle and battery manufacturing industries.
articles.description: Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030

articles.headline: NDA dominates local body elections across Tirupati district
articles.title: TDP-led NDA dominates Tirupati district in ZPTC/MPTC elections
articles.summary: The National Democratic Alliance led by the Telugu Desam Party secured a majority in recent MPTC and ZPTC elections across Tirupati district. The TDP won twenty-five Zilla Parishat seats while alliance partners secured three, whereas the YSR Congress Party won six. However, the YSR Congress Party gained ground in Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu's native Chandragiri constituency by winning three out of six mandals.

articles.headline: United States consumer prices rise higher than expected in October
articles.title: US petrol prices are down, but elevated inflation continues
articles.summary: The United States Department of Labor Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index increased by 0.4 percent in October. This rise occurred despite petrol prices falling to a four-month low following eased concerns over the Strait of Hormuz closure, continuing persistent inflationary pressures that affected voters during the midterm elections.
articles.description: Inflation has remained high, despite some easing in fuel prices caused by the US war on Iran.

articles.headline: Blackstone agrees to acquire sixteen percent stake in IIFL Finance
articles.title: Blackstone to buy about 16% stake in India's IIFL Finance for $535 million
articles.summary: Blackstone will invest fifty billion Indian rupees to acquire approximately a sixteen percent stake in non-banking financial company IIFL Finance. Announced on November 10, 2026, the transaction is part of a broader capital raise that will increase the firm's capital adequacy ratio to about thirty percent and support its secured lending businesses.
articles.description: The issue will also include a 12.64 billion ​rupee ‌investment by existing investors Nirmal Jain and R. Venkataraman, while Anchorage Capital ‌will invest ​another ₹1.5 billion

articles.headline: Anthropic unveils new artificial intelligence office tools for knowledge workers
articles.title: Anthropic has its own AI-powered office suite now
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic unveiled a suite of office tools, including Claude Meetings, Sheets, and Whiteboards, targeted at non-technical knowledge workers. Revealed at a San Francisco event on Tuesday, the beta products aim to expand the company's user base and generate revenue ahead of its anticipated initial public offering.
articles.description: For years, Anthropic has been known for its focus on enterprise and coding tools that attract high-flying corporate clients, inspiring competing frontier labs - like OpenAI, SpaceXSI, and Meta - to copy its strategies. Earlier this year, Claude Code went through its own particular hype cycle. And now, Anthropic is trying to expand its footprint […]

articles.headline: Gulf Arab states approve military command headquarters in Kuwait
articles.title: Gulf Arab states approve military command headquarters in Kuwait, GCC chief says
articles.summary: The six Gulf Cooperation Council member states approved establishing an advanced headquarters for their Unified Military Command in Kuwait along with deploying appropriate forces, according to the bloc's secretary-general. The announcement followed the 23rd meeting of the Joint Defence Council in Bahrain. The command was originally created in 2013 to manage joint operations against regional threats amid ongoing security concerns.
articles.description: The announcement followed the 23rd meeting ​of the ‌GCC’s Joint Defence Council, attended by Defence Ministers from the bloc’s member states, in Bahrain

articles.headline: Atmospheric conditions cause firecracker emissions to linger
articles.title: Why do firecracker emissions sometimes linger in the air?
articles.summary: Emissions from firecrackers can remain trapped in the air when weak local winds prevent pollutants from dispersing effectively. According to published reports on November 12, 2026, continuous firecracker use over several hours causes fine particles to accumulate near the source faster than cleaner air can dilute them. Local weather patterns and atmospheric stability directly influence how long these harmful smoke particles persist in the environment.

articles.headline: Israeli president urges lawmakers to investigate October 7 attacks
articles.title: Israeli president warns against repeat election in new Knesset session
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged politicians in the 26th Knesset to avoid repeat elections and establish an independent inquiry into the October 7 attacks by Hamas. Herzog recently tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government within 28 days. Eisenkot aims to build a national emergency coalition while Netanyahu's bloc continues protesting the election results.
articles.description: Herzog calls for an inquiry into the October 7 attacks during a Knesset session amid political gridlock following elections.

articles.headline: Power outages persist in Prakasam villages following Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Cyclone-hit villages in Prakasam district remain without electricity
articles.summary: Coastal villages in Andhra Pradesh face ongoing electricity shortages after Cyclone Murasu damaged regional infrastructure. Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited personnel are conducting repair operations, with the energy minister stating that rising restoration expenditures have exceeded seven hundred crore rupees. Officials anticipate domestic supplies will resume shortly, while agricultural connections require additional time for full recovery.
articles.description: The villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge and are facing difficulties in meeting their daily needs, including access to drinking water and arranging fuel for generators, sources say

articles.headline: National Conference creates advisory councils to address internal dissent
articles.title: National Conference plans advisory councils of MLAs to address internal dissent
articles.summary: National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah began reaching out to party legislators by offering positions in newly formed advisory councils to bridge gaps between the party and government. The initiative follows a major political upheaval involving seventeen dissenting legislators who recently drafted a ten-point charter demanding manifesto implementation and the restoration of statehood and special status.
articles.description: Farooq Abdullah reaches out to legislators after 17 MLAs raise demands following Cabinet expansion; councils to work with Ministers on policy and departmental functioning
