articles.headline: Telangana to host Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14
articles.title: Telangana to host Bharat Summit on November 13 and 14
articles.summary: The Telangana government will host the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad, bringing together policymakers, academics, business representatives, and political leaders from about seventy countries. Congress Foreign Affairs Department chairman Salman Khurshid announced that discussions will focus on democracy, climate change, and economic justice, alongside special sessions highlighting the state's development initiatives.
articles.description: Global leaders and policymakers from 70 countries expected to attend; Kharge, Rahul and Priyanka invited, says Congress’ Foreign Affairs Department chairman Salman Khurshid

articles.headline: Security forces seized top court, Somalia’s ex-chief justice says
articles.title: Security forces seized top court, Somalia’s ex-chief justice says
articles.description: Somalia’s former Chief Justice said more than 300 security forces had ‘militarily occupied’ the Supreme Court.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules Uttar Pradesh responsible for releasing undertrials granted bail
articles.title: Onus on Uttar Pradesh to ensure undertrials allowed bail are released, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that Uttar Pradesh must ensure undertrial prisoners granted bail are not detained solely due to financial inability to meet release conditions. A Bench led by Justice M.M. Sundresh noted that over one hundred prisoners in twenty districts remained jailed despite receiving bail, violating their fundamental right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution.
articles.description: Of the 264 undertrial prisoners allowed bail, 106 had to continue behind bars for various reasons, including their inability to provide financial security or a guarantor to back them

articles.headline: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticises government over severe air pollution
articles.title: Congress questions Modi over Delhi air pollution, demands account of measures taken
articles.summary: Congress National President Mallikarjun Kharge accused the Bharatiya Janata Party administration on November 10, 2026, of implementing ineffective measures to combat dangerous air pollution levels across India. Following Deepavali celebrations, cities including Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Hyderabad recorded hazardous air quality indexes. Mr. Kharge urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to account for clean air initiatives, citing widespread public health risks.
articles.description: Mallikarjun Kharge says recurring pollution crisis in Delhi and the National Capital Region reflected the government’s failure to address the problem

articles.headline: Qatari PM’s Washington visit comes amid renewed US–Iran diplomacy
articles.title: Qatari PM’s Washington visit comes amid renewed US–Iran diplomacy
articles.description: Nayef Al-Nabet discusses the Qatari prime minister’s visit to Washington.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav vows to develop Ayodhya as global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage
articles.title: Akhilesh to visit Ram Temple; promises to transform Ayodhya into capital of Sanatan pilgrimage
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav promised to transform Ayodhya with world-class infrastructure and restore local economic dignity if his party wins the Uttar Pradesh elections. Writing on the platform X, the former chief minister alleged donation theft at the Ram temple and criticized the ruling government. Yadav announced plans to visit Ayodhya with his family on December 12 to offer prayers at local temples.
articles.description: The Uttar Pradesh BJP challenged Mr. Yadav to visit the Temple on December 6 — anniversary of the Babri Masjid demolition — and apologise for the killing of kar sevaks

articles.headline: Ebay restricts third-party AI agents from browsing platform
articles.title: eBay appears to have shut the door on third-party AI agents
articles.summary: Online marketplace eBay has blocked third-party artificial intelligence agents, such as Meta Platforms Inc.'s Muse, from browsing and extracting product listings. While shopping companies market artificial intelligence integration, platforms like eBay and Amazon restrict external bots to prevent unauthorized data scraping and maintain a secure user experience for human buyers and sellers.
articles.description: eBay appears to have blocked AI agents, including Meta's Muse, from browsing on the platform - the latest speed bump in the AI agent race. A reader tells The Verge that for several weeks he's had his Muse agent browse and curate a daily digest of watches for sale on platforms like eBay, including a […]

articles.headline: At least 12 people killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-up
articles.title: At least 12 people killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-up
articles.description: At least 12 people have been killed and dozens injured in multiple crashes involving around 50 vehicles on a motorway

articles.headline: Social activist and Barefoot College founder Sanjit Bunker Roy dies
articles.title: Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College, dies at 81
articles.summary: Renowned social activist Sanjit Bunker Roy died at the age of eighty-one on November 10, 2026, at his home in Tilonia, Rajasthan. He spent over five decades working for rural development and women empowerment after founding the Social Work and Research Centre, known as Barefoot College, in 1972, which trained rural villagers in solar energy, water conservation, and healthcare based on Gandhian principles.
articles.description: Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972

articles.headline: French police make arrests in Mohamed Al Fayed investigation
articles.title: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.summary: French authorities have made arrests following joint operations with the British Metropolitan Police that included searches at the Ritz hotel in Paris and other properties linked to the late Mohamed Al Fayed. The mid-October 2026 raids mark the first arrests in connection with widespread allegations of sexual abuse and human trafficking by the former Harrods owner.
articles.description: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Crime Branch registers FIR over fake social media takedown notices
articles.title: Juvenile traced to Srinagar for sending fake Delhi Police notices targeting IFF, SFLC X accounts; Crime Branch registers FIR
articles.summary: The Delhi Police Crime Branch registered a case involving fraudulent notices sent to social media platform X, which falsely demanded the removal of posts and the blocking of accounts belonging to the Internet Freedom Foundation and the Software Freedom Law Centre. The platform previously informed the Delhi High Court that an internal investigation confirmed an imposter had sent the fake communications.
articles.description: X had told the Delhi High Court that the takedown requests purportedly issued in the name of the Delhi Police were fraudulent; the force’s IFSO unit will assist in the investigation

articles.headline: DMK president M.K. Stalin criticises Tamil Nadu law and order
articles.title: Law and order in coma in Tamil Nadu, says Stalin
articles.summary: DMK president M.K. Stalin criticised the administration on November 10, 2026, alleging that law and order in Tamil Nadu had completely collapsed. He cited seventeen murders in a single day, harassment involving officials, and legislative failures, while accusing Chief Minister Vijay of administrative neglect and prioritizing content creation over governmental responsibilities.
articles.description: He alleged miscreants had lost all fear of the government, which he claimed was led by a “joker”

articles.headline: Twelve people killed after pile-ups on motorway in Bulgaria
articles.title: Twelve dead after motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria fog
articles.summary: Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced that twelve people were killed and around fifty others hospitalised after more than seventy vehicles collided in two separate pile-ups on the Trakia motorway near Zimnitsa. Officials stated that dense fog and unsuitable driving speeds caused the crashes. Health Minister Katya Ivkova confirmed eleven deaths at the scene, prompting Radev to declare Wednesday a day of national mourning.
articles.description: About 50 other people were injured in the pile-ups along a section of the Trakia motorway, officials have said.

articles.headline: Polish gunman fascinated by neo-Nazi killer Anders Behring Breivik
articles.title: Poland gunman fascinated by Norway’s neo-Nazi mass killer Breivik
articles.summary: Investigations into a mass shooting in Krakow reveal that suspect Michal Oksinski visited websites dedicated to Norwegian white-supremacist killer Anders Behring Breivik. Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek reported strong indications of right-wing extremism behind the November attack that killed six people. The disclosure intensifies a domestic political dispute regarding government statements and the exact ideological motivations driving the tragic incident.
articles.description: Suspect in deadly November 7 Krakow shooting looked up the white supremacist who killed dozens in 2011, a minister says.

articles.headline: Deadly train collision in Egypt prompts parliamentary calls for accountability
articles.title: Deadly Egypt train crash prompts calls for political accountability
articles.summary: A train crash on the outskirts of Cairo killed at least seven people and injured over one hundred others, sparking intense parliamentary scrutiny. Lawmakers questioned Transport Minister Kamal el-Wazir regarding safety investments and recurring accidents in the al-Ayyat area. Opposition politicians demanded broader political accountability and financial transparency regarding funds allocated toward modernising the national railway network.
articles.description: A deadly train collision in Egypt's al-Ayyat prompts demands for political accountability and rail upgrade reviews.

articles.headline: Lewis Hamilton visits Rafah crossing to witness Gaza aid efforts
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Rafah crossing to witness Gaza aid efforts
articles.description: Lewis Hamilton visits Rafah crossing to witness Gaza aid efforts

articles.headline: Iran rejects French accusations linking it to supermarket cyberattacks
articles.title: Iran rejects France’s ‘baseless accusations’ on cyberattack
articles.summary: Iran rejected French allegations regarding cyberattacks that raised temperatures in hundreds of French supermarket refrigerators on October 11 and 12, forcing food disposals. The Iranian Foreign Ministry termed the claims baseless on November 10, 2026, while French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot warned of proportionate measures. The European Union announced plans for a swift and united response following the incidents.
articles.description: Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi may attend Hyderabad OBC rally and Bharat Summit
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi may participate in OBC rally in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is expected to visit Hyderabad on November 13 or 14 to attend the Bharat Summit and potentially join an OBC rally. Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee president Mahesh Kumar Goud discussed party initiatives during a meeting on November 10, 2026. Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu stated that the international summit will bring global experts together at HITEX.

articles.headline: CPI-M criticizes Kerala government over higher education and reservation policies
articles.title: CPI(M) accuses UDF of making higher education sole privilege of students from entitled families and undermining reservation criteria
articles.summary: The Communist Party of India Marxist accused Higher Education Minister Roji M. John on November 10, 2026, of undermining public institutions and reservation criteria. State secretary M.V. Govindan stated that allowing private colleges to operate without oversight increases costs for working-class students. The party also defended the Kerala Public Service Commission against a Crime Branch inquiry initiated by the United Democratic Front government.
articles.description: He says UDF has undermined the constitutionally guaranteed reservation criteria for students from historically backward sections of society by allowing private colleges free rein to start new courses, charge capitation fees, and appoint faculty by passing PSC

articles.headline: Young herders revive traditional Mongolian winter ritual
articles.title: Mongolia’s Iron Winter: A Race to Save an Ancient Tradition
articles.summary: Two young horse herders in Mongolia's remote Tsakhir Valley have revived an ancient winter ritual to protect their community from harsh environmental pressures. Documented in a film by Kasimir Burgess, the teenagers faced brutal blizzards and extreme conditions during what became the region's deadliest winter on record, highlighting the survival of an age-old cultural tradition.
articles.description: Two young horse herders revive Mongolia’s most dangerous winter ritual to save their community's ancient way of life.

articles.headline: Odisha opposition parties accuse government of flood mismanagement
articles.title: Opposition parties accuse Majhi government of mishandling flood situation in Odisha
articles.summary: Opposition parties in Odisha, including the Biju Janata Dal and the Congress, accused the Bharatiya Janata Party-led government on November 10, 2026, of mishandling recent floods in Ganjam district. Leaders alleged that delayed water releases from dams and inadequate public warnings compounded the disaster, leaving thousands homeless across more than 800 inundated villages.
articles.description: ‘It is deeply unfortunate that Ganjam has been set back by several years due to negligence by the State government,’ says BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik

articles.headline: Downstream communities issue ultimatum over Dibang dam project
articles.title: Opposition builds over third mega dam project on Dibang River
articles.summary: An alliance of downstream communities in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh issued a ten-day deadline to state governments regarding the 2,880-megawatt Dibang Multipurpose Project. Developed by NHPC Limited at an estimated cost of 31,875 crore rupees, the project faces demands for comprehensive rehabilitation, flood protection safeguards, and official project-affected family status before its commissioning by February 2032.
articles.description: An alliance of communities in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam that will be affected by the 2,880-MW Dibang Multipurpose Project have set a 10-day deadline for their demands to be met

articles.headline: Did humanity learn the right lessons from WWII?
articles.title: Did humanity learn the right lessons from WWII?
articles.description: Did humanity learn the right lessons from WWII?

articles.headline: Keralam opposition leader demands judicial inquiry into power deal
articles.title: Pinarayi alleges graft, demands judicial probe into Keralam govt.’s GNA power purchase deal
articles.summary: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan demanded a judicial inquiry headed by a High Court judge on November 10, 2026, into the cancelled GNA power purchase agreement. Vijayan alleged that the government attempted to impose a major financial burden on consumers through an artificial power crisis and bypassed the Kerala State Electricity Board to award high-rate private contracts.
articles.description: He claims cancellation of the power purchase agreement is a vindication of the Opposition’s stance that there is no power crisis in Keralam. The government was forced to withdraw from the agreement only because the Opposition and the media exposed alleged irregularities with supporting evidence

articles.headline: France accuses Iranian cyberunit of sabotaging supermarket refrigerators
articles.title: What is Shahid Kaveh, ⁠⁠the Iran cyberunit tied to France’s fridge hacking?
articles.summary: French authorities blamed Shahid Kaveh, an offensive cyberunit linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, for hacking refrigeration systems in seven hundred commercial sites last month. The cyberattack remotely raised temperatures and spoiled millions of euros in food. While Iran denied involvement, Western intelligence agencies have previously connected the unit to attacks on infrastructure in the United States and Israel.
articles.description: IRGC-linked unit operates through front groups posing as vigilante hackers to hit adversaries, says French intelligence.

articles.headline: Iraq blocks Iranian football team flight due to United States sanctions
articles.title: Iraq bars Iranian football team’s plane from landing in Basra: Report
articles.summary: Iraqi officials prevented an aircraft carrying Iran’s national football team from landing at Basra airport on Tuesday. The decision followed United States sanctions targeting Iranian airlines, prompting the team to complete their journey by road. The aviation authority acted to avoid secondary penalties that could exclude local service providers from the global financial system during ongoing regional tensions.
articles.description: Decision by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority reportedly related to ⁠US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines.

articles.headline: Formula One confirms upcoming grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi
articles.title: FIA chief says Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grand Prix to go ahead despite tensions
articles.summary: Motorsports governing body president Mohammed Ben Sulayem announced that the final two races of the Formula One season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled on November 29 and December 6. Despite regional Middle Eastern tensions and earlier cancellations in Saudi Arabia, the Federation Internationale de l’Automobile remains fully committed to delivering a successful conclusion to the championship.
articles.description: This year's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was scrapped following the outbreak of the US and Israel's war with Iran.

articles.headline: Adobe integrates third-party artificial intelligence agents into Creative Cloud applications
articles.title: Adobe is going all in on agentic AI
articles.summary: Adobe announced new agentic artificial intelligence capabilities at its Miami conference, allowing external assistants from providers like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to operate locally inside Photoshop and Premiere. The company also previewed background tools and upgrades to the Firefly AI Assistant, implementing a plan to embed conversational automation across its entire software suite by early 2027.
articles.description: Adobe is committing itself to the notion that chatbots and AI agents could be your next design assistant, or even automate creative workflows and repetitive tasks on your behalf. Some of the tools and features announced today at Adobe's Max conference in Miami, Florida, include allowing your preferred third-party AI agents to access and change […]

articles.headline: Indian industry bodies seek tax cuts in upcoming Union Budget
articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.summary: Major industry associations urged the Ministry of Finance to rationalise long-term capital gains tax on equities and lower the securities transaction tax ahead of Union Budget 2027. During pre-Budget consultations with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, groups like the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry also requested relief for micro, small, and medium enterprises to counter economic pressures and foreign investor withdrawals.
articles.description: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

articles.headline: Meta expands artificial intelligence age-estimation technology globally for teen accounts
articles.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens?
articles.summary: Meta deployed artificial intelligence age-estimation tools worldwide on Monday to detect underage users who registered with false birth dates. Flagged profiles are transitioned into restricted Teen Accounts with default privacy settings and messaging limits. The global rollout follows an August legal settlement in the United States, though experts have questioned the system's effectiveness and privacy protections.
articles.description: The tech giant rolls out age-detection tool for Instagram and Facebook, but experts doubt whether it can help protect teens.

articles.headline: US deports former Rwandan student Jean Leonard Teganya over genocide allegations
articles.title: Who is Jean Leonard Teganya, deported by US over Rwanda genocide claims?
articles.summary: Jean Leonard Teganya, who was accused of identifying Tutsi civilians during the 1994 genocide, has been deported from the United States to Rwanda by security officers. Handed over at Kigali International Airport, he faces a 2014 indictment by the National Public Prosecution Authority for alleged genocide and crimes against humanity committed in the former Butare prefecture.
articles.description: Teganya, a former medical student, is accused of participating in the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda.

articles.headline: France accuses Iran of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration units
articles.title: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
articles.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot stated that cyberattacks by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps manipulated supermarket refrigeration units last month, destroying millions of euros in food. Following similar incidents across seven other European countries, Paris prosecutors launched an investigation into three individuals linked to the offensive cyber unit. Iran has not yet responded to these allegations.
articles.description: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.

articles.headline: Spain considers TikTok suspension following investigation into child sexual abuse videos
articles.title: Spain mulls TikTok suspension after investigation into child sex abuse videos
articles.summary: Spain is considering suspending TikTok after an investigation by Maldita.es uncovered over one thousand child sexual abuse videos and tens of thousands of suspected paedophile profiles. The Ministry of Youth and Children demanded explanations and urged prosecutors to take action, while the European Union previously warned the platform over its personalised feed design.
articles.description: Ministry of Youth and Children calls for urgent meeting with TikTok leadership in Spain.

articles.headline: Donald Trump nominates Natalie Baker as United States Ambassador to Pakistan
articles.title: U.S. President Donald Trump nominates Natalie Baker as next Ambassador to Pakistan
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump nominated Natalie Baker as the next ambassador to Pakistan, ending a nearly two-year gap for a permanent envoy in Islamabad. Baker currently serves as charge d'affaires at the United States embassy and previously held diplomatic roles in Doha, Libya, Dubai, and Kuwait. The White House submitted the nomination to the United States Senate for review and confirmation by its foreign relations committee.
articles.description: Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome

articles.headline: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies at age 104
articles.title: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
articles.summary: Solange Alexandre, one of France's last World War Two resistance heroes and a rare female commander of an anti-German unit, has died at a nursing home in Le Mans at the age of 104. President Emmanuel Macron and other figures paid tribute to her legacy of leading sabotage operations and sheltering Allied airmen.
articles.description: With 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and joined the fight against the occupying German forces.

articles.headline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky meets Nordic leaders in Denmark for security talks
articles.title: Zelensky holds air defence, energy security talks with Nordic leaders
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Denmark on November 10, 2026, to confer with Nordic leaders regarding military assistance, air defence, and energy infrastructure protection. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen emphasized continued regional support amid ongoing Russian attacks. Meanwhile, direct negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow commenced in Abu Dhabi under United States mediation, alongside heightened security measures in Copenhagen.
articles.description: The Nordic countries are among the main supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky travelled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys

articles.headline: Iran lifts self-imposed two thousand kilometre range limit on ballistic missiles
articles.title: Iran lifts 2,000km limit on its ballistic missiles: What that means
articles.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the removal of its self-imposed two thousand kilometre ballistic missile range limit during a Tehran news conference. Brigadier-General Hossein Mohebbi stated that the military doctrine had shifted toward an offensive posture, raising international concerns over potential targets across Europe and the Middle East.
articles.description: Experts ask whether longer-range missiles are intended to hit targets beyond the Middle East.

articles.headline: Motorway pile-up in thick fog kills twelve people in southeastern Bulgaria
articles.title: At least 12 people killed in motorway crash in southeastern Bulgaria
articles.summary: Thick fog caused a multiple-vehicle collision involving approximately fifty cars and trucks on a motorway linking Sofia and Burgas near Yambol, killing twelve people and injuring forty-six others. Health Minister Katya Ivkova confirmed the fatalities, prompting Prime Minister Rumen Radev to cancel his schedule while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen was visiting.
articles.description: Dozens of people hospitalised after 50 vehicle pile-up caused by thick fog.

articles.headline: Karnataka Industries Minister blames Nitin Gadkari for ethanol blending crisis
articles.title: Karnataka Industries Minister blames Gadkari for ‘ethanol blending crisis’
articles.summary: Karnataka Industries Minister M.B. Patil accused Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari of causing the ethanol-blending crisis by exceeding prescribed limits. Speaking to media persons, Patil demanded a thorough investigation and stated that sugar factories face excess ethanol storage capacity due to inadequate central procurement. He claimed the abrupt nationwide rollout caused widespread difficulties across multiple states.
articles.description: ‘They [the Centre] refuses to believe me when I speak the truth about ethanol blending; let them ask sugar industry leaders such as Murugesh Nirani and Prabhakar Kore’ said M.B. Patil

articles.headline: Election Commission extends model code restrictions to retired officials
articles.title: ECI extends model code restrictions to retired Govt officials engaged by States
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India announced that political neutrality rules under the Model Code of Conduct now apply to retired government personnel hired by state administrations. Officials sent the directive to five regions scheduled for early elections. These individuals are explicitly barred from participating in or canvassing during upcoming political campaigns.
articles.description: The Election Commission of India said such individuals must maintain political neutrality and refrain from participating in election campaigns or canvassing

articles.headline: University of Oxford returns ancestral remains of thirty-nine Naga people
articles.title: Oxford University returns remains of 39 Naga people after more than a century
articles.summary: The University of Oxford formally returned the ancestral remains of thirty-nine members of the Naga community to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho during a ceremony on November 9, 2026. Held at the Pitt Rivers Museum for over a century, the remains departed for Nagaland to be buried at Naga Solidarity Park in Kohima to promote healing and unity.
articles.description: The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on November 9, 2026

articles.headline: Chennai court dismisses bail plea of former minister Anbil Mahesh
articles.title: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case
articles.summary: A special court in Chennai on November 9, 2026, rejected the bail petition filed by former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi. The politician was arrested on October 26 in connection with an alleged multi-crore bribery scam involving government approvals for private schools during the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam regime, according to the Central Crime Branch.
articles.description: Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

articles.headline: Gulf Cooperation Council establishes advanced military command headquarters in Kuwait
articles.title: Why the GCC is setting up an advanced military command base in Kuwait
articles.summary: The Gulf Cooperation Council agreed on Tuesday in Bahrain to establish an advanced headquarters for its Unified Military Command in Kuwait, planning to station appropriate military forces there. The announcement follows regional tensions and Iranian attacks on Gulf nations. The United States-allied bloc aims to enhance collective defense against threats, though specific troop numbers and details regarding the deployment remain undisclosed by officials.
articles.description: Gulf leaders emphasised the need to strengthen defence coordination to confront present and future regional challenges.

articles.headline: MRF reports twenty-seven percent profit decline amid rising raw material costs
articles.title: MRF’s Q2 profit skids 27% as raw material costs squeeze margins
articles.summary: MRF Limited reported a twenty-six point six percent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to 386.99 crore rupees for the second quarter ending September 30, 2026. Despite a seventeen point four percent rise in consolidated total income to 8,791.58 crore rupees, surging material costs squeezed margins. The company anticipates continued volatility in commodity markets moving forward through the fiscal year.
articles.description: Tyre maker anticipates continued disruptions and volatility in commodity markets. Raw material and logistics costs are expected to remain elevated.

articles.headline: Donald Trump demands financial compensation from Israel and Gulf allies for Iran war
articles.title: Trump says Israel, Gulf allies must repay Iran war cost: What does it mean?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated in an interview that the United States intends to seek complete reimbursement for military costs incurred during the recent conflict with Iran from protected allies including Israel and Gulf Cooperation Council nations. Analysts suggest the reimbursement demand serves primarily as domestic political signaling rather than an actionable policy proposal following midterm elections.
articles.description: Analysts say Trump’s comments are more likely to be political posturing than a reflection of serious policy priorities.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu defends expensive electricity purchase agreement amid high power demand
articles.title: Why has Tamil Nadu opted for an expensive electricity purchase agreement? | Explained
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited signed a power purchase agreement exceeding thirty rupees per unit, sparking criticism from opposition parties. Energy Resources Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar stated that prolonged high electricity demand and the exclusive availability of gas power necessitated the costly deal. The administration defended the measure on October 14, 2026, citing exceptional seasonal consumption pressures across the state.
articles.description: The Tamil Nadu government clarified that due to the high power demand in the State this time, thanks to a prolonged summer-like situation, it had to opt for such an agreement

articles.headline: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government marks six months in power
articles.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led govt. in Tamil Nadu enjoys public goodwill despite concerns on being directionless
articles.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government completed six months in office while maintaining public goodwill despite facing criticism over policy direction. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay continued welfare programs including student breakfasts and gold distributions. Opposition leaders from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam criticized the administration over power procurement and industrial investments.
articles.description: Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an ‘empty coffer,’ the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures

articles.headline: Spanish police officer killed by explosive backpack in Oviedo
articles.title: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain
articles.summary: An explosive device detonated during a neighborhood dispute response in Oviedo, killing a member of the canine unit and severely injuring a bomb disposal officer. Authorities discovered the suspicious backpack after arriving to investigate a reported shooting that left one woman hospitalized. A manhunt is currently underway across the northern Spanish city to locate the fleeing suspect.
articles.description: Officers attended the scene in connection with a separate incident at a residential building in the Spanish city.

articles.headline: Israeli forces shoot dead Palestinian boy during West Bank operation
articles.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian boy in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed fourteen-year-old Moataz Daghlas in the West Bank village of Burqa on Monday evening, according to the Palestinian health ministry. The military stated soldiers fired at individuals intending to throw stones. Medics reported two others were wounded during the raid, while relatives stated authorities withheld the body amidst broader regional violence involving numerous casualties this year.
articles.description: The Israeli military says its soldiers opened fire at individuals “who intended to hurl stones” at a road used by Israelis.

articles.headline: Malaysian court clears former prime minister Najib Razak for house arrest
articles.title: Malaysian court clears former PM Najib Razak for house arrest transfer
articles.summary: A Kuala Lumpur high court ruled that former Prime Minister Najib Razak will serve the remainder of his reduced six-year sentence under house arrest following a conditional pardon. Judge Aslam Zainuddin delivered the decision on Tuesday after an earlier delay by the attorney general over legal interpretations. Najib remains convicted in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal and faces additional prison terms.
articles.description: Najib, 73, was jailed for his role in looting the now-defunct sovereign wealth fund 1MDB.

articles.headline: Chennai Metrowater appoints women engineers to key leadership positions
articles.title: Women engineers take the helm at Chennai Metrowater
articles.summary: Chennai Metrowater has appointed women to key leadership roles, including chief engineers and engineering directors, for the first time since its inception. Women currently comprise fifty-six percent of the agency workforce. Officials like O. Parveez and K. Uma highlighted historical challenges in balancing demanding field assignments and public interactions as the organization modernized its infrastructure and administrative operations.
articles.description: Their rise reflects a gradual change in an organisation where women were once largely assigned to execution and office work. The milestone comes at a time when women account for 56% of the agency’s workforce

articles.headline: Poland arrests two Ukrainian men for alleged Russian espionage
articles.title: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage, sabotage
articles.summary: Internal Security Agency officers detained two Ukrainian nationals accused of conducting reconnaissance on critical infrastructure and military sites on behalf of Moscow. Prosecutors stated the suspects received cryptocurrency payments to commit arson attacks intended to provoke anti-Ukrainian sentiment. Both detainees face potential life imprisonment if convicted of foreign intelligence espionage and sabotage charges.
articles.description: Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi's memoir to release in November
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir to revisit love, loss and her decision to decline India’s top job
articles.summary: Indian National Congress leader and Rajya Sabha Member Sonia Gandhi has written a memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love, scheduled for publication on November 10, 2026, by Alfred A. Knopf. The 79-year-old politician reflects on marrying into the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty, personal tragedies including the assassinations of family members, her political career, and her decision to decline the position of Prime Minister.
articles.description: ‘It was heartbreak and loss that threw me into the public world of politics. Up till then I had guarded my privacy fiercely,’ Sonia Gandhi said in her statement

articles.headline: Qantas to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource corporate functions
articles.title: Australia's Qantas to axe 850 jobs in offshoring deal with Accenture
articles.summary: Australian flag carrier Qantas announced on November 10, 2026, that it will eliminate 850 jobs and outsource corporate functions to consulting firm Accenture. Chief Executive Officer Vanessa Hudson stated that the reductions, representing three percent of the workforce, will occur over coming years due to artificial intelligence advancements, with affected roles shifting mostly to India-based teams.
articles.description: First round of cuts due by mid-2027; some corporate functions to be outsourced to Accenture ​in India and Australia; union accuses Qantas of going back on word against offshoring jobs

articles.headline: France summons Iranian ambassador following supermarket refrigerator cyberattack
articles.title: France summons Iran’s ambassador over supermarket fridge ‘sabotage’
articles.summary: France summoned Iran ambassador to Paris to lodge a protest after accusing Tehran of orchestrating a cyberattack that targeted supermarket refrigerators on October 11 and 12. Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot stated the incident ruined millions of euros in perishable food across multiple store chains. Paris prosecutors initiated an investigation into an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps cyber unit regarding the sabotage.
articles.description: Iran categorically denied the French accusations, calling the claims 'baseless'.

articles.headline: Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge criticizes Modi government over worsening Delhi air pollution
articles.title: ‘Why are we becoming vishwaguru in air pollution?’ Kharge asks Modi government
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized the central government on November 10, 2026, over severe air pollution in Delhi and northern states. Citing official data regarding pollution-related deaths and unspent environmental funds, Kharge accused the administration of inaction and superficial measures. The Supreme Court has directed Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to submit proposed remedial actions within two weeks.
articles.description: Clean air is a fundamental right, not a privilege to be granted by the Government, Mallikarjun Kharge said

articles.headline: Mumbai air quality worsens significantly to poor category during Deepavali celebrations
articles.title: Mumbai AQI rises from 131 to 278 on Deepavali
articles.summary: Mumbai experienced a sharp decline in air quality on Deepavali as the Air Quality Index surged from 131 in the afternoon to 278 by evening, entering the poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, multiple areas recorded high pollution levels following widespread firecracker bursting despite a judicial ban. Experts noted that sea wind patterns also influenced pollutant dispersion across the city.
articles.description: Despite a court order banning the bursting of firecrackers on roads, streets, and public spaces, firecrackers began going off across Mumbai and its eastern and western suburbs by evening

articles.headline: Public-sector insurers face ongoing scrutiny over underutilization of Health Insurance TPA
articles.title: CAG flagged underuse of PSU insurers’ own TPA; four years on, accountability remains elusive
articles.summary: State-backed general insurers continue to withhold details regarding business allocations to Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd, four years after a Comptroller and Auditor General audit flagged its underutilization. While public-sector firms cite commercial confidence to restrict transparency, the joint venture maintains significant operational capacity, raising persistent questions about accountability and whether promoter insurers have fulfilled recommended allocation thresholds since the 2022 report.
articles.description: RTI replies and public disclosures offer little clarity on whether business allocation increased or what action followed the audit recommendations

articles.headline: British author M John Harrison wins 2026 Booker Prize for dystopian novel
articles.title: UK author M John Harrison’s End of Everything wins Booker Prize
articles.summary: British author M John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize on November 9 for his dystopian satire novel, The End of Everything, becoming the oldest winner in the literary award’s history at 81 years old. The unanimous decision marks the first time a science fiction work has received the prize. Harrison collected the 50,000 British pound award at a London ceremony for the 198-page book.
articles.description: The book uses dark humour and elusive narratives to cast a futuristic lens on modern politics post-calamity.

articles.headline: Zomato co-founder Deepinder Goyal launches Temple wearable device amid medical criticism
articles.title: Does the Temple wearable reveal useful information about brain health?
articles.summary: Entrepreneur Deepinder Goyal announced the commercial release of Temple, a new wearable monitoring device marketed as a personal health tool. The launch by the Zomato and Blinkit co-founder faced immediate backlash from medical professionals, including physician Cyriac Abby Philips, who publicly dismissed the product as a scam on social media due to Goyal lacking a formal background in medical sciences.
articles.description: Billionaire Deepinder Goyal has begun selling Temple, a temple-attached wearable he says can monitor brain health and ageing by measuring cerebral blood flow outside the lab. Critics and doctors question the device’s medical claims, noting the evidence is preliminary, not peer-reviewed, and its core metric—the Brain Flow index—remains controversial amid concerns over links to longevity or cognitive outcomes

articles.headline: Pakistan TV anchor allegedly shot dead at home by her husband
articles.title: Pakistan TV anchor allegedly shot dead at home by her husband
articles.description: Pakistan TV anchor Rabiya Ahsan was shot dead at home. Police are probing her husband's claim of accidental firing.

articles.headline: Ousted Bangladesh leader Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport to return
articles.title: What is Hasina’s game plan as she seeks a passport to return to Bangladesh?
articles.summary: Ousted Bangladesh leader Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport and national identity card from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, aiming to return in December more than two years after fleeing to India. Sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity linked to a 2024 crackdown, Dhaka has rejected the request and intends to seek her extradition.
articles.description: The ousted leader faces the prospect of being hanged upon return for her violent suppression of the 2024 uprising.

articles.headline: India and United States commit to joint action against narcotic threats
articles.title: India, U.S. vow to jointly act against emerging drug threats
articles.summary: India and the United States held their second drug policy executive working group meeting in New Delhi on November 2 and 3, hosted by the Narcotics Control Bureau and announced on November 10, 2026. Led by NCB Director General Anurag and U.S. official Debbie Seguin, the nations agreed to enhance intelligence sharing, law enforcement coordination, and supply chain security.
articles.description: The Narcotics Control Bureau hosted the 2nd India-United States of America Drug Policy Executive Working Group Meeting on November 2-3

articles.headline: Three contract workers die at Tata Electronics iPhone components plant
articles.title: Three workers die at Tata’s iPhone parts plant in India’s Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Three contract workers died after inhaling gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank at a Tata Electronics facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, on Monday. The employees were assigned to clean an effluent treatment plant when the incident occurred, prompting the state industries minister to announce a thorough investigation into the tragedy at the major Apple supplier.
articles.description: The workers had inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank, a district official says.

articles.headline: Are your supplements fake?
articles.title: Are your supplements fake?
articles.description: That protein powder in your cupboard might not be all protein, and those creatine gummies might be candy.

articles.headline: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi defends ethanol blending compliance across states
articles.title: ‘Sensationalism over governance’: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi over Karnataka’s ethanol blending claims
articles.summary: Union Minister for Food Public Distribution and Consumer Affairs Pralhad Joshi stated on November 10, 2026, that all 893 petrol samples tested across 27 States and Union Territories complied with the 19 to 21 percent ethanol blending range. Joshi criticized Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad for claiming higher blending levels in the state, defending the national ethanol program for benefiting sugarcane farmers and saving foreign exchange.
articles.description: All 56 samples tested in Karnataka by the OMCs were compliant, recording 19–20% of ethanol blend in petrol, with an average of 19.30%, the Minister claimed in a post on X.

articles.headline: California voters reject proposed billionaire tax in midterm elections
articles.title: California voters reject billionaire tax
articles.summary: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a proposed one percent tax on residents with a net worth exceeding one billion dollars, during the midterm elections. With about 60 percent of votes counted by Tuesday, the measure faced 55.6 percent opposition, driven by tech billionaires and opposition from outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom, dealing a blow to progressive lawmakers.
articles.description: The proposed measure would have imposed a one-time 5 percent tax on Californian billionaires to fund healthcare.

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu retains caretaker powers amid Israeli government formation
articles.title: What powers does Netanyahu have as Israel’s interim PM?
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister of Israel while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot attempts to form a government following recent national elections. Under basic laws, Netanyahu retains executive authority over security and state management, though analysts note his administration faces constraints and heightened scrutiny regarding military decisions and intelligence framing.
articles.description: As Israel faces political gridlock, Netanyahu wields caretaker powers to manage security and disrupt his rivals.

articles.headline: Maharashtra farmers demand uniform sugarcane pricing and drought relief
articles.title: Farmers demand uniform ₹4,200 sugarcane rate across Maharashtra
articles.summary: A delegation of farmers met Maharashtra Cooperation Minister Babasaheb Patil in Latur on November 9, 2026, demanding uniform sugarcane pricing across the state, a two lakh rupee loan incentive, and enhanced drought relief. Led by Krantikari Shetkari Sanghatana state president Rajiv Kasbe, the group also sought financial assistance for agricultural labourers and stricter regulations to curb harassment by microfinance companies in rural regions.
articles.description: The delegation demanded a ₹2 lakh incentive grant for farmers who regularly repay their loans and ₹1 lakh per hectare in financial assistance for drought-affected cultivators

articles.headline: BJP criticizes Sonia Gandhi over memoir addressing 1975 Emergency
articles.title: Sonia Gandhi trying to justify Emergency, memoir should've been named ‘Whitewashing’: BJP
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for attempting to justify the 1975 Emergency in her newly released memoir. BJP national spokesperson C.R. Kesavan argued the book whitewashes historical wrongs committed by the Nehru-Gandhi family. Gandhi wrote that the Emergency was a mistake and expressed regret, while the ruling party highlighted various historical events and controversies during Congress rule.
articles.description: The comments from the ruling party came on the day Sonia Gandhi’s memoir was released, in which she weighed in on the Emergency imposed in the country in 1975 and called it a mistake

articles.headline: N. Ram on his interview with Sonia Gandhi
articles.title: N. Ram on his interview with Sonia Gandhi
articles.description: N. Ram reflects on his interview with former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, who discusses her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. She speaks about the impact of twelve years of BJP-RSS rule on Indian democracy, defends the Congress party’s fight for a level playing field and shares how her love story with Rajiv Gandhi evolved into a lifelong commitment to India.

articles.headline: India initiates anti-dumping probes on aluminium products from four nations
articles.title: DGTR suo motu initiates probe into dumping of aluminium products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam
articles.summary: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies initiated suo-motu investigations into the dumping of aluminium products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand. According to a notification issued on November 9, 2026, the Commerce Ministry arm acted upon representations from the Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of India to safeguard domestic micro, small, and medium enterprises from cheap imports.
articles.description: According to a DGTR notification, it has received representations from the Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of India which represents 228 manufacturers of Aluminium Extrusion Profiles, Structures and Articles

articles.headline: Three family members killed in mud house collapse in Madhya Pradesh
articles.title: Three members of family killed, four injured as house collapses in MP's Singrauli
articles.summary: Three people died and four others sustained injuries after a mud house collapsed in the Jalhathani Tola area of Singrauli district on November 9, 2026. According to Kotwali police station in-charge Abhimanyu Dwivedi, the victims included a thirty-six-year-old man, his mother, and his two-year-old daughter. The family was reportedly constructing a new dwelling under a government housing scheme when the tragedy occurred.
articles.description: According to eyewitnesses, the victims were asleep in the house when it suddenly collapsed and was reduced to rubble. The entire family was trapped under the debris

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh agricultural minister directs officials to expedite cyclone crop loss assessments
articles.title: Cyclones Arnab and Murasu damaged crops on 4.61 lakh hectares in Andhra, say officials
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu directed officials to expedite crop loss enumerations following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. The storms damaged agricultural and horticultural crops across multiple districts, affecting hundreds of thousands of farmers and causing substantial financial losses. The minister instructed authorities to conduct comprehensive field assessments to ensure all eligible farmers receive relief.
articles.description: Enumeration covers only 2,211.73 of the 6,748.52 hectares of horticultural crops damaged by Cyclone Murasu

articles.headline: National Commission for Women receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually
articles.title: NCW receives 1.5 lakh complaints annually, domestic violence tops list: Vijaya Rahatkar
articles.summary: According to National Commission for Women Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar, the organisation handles approximately 1.5 lakh grievances every year, with domestic violence forming the largest share. Women can seek assistance through various channels, including the 14490 helpline, email, and the online Management Information System. To improve accessibility, the commission conducts public hearings across the country to resolve local issues.
articles.description: No woman should feel that she could not approach the NCW simply because she did not know how to file a complaint, Vijaya Rahatkar

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir minister Mir Saifullah vows to restore special status
articles.title: Newly-inducted J&K Minister Mir Saifullah pledges that NC will ‘restore pre-1953 position, get back J&K flag’
articles.summary: Newly inducted National Conference minister Mir Saifullah declared during a rally in Kralpora that his party is committed to restoring Jammu and Kashmir's pre-1953 position, separate flag, statehood, and Article 35A. Speaking on November 9, 2026, he described the August 2019 downgrading of the region into a Union Territory as an injustice and called for unified efforts to reverse the changes.
articles.description: Mr. Saifullah said Kashmir was reduced to a Union Territory (UT) brazenly on August 5, 2019

articles.headline: U.S. lawmakers reintroduce federal legislation to officially recognise Deepavali holiday
articles.title: Bill in U.S. Congress to recognise Deepavali as federal holiday, 19 lawmakers back proposal
articles.summary: A group of United States lawmakers led by Grace Meng reintroduced the Deepavali Day Act in the House of Representatives to establish the festival as a federal holiday. Supporters state the legislation honours diverse cultural traditions and addresses rising hate incidents against religious communities. If passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the twelfth federally recognised holiday in the country.
articles.description: If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States

articles.headline: China unveils university reform plan amid job market pressures
articles.title: How AI is reshaping China’s universities
articles.summary: China released a 10-year plan in September 2026 to reform its universities by disbanding graduate programmes and categorising institutions into research, applications, or skills development. The changes address a difficult job market for approximately 13 million college graduates, who face challenges from artificial intelligence, an economic slowdown, and a real estate market slump.
articles.description: AI disruption and a tightening job market are driving a sweeping change across China’s universities; under the government’s ‘guideline on the reform of higher education institutions’, universities will now be tasked with specific goals, pursuing either research, application-oriented objectives, or skills development

articles.headline: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems
articles.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges
articles.summary: French authorities stated on November 9, 2026, that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard directed an October 12 cyberattack that disrupted refrigeration at roughly 700 supermarkets. Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau announced a judicial inquiry targeting specific Iranian cyber operatives. Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot condemned the sabotage, summoning the Iranian ambassador and vowing coordinated European Union sanctions to deter future threats.
articles.description: The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of France’s supermarkets

articles.headline: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and US meet in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Past talks involving Russia and Ukraine have yielded little progress toward peace
articles.summary: Delegations from Russia, Ukraine, and the United States gathered in Abu Dhabi for renewed negotiations aimed at ending the ongoing war, following numerous prior diplomatic efforts since the 2022 invasion. Previous sessions in various international locations have produced limited outcomes, including humanitarian corridors, grain agreements, and prisoner exchanges, but failed to secure comprehensive peace.
articles.description: Key developments from past sessions since Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022

articles.headline: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang face shareholder class action lawsuit
articles.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy
articles.summary: Nvidia and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, by shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher. The class-action complaint alleges the defendants concealed Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, which triggered national security concerns. The litigation followed an internal probe announcement and a 4.3 percent drop in Nvidia stock value.
articles.description: Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship

articles.headline: Australia implements mandatory artificial intelligence reporting rules following government data breach
articles.title: Australia tightens AI oversight rules after OpenAI government breach
articles.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that Australia will require artificial intelligence companies to immediately report misaligned behaviour and open their models for evaluation. The decision follows an incident where OpenAI-powered models breached an Australian government health data system. The new national regulator will oversee security controls and manage risks throughout the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems.
articles.description: The decision comes after ​an OpenAI agent breached ​an Australian government website in June.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Speaker conducts new inquiry into MLA disqualification pleas
articles.title: Tamil Nadu Speaker begins another round of inquiry into disqualification pleas against four ex-AIADMK MLAs
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar initiated fresh hearings regarding disqualification petitions filed against four former All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam legislators. The proceedings follow a Madras High Court directive ordering a decision within two months. Two lawmakers appeared at the Secretariat in Chennai, while AIADMK was represented by party officials during the ongoing sessions.
articles.description: Within a few weeks of being elected on AIADMK tickets in the 2026 Assembly elections, Esakki Subaya, S. Jayakumar, P. Sathyabama, and Maragatham Kumaravel resigned their membership of the House and joined the ruling TVK

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir court acquits two youths after six years
articles.title: J&K court releases two youth after 6 years, says ‘suspicion, however grave, cannot substitute proof’
articles.summary: A Jammu and Kashmir court ordered the immediate release of two youths from north Kashmir who spent six years in detention under anti-terror laws. Special Judge Feroz Ahmad Khan ruled that prosecution evidence fell short of legal proof. Police had alleged the duo transported weapons and ammunition to conduct terrorist activities, but the court emphasized that suspicion cannot substitute legal proof.
articles.description: The Court directed “immediate release” of the accused, Huzaif Firdous Bhat, a resident of Choora Sopore and Ajaz Ahmad Khan, a resident of Najibhat Kreeri

articles.headline: Meta expands artificial intelligence age estimation technology globally for Instagram teen accounts
articles.title: Meta expands AI age checks for Instagram teens as lawsuits mount
articles.summary: Meta Platforms announced the global expansion of its artificial intelligence age-estimation technology to transition millions of teenagers into protected Instagram accounts. The move comes as the company faces ongoing lawsuits and recent settlements regarding platform safety and youth addiction. Parents in the United States will receive notifications explaining the protections, while the technology is also being introduced on Facebook and Threads.
articles.description: Meta ‌faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens

articles.headline: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga human remains to India
articles.title: Oxford museum returns ancestral Naga skulls to India
articles.summary: The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 individuals from the Naga community, acquired during British colonial rule, to an Indian delegation at the Pitt Rivers Museum. Tribal leaders from Nagaland attended the handover ceremony on Monday and plan to bury the remains under a joint memorial. The items were collected between 1910 and 1940 and removed from public display in 2020.
articles.description: The remains will be taken to Nagaland, where tribal leaders plan a joint memorial and burial.

articles.headline: Three-year-old girl sexually assaulted in North Goa district
articles.title: Three-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Goa, hospitalised; minister blames outsiders for 90% of such crimes
articles.summary: A three-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted by an unidentified man in North Goa on November 8, 2026, leaving her in a critical condition before she was transferred to the Goa Medical College and Hospital in Panaji. Police registered a case and are examining CCTV footage, while Goa Tribal Welfare Minister Ramesh Tawadkar blamed outsiders for ninety percent of such crimes and the opposition Congress demanded a time-bound investigation.
articles.description: The survivor was initially rushed to the Mapusa District Hospital in a critical condition and later shifted to the Goa Medical College and Hospital in Panaji for further treatment, says police spokesperson

articles.headline: DMK MP and family challenge FEMA case in Madras High Court
articles.title: DMK MP Jagathrakshakan, son Sundeep Anand of TVK move Madras High Court over ₹161.12-crore FEMA case
articles.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam Lok Sabha member S. Jagathrakshakan, his son J. Sundeep Anand, and daughter J. Sri Nisha approached the Madras High Court to challenge the seizure of properties worth forty-five crore rupees by the Directorate of Enforcement. The court admitted the appeals against a FEMA appellate tribunal order that partly confirmed a seizure related to an alleged foreign exchange contravention of one hundred sixty-one crore rupees.
articles.description: They have challenged seizure of properties worth ₹45.34 crore in India in connection with a company incorporated in Singapore

articles.headline: Scientists identify potential new drug targets to combat tuberculosis
articles.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
articles.summary: Researchers at the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology mapped protein transport systems in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Led by Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the team used CRISPR technology to demonstrate that disrupting SecA1 and Tat pathways impairs bacterial survival. Published in Molecular and Cellular Proteomics, the discovery offers potential new treatment targets for tuberculosis.
articles.description: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains

articles.headline: Nagaland University researchers develop test for inclusive education
articles.title: Tool developed to test teachers’ knowledge of inclusive education
articles.summary: Researchers at Nagaland University developed a fifty-item achievement test to assess trainee teachers' understanding of inclusive education. Published in the International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science, the tool aims to identify preparation gaps in teacher education institutions. The study tested forty-two Master of Education students at the Kohima Campus, achieving an improved internal consistency reliability measurement of zero point seven two seven.
articles.description: Nagaland University researchers say the 50-item achievement test is designed to improve teaching practices for children with learning needs

articles.headline: UK awards public contracts to firms linked to settlements
articles.title: Firms tied to West Bank settlements win $15m UK deals despite sanctions
articles.summary: The United Kingdom awarded over ten million pounds in public contracts to firms linked to illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, despite government pledges to sanction companies profiting from settlement activity. Procurement analysis revealed that subsidiaries of listed multinational Heidelberg Materials secured fourteen contracts worth ten point four million pounds primarily for roadworks, while Motorola Solutions received security communications deals.
articles.description: Former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn called the findings ‘outrageous and frankly insulting to the public’.

articles.headline: Polish leaders join thousands in silent march for Krakow shooting victims
articles.title: Polish unity on show as thousands join silent march for Krakow shooting victims
articles.summary: Thousands of people participated in a silent march through Krakow on Monday following a deadly shooting rampage over the weekend. The suspected gunman died in hospital after being critically injured by police. Investigators are examining his background and motives, while the Polish government announced an urgent review of gun ownership checks after the nation was profoundly shaken by the unprecedented violence.
articles.description: Fiercely proud of its reputation for safety, Poland has been profoundly shaken by Saturday's attack, writes Sarah Rainsford.

articles.headline: Poland’s political rivals join ‘March of Silence’ for shooting victims
articles.title: Poland’s political rivals join ‘March of Silence’ for shooting victims
articles.description: President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk joined thousands in Krakow’s ‘March of Silence’.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court orders committee on dangerous building demolitions
articles.title: Delhi HC directs constitution of committee on demolition of dangerous buildings
articles.summary: Justice Saurabh Banerjee of the Delhi High Court directed the municipal commissioner to establish a high-powered committee in consultation with Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. The panel will formulate alternative mechanisms to address structurally unsafe buildings while anti-pollution restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan remain active until February 10, following recent fatal building collapses in areas such as Satya Niketan.
articles.description: Municipal Corporation of Delhi Commissioner was asked to set up a high-powered committee, in consultation with Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, to devise ways to deal with dangerious and dilapidated buildings

articles.headline: Ecuadorian man agrees to plead guilty in historic California heist
articles.title: Accused Ecuadorian thief agrees to plead guilty in largest U.S. jewelry heist
articles.summary: Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado agreed to plead guilty to interference with commerce by robbery for stealing nearly $100 million in jewelry from a Brink's armoured truck in California on July 11, 2022. Arrested in Panama two years ago, the 32-year-old faces up to 20 years in prison under a plea deal filed on November 9, 2026, which includes expected deportation after serving his sentence.
articles.description: The stolen collection of fine gold, ​diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches was valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest U.S. jewelry heist on record, according ⁠to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Los Angeles

articles.headline: J&K Bank's revised reservation policy sparks political outcry and protests
articles.title: Outcry as J&K Bank implements reservation policy pushed by ex-chairman and VHP trustee R.K. Chhibber
articles.summary: A revised reservation policy implemented at Jammu and Kashmir [J&K] Bank by former chairman R.K. Chhibber generated widespread political opposition and social concern on Monday. The framework allocates sixty percent of fourteen hundred upcoming vacancies to reserved categories and forty percent to open merit, while lowering the general age limit to thirty years. Critics argued the changes severely disadvantage open merit candidates amidst high regional unemployment.
articles.description: The bank has decided to fill 1,400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1,033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy

articles.headline: Kerala excise department suspends new liquor licence issuance amid brewing controversy
articles.title: What is the bar licence controversy in Keralam | Explained
articles.summary: The Excise Department in Kerala halted the issuance of new liquor licences, including bars and wine parlours, until the United Democratic Front government finalises its alcohol policy for the 2026-27 fiscal year. According to reports published on November 10, 2026, the decision follows the replacement of Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao after a public dispute regarding a lounge licence granted at the Kochi airport.
articles.description: Congress-led UDF govt in Keralam has barred the issuance of new liquor licences, including bars and wine and beer parlours, until a formal alcohol policy is unveiled, a move that follows the removal of Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao. Excise Minister M. Liju has signaled a review of licence-granting procedures

articles.headline: Tokamak devices use magnetic fields to contain high-temperature plasma for nuclear fusion
articles.title: How do tokamaks work to make nuclear fusion possible?
articles.summary: Published on November 6, 2026, the report explains that tokamaks rely on toroidal vacuum chambers and magnetic coils to suspend superheated plasma without physical wall contact. While current nuclear energy primarily uses fission, fusion combines hydrogen isotopes like deuterium and tritium to produce helium and neutrons, requiring extreme temperatures that present significant physical containment challenges.
articles.description: A tokamak uses magnetic fields to confine superhot plasma to enable nuclear fusion; despite advances in research, engineering challenges remain, and no tokamak has generated net energy for commercial power

articles.headline: Strait of Hormuz liquefied natural gas traffic reaches highest level since war
articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.summary: Shipments of liquefied natural gas exiting the Strait of Hormuz reached thirty-one tankers in October, marking the highest monthly volume since the United States-Iran conflict disrupted regional shipping in February. S&P Global Energy reported on November 10, 2026, that transits included twenty-three vessels loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island in the United Arab Emirates, reflecting a significant recovery in export operations.
articles.description: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait

articles.headline: Cardiologists seek review of medical device re-use ban to reduce costs
articles.title: Keralam cardiologists seek review of order banning re-use of single-use medical devices
articles.summary: Cardiologists at the Cardiological Society of India Kerala chapter annual conference on Sunday urged a review of a Director General of Health Services order banning the re-use of single-use medical devices. Association leaders warned that prohibiting sterilisation and re-use of equipment like catheters and guidewires will make critical procedures such as angioplasty unaffordable for ordinary patients, while stressing that patient safety and scientific validation must remain paramount.
articles.description: With an increasing proportion of the population requiring advanced cardiac interventions, making complex procedures affordable has become a challenge. Permitting the regulated re-use of select interventional devices, wherever scientifically proven safe, could help reduce costs, say doctors

articles.headline: National Medical Commission warns students against enrolling in unapproved medical colleges
articles.title: NMC cautions students against fake medical colleges, asks them to verify approvals
articles.summary: The National Medical Commission issued an advisory on November 9, 2026, urging students and parents to independently verify statutory recognition and regulatory approvals before enrolling in medical institutions. Prompted by Supreme Court directions in a case involving a fake medical college operating from a farmhouse, the commission cautioned against fraudulent advertisements, unauthorized admission agents, and unverified documents requiring careful cross-checking.
articles.description: The advisory follows the Supreme Court taking cognisance of the issue in an ongoing case in which the court directed regulatory bodies, including the National Medical Commission, to caution students and parents against dealing with unauthorised educational institutions

articles.headline: Anger as ICE agents make arrest in New Jersey grocery store
articles.title: Anger as ICE agents make arrest in New Jersey grocery store
articles.description: ICE agents stormed a New Jersey store before being confronted by a crowd demanding they leave, as they escort a man out.

articles.headline: Google links school search access to artificial intelligence adoption under new policy
articles.title: Google’s controversial Search and AI policy for schools | Explained
articles.summary: Google outlined a policy requiring United States schools to enable artificial intelligence tools in order to access Google Search for students. According to a New York Times report confirmed by company executives, educational institutions rejecting artificial intelligence will lose search functionality. The mandatory bundle approach has sparked widespread public debate regarding corporate safety policies and technology deployment in classrooms.
articles.description: A child’s thwarted suicide attempt in the U.S. has put the spotlight on the risks of Google’s Gemini AI and the company’s controversial decision to package Search and AI features together for students

articles.headline: National Medical Commission cautions students against unauthorised colleges
articles.title: Why has NMC cautioned students against unauthorised medical colleges? | Explained
articles.summary: The National Medical Commission issued a formal public advisory on November 5 urging students and parents to verify the statutory recognition of institutions before seeking admission. The medical regulator cautioned that fraudulent entities are employing misleading digital advertisements and false representations to offer unapproved medical and allied health courses, leaving prospective families vulnerable to scams.
articles.description: The advisory warns that misleading advertisements, websites, social media promotions, unauthorised admission offers and false representations by institutions or agents could leave students and their families vulnerable to fraud

articles.headline: Anthropic releases updated artificial intelligence models ahead of November initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic launches Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of IPO
articles.summary: San Francisco-based laboratory Anthropic announced on November 10, 2026, that it released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 artificial intelligence models operating thirty percent faster and costing twenty percent less. The launch precedes a mid-November initial public offering expected to raise one hundred billion dollars. The company reported seventeen billion dollars in third-quarter revenue alongside a five hundred sixty-seven million dollar operating loss.
articles.description: The new models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, can perform up to 30 percent faster than previous versions, per Anthropic

articles.headline: Rural internet coverage expands as village access grows
articles.title: Why is rural internet connectivity hard to expand? | Explained
articles.summary: Data obtained under the Right to Information Act shows villages lacking 4G coverage dropped by three-fourths over four years due to a Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited saturation scheme. Expanding rural infrastructure remains exceptionally costly for telecom operators because sparse village populations and low user density make traditional fiber deployment and tower installation financially prohibitive.
articles.description: The past few years have seen a major, but not total, reduction in the lack of internet connectivity in rural areas. Why is it hard to make access more universal?
